artigo.texto: Growing voter opposition to data center construction across the US, reflected in the midterm election results, is putting pressure on South Korean power equipment makers that have been counting on the region’s AI infrastructure boom. Of 41 local ballot measures related to data center construction across 10 US states, 28 proposed restrictions ranging from construction bans to temporary moratoriums and stricter regulations, according to Ballotpedia. Locals have raised concerns over electricity costs, water consumption, noise and emissions from emergency generators. A Gallup survey published in May found that roughly 70 percent of US respondents opposed constructing AI data centers in their communities. Growing opposition to data center construction directly challenges a key growth driver for major Korean suppliers such as HD Hyundai Electric, Hyosung Heavy Industries and LS Electric, whose combined order backlogs have climbed to roughly 37.9 trillion won ($27.9 billion) amid surging electricity demand. Hyosung Heavy Industries is the leading beneficiary of US big-tech’s infrastructure expansion because of its expertise in ultrahigh-voltage transformers and circuit breakers. As hyperscale data centers consume massive power, they depend on these specialized high-voltage systems to maintain grid stability and prevent outages. As of the third quarter, the company recorded a record-high backlog of 18.9 trillion won in its heavy industrial division, with the North American market accounting for 60 percent. HD Hyundai Electric holds $8.84 billion in backlog orders, including a landmark 1.12 trillion won supply agreement signed with a major global tech firm. LS Electric boasts a 7.04 trillion won backlog, with power distribution panels accounting for 2.25 trillion won. Amid growing uncertainty surrounding the US data center sector, industry sources say key risks for Korean manufacturers include additional regulatory hurdles and potential delays to project timelines. During a Korea Financial Investment Association webinar on Wednesday, Bloomberg Economics Chief Economist Tom Orlik warned, “State governors may take the election results as a signal to impose new restrictions on data center construction.” He emphasized that Korea and Taiwan, which benefited most from the AI boom, could end up being the biggest losers if momentum stalls. He added, “While this may not impact orders already in the pipeline, it will weigh on market expectations for future orders and long-term profitability, and that is where the real risk lies.” “We have not yet received any notifications regarding order delays from our clients,” said an industry source. “However, we are closely monitoring the situation for any potential regulatory developments on data centers.” Given their recent push to scale up their production footprint across North America and Korea, Korean suppliers are highly vulnerable to operational delays. Currently, HD Hyundai Electric is boosting capacity at its Ulsan transformer plant and Cheongju facilities, while Hyosung Heavy Industries is carrying out a $157 million upgrade in Memphis and LS Electric is pushing forward with a $250 million expansion in Utah. hyejin2@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Blue-chip semiconductor stocks plunged around 10 percent during intraday trading Friday, dragging the benchmark Kospi below the 5,000-point mark as investor sentiment was rattled by a sharp overnight sell-off in major technology stocks on Wall Street following the US midterm elections. The benchmark Kospi opened at 5,263.63, down 2.2 percent from its previous close. Losses deepened, triggering a 20-minute trading halt just three minutes into the regular session. The first-stage circuit breaker kicks in when the index stays at least 8 percent below its previous close for one minute. Prior to the circuit breaker activation, Samsung Electronics was trading at 181,400 won ($133.71), down 20,100 won, or 9.98 percent, from the previous session as of 9:14 a.m. SK hynix shares were also down 148,000 won, or 11.71 percent, at 1.116 million won at the same time. In premarket trading, Samsung Electronics had fallen as much as 13 percent from its previous close, while SK hynix had dropped as much as 15.3 percent. Both stocks pared some of their losses after the market opened. The losses followed an overnight selloff on Wall Street, where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25 percent and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52 percent amid concerns about delays in AI data center construction. The Kospi had already fallen 5.28 percent on Thursday amid concerns that the Democrats' midterm sweep could bring tighter US regulation of AI data centers. The tech-heavy Kosdaq opened 3.5 percent lower at 654.43 and was down more than 7 percent within the first half-hour of trading. jwc@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Combined share of CATL and BYD rises 7.8 percentage points year-on-year; South Korea's three battery makers lose 11.7 percentage points Chinese electric vehicle battery makers CATL and BYD are rapidly expanding their influence in global markets outside China. According to SNE Research, an energy-focused market research firm, total battery usage in electric vehicles — including plug-in hybrids and hybrids — sold in markets outside China reached approximately 426.7 gigawatt-hours in the first nine months of this year, up 24.7 percent from the same period last year. Chinese manufacturers led the growth. CATL recorded 143.7 GWh, a 46.7 percent increase year-on-year, lifting its market share from 28.6 percent to 33.7 percent — a gain of 5.1 percentage points. Usage in Europe climbed 35.4 percent to 96.8 GWh from 71.5 GWh, while usage in Asia more than doubled to 27.1 GWh. On Sept. 22, the first two production lines at CATL's factory in Debrecen, Hungary — with a first-phase capacity of 34 GWh — entered trial production, a development expected to strengthen local supply to European customers such as Mercedes-Benz and BMW. BYD held third place with 45.9 GWh, up 66.8 percent, as its share rose 2.8 percentage points to 10.8 percent from 8.0 percent. Growth was broad-based, with usage rising in Europe (17.4 GWh, up 68.8 percent), Asia (14.8 GWh, up 41.0 percent) and South America (7.1 GWh, up 135.7 percent). SNE Research projected that BYD's usage growth in non-China markets would continue for now, noting that the company's overseas EV sales in September reached roughly 180,000 units — more than double the figure from a year earlier — as exports and local production expand rapidly. South Korea's three battery makers — LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI — posted combined usage of 113.0 GWh, down 13.5 percent from the same period last year. Their combined market share fell 11.7 percentage points to 26.5 percent from 38.2 percent. LG Energy Solution recorded 69.8 GWh, down 4.9 percent year-on-year, but retained second place in the non-China market. Usage in Europe rose 13.2 percent to 38.6 GWh and in Asia climbed 49.4 percent to 11.1 GWh, but North America fell 44.9 percent to 16.5 GWh from 29.9 GWh, dragging down overall performance. Its market share slipped 5.1 percentage points to 16.4 percent from 21.5 percent. In the third quarter, the utilization rate at LG Energy Solution's North American ESS lines climbed to around 90 percent, generating record quarterly sales. The pace of ESS conversion at its North American factories and the expansion of its European customer base will be key to defending its market share. SK On's usage fell 17.9 percent to 28.2 GWh, with its share dropping 3.4 percentage points to 6.6 percent from 10.0 percent. The company supplies batteries to Hyundai Motor Group, Ford, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, but usage declined 46.7 percent in North America and 2.2 percent in Europe. SK On is diversifying beyond electric vehicles by converting part of its Georgia factory to a lithium iron phosphate line for ESS applications and signing a contract to supply 9 GWh to a US ESS company over five years starting in 2027. Samsung SDI posted the steepest decline among the top 10, with usage falling 34.4 percent to 15.0 GWh and its share shrinking 3.2 percentage points to 3.5 percent from 6.7 percent. European usage held roughly flat at 9.4 GWh, but North America plunged 66.2 percent to 4.1 GWh from 12.0 GWh. In the third quarter, strong sales of ESS products and battery backup units for data centers helped Samsung SDI post its highest operating profit in 12 quarters. With LFP cell mass production for ESS under way at its StarPlus Energy factory in the United States since October, attention is turning to how much ESS demand can offset the shortfall in EV orders. "Going forward, regional policy and demand diversification will determine supplier competitiveness," SNE Research said. "In North America, EV demand has contracted following the end of tax credits, but LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI found a path to earnings recovery through ESS sales growth in the third quarter. With SK On also set to begin reflecting ESS results from next year, the speed of EV-line-to-ESS conversion is now driving utilization rates." The firm added that in Europe, discussions about softening the 2035 internal combustion engine phase-out target are proceeding alongside moves to tighten local-content requirements, while Chinese manufacturers are ramping up their local factories in earnest. "Local production capacity, price competitiveness and supply chain traceability ahead of the battery passport regulation taking effect in February 2027 will determine market position," it said. likehyo85@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Understanding how ions move through solid materials is key to advancing technologies such as batteries, fuel cells and sensors. A team of scientists led by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory has demonstrated a cutting-edge method for gauging the activity of ions, revealing a new level of detail about how they move and interact. The team tested the technique, which they have called 4D quasielastic neutron scattering (4D-QENS), at the Spallation Neutron Source, a DOE Office of Science user facility at DOE's Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The results show that 4D-QENS provides critical insights that will help improve the theoretical models needed to design next-generation solid-state batteries and related technologies. Some materials allow charged atoms or molecules - called ions - to move quickly. This property makes them suitable as electrolytes in solid-state batteries, which could store more energy and offer greater safety compared to conventional batteries - most of which use liquid electrolytes to move ions during charging and discharging. But a clearer understanding of the mechanisms underlying ionic conduction would help scientists optimize solid-state battery performance. Historically, researchers generally believed that ionic motion in solids was essentially an independent, diffusion-based process. Researchers are now exploring the idea that correlated motion - movement driven by interactions between ions - is key to ultrafast conductivity. However, direct experimental observation remains elusive. Ionic motion is best studied by quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS), which involves directing neutrons at a material sample and measuring the changes in direction and energy as they scatter off the sample. Those changes reveal movements of atoms or molecules within the material. Such studies have provided important insight into the independent, diffusion-based dispersion of ions. The 4D-QENS technique involves rotating a single-crystal sample as it is exposed to the neutrons. This results in data that allows the researchers to generate a complete picture not only of how ions are moving but also of interactions that drive correlated motion. "The idea of doing these sample rotations has been around at pulsed neutron sources for about 15 years, but it has not been applied to QENS before," said Raymond Osborn, senior physicist at Argonne and lead author of a study unveiling this new method. "With 4D-QENS, we show new effects that we would never have seen without such large, contiguous volumes of data." To test the method's potential, the researchers performed 4D-QENS on single-crystal samples of strontium chloride, a salt that becomes a fast-ion conductor at temperatures above 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit. Though strontium chloride is not a candidate for future applications, its well-studied properties made it an ideal model crystal on which to test the technique. The study delivered a refined understanding of ion movement from one site to another within the crystal lattice structure - hopping - that agreed with previous studies. But it also revealed direct evidence of correlated motion among ions that can either facilitate movement through the material or lead to traffic jams that would be detrimental in a battery. A deeper understanding of such correlated motion through 4D-QENS is crucial to help improve solid-state electrolytes. The unique properties of neutrons, which are electrically neutral with a mass similar to the atoms and ions, are key for this technique. Minute changes in neutron velocity, accompanied by significant changes in direction, allow researchers to chart ion movements in considerable detail. That led researchers to the Spallation Neutron Source at ORNL, the world's most powerful pulsed neutron source. The volume of data from such measurements further increased with the recent power upgrade of the Spallation Neutron Source, along with ever more powerful DOE computing resources such as the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF), also a DOE Office of Science user facility. "The questions that we were able to ask about ion conductivity even a few years ago were much more limited in scope. Now we're measuring 3D volumes plus energy transfer, making it 4D," said Stephan Rosenkranz, Argonne Distinguished Fellow and group leader in the Materials Science division. "These comprehensive datasets are allowing new modes of data analysis. Those modes demand computing resources that can match the quality of the data." This type of analysis would be appropriate in future applications of 4D-QENS to more complex materials that are directly relevant to solid-state electrolytes and other energy technologies, the researchers said. The work, supported by DOE's Office of Basic Energy Sciences, is detailed in the journal PRX Energy. In addition to Osborn and Rosenkranz, Argonne authors include Jared Coles, Omar Chmaissem, Matthew Krogstad, Daniel Pajerowski, Feng Ye, Duck Young Chung and Mercouri Kanatzidis. Along with Argonne and ORNL, the team's affiliations include Northern Illinois University and Northwestern University. Christina Nunez is a freelance writer and editor who covers science, technology, and innovation at Argonne and other research facilities under the U.S. Department of Energy. Her work also appears at National Geographic and other publications. She has been writing for Argonne since 2018. The Argonne Leadership Computing Facility provides supercomputing and AI capabilities to the scientific and engineering community to advance fundamental discovery and understanding in a broad range of disciplines. Supported by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE's) Office of Science, Advanced Scientific Computing Research (ASCR) program, the ALCF is one of two DOE Leadership Computing Facilities in the nation dedicated to open science. artigo.texto: A Korean research team has developed a transfer printing process that enables solid electrolytes, a key component of solid-state batteries, to be fabricated as very thin, uniform, and defect-free layers over large areas. The technology is expected to provide a foundation for the large-area manufacturing of high-energy-density solid-state batteries. A research team led by Principal Researcher Yongku Kang and Senior Researcher Myung-Soo Park at the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology (KRICT, President Seokmin Shin) developed a transfer printing technology using the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte LLZTO, in which a solid electrolyte layer is first fabricated on a separate substrate and then transferred onto an electrode. Solid-state batteries use solid-based electrolytes instead of liquid electrolytes, offering the potential to reduce fire risks and increase energy density. To achieve high energy density, the solid electrolyte must be thinner than 20 micrometers (µm) while maintaining uniform thickness over a large area. Conventional methods for fabricating solid electrolytes as freestanding films require thicknesses of 70-120 µm to prevent tearing. Directly coating an electrolyte slurry onto an electrode also presents problems because the liquid-state slurry can infiltrate the porous electrode, causing electrode deformation and nonuniform electrolyte thickness. The research team applied a transfer printing method in which a solid electrolyte slurry is coated and dried on a PET-PDMS substrate, after which only the completed thin layer is pressure-laminated with a roller and transferred onto the electrode like a sticker. Rather than testing numerous material combinations through trial and error, the team used Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) to quantify the affinity between materials and design optimal conditions for both the coating and transfer processes. During the coating step, the researchers selected material combinations with high affinity to allow the slurry to spread uniformly across the substrate. During the transfer step, combinations with low adhesion were selected so that the dried layer could be cleanly detached from the substrate. In this way, the researchers established a generalizable and quantitative design principle for rationally selecting material combinations without repeated trial-and-error experiments. As a result, the team fabricated a uniform solid electrolyte layer over an area of 6 × 20 cm, or 120 cm2, with an average thickness of 15 µm and a thickness deviation of approximately 1 µm. By comparison, direct coating onto an electrode resulted in nonuniform film thicknesses ranging from 10 to 25 µm, even over a smaller area of 6 × 11 cm. The electrolyte performance was also improved. At 25 °C, the ionic conductivity of the hybrid solid electrolyte reached 2.83 × 10-4 S/cm, approximately 50% higher than the 1.69 × 10-4 S/cm measured for a control in which the same polymer electrolyte was incorporated into a polyethylene (PE) separator widely used in conventional batteries. The Li+ transference number was also 0.69, nearly twice the 0.36 of the control. This improvement resulted from the LLZTO-rich electrolyte layer itself serving as a continuous pathway for Li+ transport. To evaluate the effectiveness of transfer printing, the researchers compared it with direct coating. After 100 charge-discharge cycles, the cell fabricated by transfer printing retained 83.6% of its capacity, whereas the directly coated cell retained only 36.1%. Safety was also improved. In a pouch-cell test conducted at 150 °C for 2 hours and 30 minutes, the transfer-printed cell maintained a stable voltage. In contrast, the conventional PE separator-based cell experienced an internal short circuit caused by separator shrinkage, resulting in a rapid voltage drop after approximately 10 minutes. The research team expects that accumulating data on the Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) of different materials together with actual coating, adhesion, and transfer results could eventually enable AI-based research to prescreen suitable combinations from among numerous candidate materials. The study was published in the international materials science journal Advanced Functional Materials (IF: 19.9) in September 2026. Post-Master's Researcher Seul Gi Chu participated as the first author, while Principal Researcher Yongku Kang and Senior Researcher Myung-Soo Park served as corresponding authors. KRICT is a non-profit research institute funded by the Korean government. Since its foundation in 1976, KRICT has played a leading role in advancing national chemical technologies in the fields of chemistry, material science, environmental science, and chemical engineering. Now, KRICT is moving forward to become a globally leading research institute tackling the most challenging issues in the field of Chemistry and Engineering and will continue to fulfill its role in developing chemical technologies that benefit the entire world and contribute to maintaining a healthy planet.

artigo.texto: SUZHOU, China, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BloombergNEF (BNEF) has released its Q4 2026 Tier 1 list of global energy storage manufacturers, with LONGi securing its 10th consecutive quarterly listing. The recognition reflects its track record in global project delivery, system integration and commercial execution. LONGi Secures 10th Consecutive BNEF Tier 1 Energy Storage Listing This quarter, BNEF introduced stricter project financing requirements, requiring qualifying projects to secure non-recourse financing from at least two commercial banks. The higher threshold places greater emphasis on project bankability and commercial viability, adding significance to LONGi's continued inclusion. Full-Stack Innovation Strengthens System-Level Capabilities Under its LONGi ONE strategy, LONGi has developed a full-stack, in-house 5S technology platform spanning iCCS, BMS, PCS, TMS and EMS. This enables native system integration and coordinated management across utility-scale, commercial and industrial (C&I), and microgrid applications. By combining proprietary technologies with integrated system design, this approach supports reliable performance and efficient project execution. A unified responsibility framework and Long-Term Service Agreements (LTSA) provide support throughout the project lifecycle. Global Projects Demonstrate Versatility Across Applications LONGi's global projects demonstrate the adaptability of its solutions across diverse power markets, grid requirements and operating environments. In Australia, the 5MW/20MWh Lunio Energy project in South Australia was connected to the grid in September 2026 and entered the National Electricity Market (NEM), enabling participation in electricity market trading. In Germany, a project in Stralsund integrated energy storage with an existing solar-thermal plant, delivering frequency response in under 50 milliseconds to support grid stability and power quality for critical infrastructure. LONGi also demonstrates its capabilities in challenging environments. In Finland, a microgrid solution achieved black start in under two minutes, supporting independent power supply in extreme cold. In coastal Italy, a 50.16MWh storage system integrated with a 35MWp solar plant features comprehensive anti-corrosion protection, maintaining over 99% system availability in high-salt and high-humidity conditions. Advancing Global Energy Storage Capabilities From proprietary technologies and integrated solutions to global project delivery and lifecycle services, LONGi continues to strengthen its capabilities across the energy storage value chain. The launch of its new smart manufacturing base also further enhances manufacturing and delivery capacity for global markets. Looking ahead, LONGi will continue to advance its LONGi ONE strategy, combining full-stack innovation, global project experience, smart manufacturing and localized services to deliver efficient, reliable energy storage solutions and support the global energy transition. artigo.texto: The International Flow Battery Forum (IFBF) has opened its call for papers and presentation proposals for its 2027 conference in Barcelona, Spain. The 18th edition of the forum will take place at the Barceló Sants Hotel on 22–24 June 2027, with online access available for remote delegates. Proposals must be submitted by 15 January 2027. IFBF is inviting proposals for presentations, keynote addresses, interviews, panel discussions and posters covering the latest commercial and technical developments in flow batteries. Suggested subjects include regulation and legislation, project bankability, manufacturing methods, materials and component supply chains, new applications and measures to improve battery performance, reliability and cost. The organiser is also seeking contributions examining how research can translate into operational improvements and commercially viable flow battery projects. Speakers will be asked for a standalone paper for inclusion in the IFBF Book of Papers All selected presenters will be expected to attend the conference in Barcelona. Speakers will also be asked to prepare a short standalone paper for inclusion in the IFBF Book of Papers. Proposals are being accepted through the Oxford Abstracts submission portal. The conference language will be English. IFBF said it expects the event to attract more than 300 delegates, over 50 speakers, at least 25 exhibition stands and more than 50 poster presentations. The programme is intended to bring together battery manufacturers and developers with utilities, grid operators, investors, researchers and potential customers for long-duration energy storage. BEST reported from IFBF 2026 in Budapest that the sector was moving into a scale-up phase, although access to finance, supportive regulation and dependable supply chains remained significant challenges.

artigo.texto: Marketing Bago’s Carbon Market Initiative at COP31, by Aliyu Umar Aliyu As global climate diplomacy shifts from promises to practical implementation, Niger State has an opportunity to position its emerging carbon market initiative as a vehicle for investment, job creation and sustainable development. For Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago, popularly known as the Farmer Governor, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled for November 9–20, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye, offers a strategic platform to advance the state’s green economy vision. The conference will bring together governments, investors, climate finance institutions, development partners and environmental experts to discuss practical responses to climate change. For Niger State, however, participation should go beyond showcasing its environmental ambitions. The priority should be to secure credible partnerships, develop investment-ready projects and establish a clear pathway for converting its natural resources into measurable climate and economic benefits. Governor Bago’s vision presents an opportunity to connect climate action with Niger State’s agricultural strength, forest resources, renewable energy potential and waste-management needs. If properly developed, these assets could support projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions while creating employment, improving energy access and strengthening rural livelihoods. Niger State’s participation at COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024 provided an earlier opportunity to promote its green economy agenda, including sustainable agriculture, renewable energy and forest conservation. COP31 should build on that engagement by moving from international advocacy towards practical project development and investment mobilisation. From Green Economy Vision to Carbon Market Investment Carbon markets provide a potential mechanism for financing projects that reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions. Under recognised crediting systems, a carbon credit generally represents one metric tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent reduced or removed, subject to the applicable methodology and verification requirements. For Niger State, opportunities could include methane capture at landfills, climate-smart rice cultivation, solar mini-grids and forest restoration. These initiatives could attract investors while supporting the state’s wider development objectives. However, natural resources alone do not guarantee carbon revenue. Projects must demonstrate credible emissions reductions, additionality, appropriate monitoring and independent verification. They must also comply with relevant national regulations and international carbon market requirements. This is particularly important as Niger State seeks to position itself as a pioneer in subnational carbon market development in Nigeria. The ambition to become the country’s first subnational government to open its carbon market to investment, and to advance towards international carbon-credit sales, could be significant. The proposed Niger State Carbon Market Office could play a central role by coordinating project identification, technical assessments, investor engagement, regulatory compliance and stakeholder participation. Its effectiveness will depend on a clear mandate, adequate expertise, transparent procedures and coordination with the relevant federal authorities. International cooperation could accelerate this process. In correspondence to the Niger State team concerning a post-feasibility mission action plan, myclimate’s Article 6 Bilateral Cooperation Team disclosed that a draft memorandum of understanding (MoU) on project development and carbon market activities was undergoing internal legal review, with the intention of finalising it before COP31. The correspondence, signed on behalf of the team by Nsikan-George Emana, Senior Project Manager for Bilateral Cooperation at myclimate, proposed November 12, 2026, for a strategic meeting with the Niger State Government, during which the parties hope to sign the agreement. The proposed engagement offers an opportunity to establish a framework for technical cooperation, project development and potential international market participation. Nevertheless, the MoU remains prospective until formally concluded, and its existence should not be mistaken for evidence that investment has already been secured or carbon credits sold. Niger State should approach the meeting with clearly defined priorities, including project timelines, financing arrangements, responsibilities, community safeguards and measurable implementation targets. Article 6 and the International Opportunity The proposed partnership is particularly relevant to Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which provides frameworks for international cooperation in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. At COP29 in November 2024, countries made significant progress on the rules governing international carbon trading and the UN-supervised carbon crediting mechanism. Under Article 6.2, countries can cooperate through internationally transferred mitigation outcomes, subject to applicable accounting and authorisation requirements. Article 6.4 provides a UN-supervised crediting mechanism, while Article 6.8 addresses non-market approaches. For Niger State, these frameworks could create opportunities to develop projects that attract international finance and contribute to Nigeria’s climate commitments. However, the state must work within Nigeria’s national climate governance arrangements. International transfers under Article 6 cannot be treated as an exclusively state-level transaction where national authorisation and accounting are required. artigo.texto: As artificial intelligence (AI) drives the expansion of data centers, power supply systems are undergoing significant changes. Data center capacity is increasing from tens of megawatts (MW) to 100–200MW, while next-generation AI server racks are expected to consume more than 1MW each. Surging power demand is pushing up incoming supply voltages and increasing the importance of technologies that ensure stable power delivery at every stage. Responding to these trends, French energy management company Schneider Electric presented integrated solutions covering high-voltage distribution, server power delivery and liquid cooling. At Data Center Korea 2026, held in Yangjae-dong, Seoul, on Nov. 4, the company showcased high-voltage switchgear, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), coolant distribution units (CDUs) and integrated operations software under the theme “From Grid to Chip, From Chip to Cooling.” 1. Higher Incoming Voltages as Data Centers Expand As AI data centers grow, the first major change occurs in the equipment receiving electricity from external power grids. Conventional data centers typically receive power at 22.9 kilovolts (kV), while large-scale facilities use 154kV supplies. In such cases, data centers must install their own substations to step down the voltage to 22.9kV. Receiving electricity at higher voltages also increases investment in on-site substations and distribution equipment. “In the past, power infrastructure was not an area that frequently required large-scale investment,” a Schneider Electric official said. “However, growing data center power demand has increased investment in equipment for power intake and distribution.” Data centers step down high-voltage electricity received from external grids at substations before distributing it through high-voltage switchgear. The switchgear distributes electricity and protects equipment by interrupting current through circuit breakers when abnormalities occur. Distribution transformers then reduce the voltage to low-voltage levels, such as 380 volts (V), allowing low-voltage switchgear to supply power to UPS systems and cooling equipment. Schneider Electric offers products covering each stage of this process. Its intelligent power control centers (IPCCs) and intelligent motor control centers (IMCCs) also provide automatic transfer functions that switch power supply routes to backup sources when the primary supply fails. 2. How 800V DC Will Change UPS and Battery Roles Power delivery architectures are also expected to change as AI servers consume more electricity. Nvidia is pursuing the adoption of an 800V high-voltage direct current (DC) architecture for next-generation AI data centers. Higher voltages reduce the current required to deliver the same amount of power, lowering heat generation and transmission losses in wiring. High-voltage DC architectures can also improve efficiency by reducing the number of power conversion stages. “We are preparing a roadmap toward an eventual transition to fully DC-based systems,” a Schneider Electric official said. “Because the transition to DC will take considerable time, UPS systems may still be used during the interim, but some applications may no longer require them once the transition is complete.” As power delivery systems shift toward DC, other power equipment, such as solid-state transformers (SSTs), could replace certain UPS functions. Batteries, however, are expected to remain essential for managing sudden fluctuations in AI server loads. “AI workloads cause substantial power fluctuations, which could destabilize the upstream power grid unless batteries supply electricity,” the official said. “We expect the role of batteries, including battery backup units (BBUs), to become even more important.” 3. Integrated Management From Chip Cooling to Power Equipment Cooling systems are becoming increasingly important as AI servers consume more electricity. Rising heat output from graphics processing units (GPUs) makes it difficult for conventional air cooling systems to handle thermal loads. In particular, growing power consumption per server rack is accelerating the adoption of liquid cooling technologies that deliver coolant directly to chips. Schneider Electric acquired liquid cooling specialist Motivair last year, securing direct-to-chip (D2C) cooling and high-capacity thermal management technologies. At the event, it showcased Motivair’s MCDU-25 coolant distribution unit. CDUs regulate the temperature and flow rate of coolant supplied to servers. AI data centers also require technologies that integrate the management of power and cooling equipment, as disruptions in either system can affect server operations. Schneider Electric links its electrical power management system (EPMS) with its building management system (BMS) to provide integrated management of power and cooling infrastructure.

artigo.texto: Hyosung Goodsprings, a pump manufacturing subsidiary of Hyosung Group, will supply high-efficiency cooling pumps for SK Telecom’s (SKT) artificial intelligence (AI) data center in Ulsan. The pumps reduce power consumption by regulating the circulation of cooling water used to dissipate heat generated by servers. The company has secured orders covering the Ulsan data center’s 100-megawatt (MW) capacity. With SKT planning to expand its domestic AI data center capacity to 15 gigawatts (GW) by 2035, Hyosung Goodsprings’ cooling pump shipments are expected to increase further. According to industry sources on Nov. 4, Hyosung Goodsprings has secured contracts to supply sensorless inline pumps for both the 40MW first-phase facility (Building A) and the 60MW second-phase facility (Building B) at SKT’s Ulsan AI data center. Sensorless inline pumps automatically adjust motor speeds according to server cooling loads. They operate at higher speeds when cooling demand increases and slow down when demand decreases. This eliminates the need to operate continuously at maximum output, reducing unnecessary power consumption. The pumps also control operating conditions without separate flow sensors, simplifying equipment configuration and maintenance. The integrated inverters are supplied by ABB, a Swedish-Swiss power technology company. Hyosung Goodsprings has also added a total harmonic distortion (THD) monitoring function to its sensorless inline pumps. THD measures the extent to which an electrical waveform deviates from its normal shape. The function allows operators to monitor electrical conditions without separate measuring equipment, simplifying facility management. The number of cooling pumps required increases with a data center’s power capacity. A 40MW data center typically requires about 20 to 30 pumps. Applying the same standard, SKT’s 100MW Ulsan data center would need more than 50 pumps. With a set of pumps for a 40MW facility costing approximately 1.5 billion won, the total supply value for the 100MW Ulsan data center is estimated at around 4 billion won. AI data centers generate substantial heat by operating large numbers of servers equipped with high-performance graphics processing units (GPUs). Server overheating can degrade computing performance or cause equipment failures, making cooling systems essential. Data center cooling systems operate by using cooling water to absorb heat generated by servers and release it outside the facility. Cooling pumps circulate the water through pipes and maintain the required flow rate. With cooling systems accounting for approximately 40% of a facility’s total energy consumption, pump efficiency plays an important role in reducing operating costs. SKT plans to expand its domestic AI data center investments, starting with Ulsan. The company intends to establish AI data center clusters with capacities exceeding 2GW in the Yeongnam region and 1GW in the southwestern region, before gradually expanding domestic capacity to 5GW starting in 2029. Its goal is to reach 15GW by 2035. Applying the same cooling equipment requirements, the total demand for pumps could reach approximately 600 billion won. Hyosung Goodsprings could see substantial revenue growth if it secures additional orders for SKT’s future data centers. The company’s revenue declined slightly to 230.1 billion won last year from 236.3 billion won a year earlier. Operating profit, however, increased approximately 48% to 20.9 billion won from 14.2 billion won over the same period. Hyosung Goodsprings has also secured several domestic data center operators as customers beyond SKT. The company supplies cooling pumps to facilities including the 35MW Deogi-dong Internet Data Center (IDC) in Ilsan, the 80MW GPC IDC in Hwaseong, the 50MW TIMBUKTU IDC in Ansan and the 25MW Global Cloud Center (GCC) IDC in Ansan. Hyosung Goodsprings is an unlisted, wholly owned subsidiary of Hyosung specializing in industrial pump manufacturing. In addition to cooling pumps for data centers, it produces large industrial pumps for oil refining, petrochemical facilities and power plants, as well as pumps for nuclear power plants. Major customers include ExxonMobil and Aramco.

artigo.texto: Sunwoda Solid-State Battery Survives 200°C Heat Test Without Fire Sunwoda solid-state battery: the 20 Ah Xin Bixiao cell passed a 200°C hot-box test with 400 Wh/kg and 1,200+ cycles, now in carmaker testing. Published 2 min read Chinese battery maker Sunwoda says its 20 Ah Xin Bixiao solid-state cell did not catch fire or explode when heated to 200°C (392°F) in a hot-box safety test. The Sunwoda solid-state battery also reaches more than 400 Wh/kg and over 1,200 charge cycles, figures the company links to electric cars with a range above 1,000 km (about 620 miles). The update came from Sunwoda Electric Vehicle Battery (SEVB), the group’s automotive unit, in an October 30 reply on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange investor platform. SEVB said the cell has completed design and process verification and is still being evaluated by carmakers, which it did not name. As CarNewsChina notes, customer testing first started in May 2026. How the Sunwoda Solid-State Battery Is Built Xin Bixiao uses a polymer-composite electrolyte instead of the sulfide chemistry that rivals such as CATL are pursuing. The cell combines a 12-micron polymer-composite membrane with a nanoscale high-entropy silicon anode, and Sunwoda says it reaches its cycle life at an external pressure below 1 MPa. That low pressure matters. Solid electrolytes can lose contact with the electrodes as materials swell and shrink during charging, so some sulfide designs need constant clamping force inside the pack. Sulfide materials also react with moisture and can release toxic hydrogen sulfide, which makes factories harder to run. After 1,200 cycles the cell keeps more than 80% of its original capacity. Sunwoda estimates that would cover more than a decade of use for a driver who covers about 20,000 km (12,400 miles) a year. Results Are for One Cell, Not a Car The important caveat is scale. The heat, energy density and lifespan figures come from a single cell, not a full battery pack installed in a vehicle, and Interesting Engineering points out that the company has not committed to a launch date for its high-density cells. Earlier lab results, such as a NASA solid-state battery built for extreme cold, show how long the path from cell to product can be. Production is also small for now. SEVB has connected a pilot line with an annual design capacity of 0.2 GWh, enough for roughly 2,600 to 2,700 electric cars a year. Its roadmap lists a second-generation sulfide battery for 2027 and a cell above 500 Wh/kg for 2030, both still development targets. What It Means for the EV Battery Race CATL, the world’s largest EV battery maker, reaffirmed on October 27 that it aims for small-batch production of sulfide solid-state cells in 2027. Sunwoda’s polymer route gives carmakers a second option, at a time when many Chinese automakers are losing money and looking for any edge on range and safety. Sunwoda is also working on cells of at least 450 Wh/kg for electric aircraft (eVTOL) that can deliver 1,000 W/kg of continuous power, alongside a fast-charging LFP pack that goes from 10% to 70% in about five minutes. Other chemistries are moving too, including a sodium metal battery that keeps 90% capacity after 1,000 cycles. For buyers, solid-state cars with these specs are still years away, but the safety data is a step in the right direction.

artigo.texto: Aiel Completes Development of Patent-Based Roll-to-Roll Equipment for Lithium-Metal Anodes Aiel, a physical AI operations data platform company, has begun bringing next-generation battery manufacturing technology in-house. A roll-to-roll machine for manufacturing lithium-metal anodes, developed by Aiel using its proprietary patented technology. Aiel View original image Aiel announced on November 6 that it had completed development of roll-to-roll equipment for manufacturing lithium-metal anodes, based on its proprietary patented technology. The equipment is significant because it puts into an actual continuous manufacturing process Aiel's core technologies related to lithium-metal anode materials and protective layers. In particular, by bringing not only materials development but also key manufacturing processes and equipment technology in-house, the company has further strengthened the technological foundation of its next-generation battery business. The roll-to-roll process is a manufacturing method in which roll-shaped materials are moved continuously while undergoing processing and surface treatment. It can be designed to enable continuous production of lithium-metal anodes and is considered a key technology for future large-scale production, improved manufacturing efficiency, and cost competitiveness. Aiel previously filed a patent for "Lithium-Metal Anodes Including a Dual-Functional Protective Layer with Improved Ionic Conductivity and Physicochemical Stability, and a Continuous Manufacturing Method Thereof." The technology centers on a dual protective layer (DPL) structure designed to suppress the formation of lithium dendrites, one of the key challenges to commercializing lithium-metal batteries, and a continuous manufacturing process in a vacuum environment. Lithium metal is a next-generation anode material capable of achieving high theoretical energy density. However, dendrites formed during charging and discharging and interfacial instability have made achieving longer lifespan and safety a significant challenge. Aiel is considering expanding the application of this technology beyond all-solid-state batteries to various fields, including humanoid robots and future mobility, where high energy density and lightweight design are required. artigo.texto: The blue tidal wave that shook up U.S. politics last night ushered in several anti-data center governors in key states that could complicate Big Tech’s plans to build out the infrastructure powering AI. Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress as a result of the midterm election Tuesday, flipping at least seven Senate seats in a historic wave that The Washington Post called a rebuke on a scale not seen since 1974. Democrats also flipped more than two dozen Republican-held House seats, with some races still undecided. Democrats’ victories were fueled by concerns over affordability and the Iran war, as well as President Trump’s unpopularity. Yet another factor also played a role: voters’ widespread concern over the rapid buildout of data centers across the country. Among the Democratic victories, the elections of three governors who campaigned on restricting data center development, Gina Hinojosa in Texas, Amy Acton in Ohio, and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia could be consequential for the AI industry’s future expansion. While members of Congress would need to pass legislation, and potentially overcome a veto by President Trump, to impose new restrictions on data centers, the incoming Democratic governors have more tools at their disposal, including the power to influence permitting, regulation, and tax incentives at the state level, although some actions may require the approval of state legislatures. We have already seen Gov. Abbott wield the power of the governor’s office to take action on data centers in Texas, the state with more data center capacity operating and under construction than any other, according to Baxtel, and which is projected to hold nearly 30% of U.S. data center capacity by 2028, according to a Bloom Energy report. Abbott, who was defeated Tuesday by Governor-elect Hinojosa, initially supported data centers, yet he adjusted his stance earlier this year amid widespread concerns over their resource use. In June, Abbott directed state regulators to develop measures requiring data centers to cover the costs for the energy infrastructure they use for their operations. In August, he halted new grid connection approvals for data centers while regulators conducted an audit of proposed projects. And later directed state officials to enforce water-use reporting requirements and instructed regulators to pause new data center permits until audits on their electricity and water use were completed. Hinojosa, for her part, said Gov. Abbott’s tough talk on data centers was “nothing more than an election year stunt.” Hinojosa promised in the run up to the election that, were she to win, she would impose a moratorium on data center construction and eliminate subsidies and tax breaks awarded to major data center developers. Governor-elect Amy Acton in Ohio made similar promises, calling for a conditional moratorium on new data centers unless developers agree to cover all their utility costs, use union labor, and meet environmental standards. Meanwhile, in Georgia, Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms also promised a temporary statewide pause on new data center construction to assess the industry’s impact on electricity bills, communities, and the environment. Across eight major North American markets, a record 7,481 megawatts of data center capacity was under construction during the first half of 2026, a nearly 25% increase from a year earlier, according to commercial real estate firm CBRE. And yet, taken together, the election of these three governors represents a “new reality” for tech companies that have been pouring billions of dollars into data center construction and will now need to reassess, said longtime tech analyst Dan Ives, of merchant banking firm Yorkville Ives. While Trump may veto any draconian AI safety or regulatory laws passed by a Democratic-controlled Congress. The newfound influence of AI skeptical politicians in Congress will force tech companies to come to the negotiating table to reach compromises on AI-related legislation, Ives wrote in a Wednesday note. “Tech needs to adjust and focus on a slower pace of this AI rollout,” he said in an email. Shares of companies involved with the AI compute and data center construction fell Wednesday including CoreWeave, Applied Digital, and Cipher Digital. Yet, the overall market was up as of afternoon trading, with the S&P 500 up 1.82% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq up 1.94%. Ives said in the note Wednesday that while tech companies may now face obstacles to building out their data center capacity, the Democratic wins could actually be a positive for tech stocks as it will likely force hyperscalers, like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, to slow down their capital expenditures, which are expected to hit at most $828 billion in 2026. “The Street still is way underestimating the future revenue growth and profitability that AI will bring to the tech world (and other industries) over the next few years,” he wrote. “Now it will happen at a more measured pace which is likely a good thing in the eyes of many investors…and the market will digest this news and move forward.”

artigo.texto: Prefeito de Nova York critica avanço dos data centers de IA em meio às eleições: "Nosso risco, recompensa deles" Zohran Mamdani afirma que resistência à construção de data centers une democratas e republicanos e alerta para os custos ambientais e econômicos da inteligência artificial Atualizado A expansão dos data centers para sustentar o avanço da inteligência artificial se tornou um dos temas de debate nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos, realizadas nesta terça-feira (3). Às vésperas da votação, o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, afirmou que a crescente oposição à construção dessas instalações representa um raro ponto de convergência entre democratas e republicanos, preocupados com os impactos da tecnologia sobre o consumo de energia, as tarifas de eletricidade e o meio ambiente. Em entrevista à revista Wired, publicada nesta terça-feira, Mamdani afirmou que a resistência aos data centers lhe dá esperança justamente por ultrapassar as tradicionais divisões políticas americanas. "Eu e Ron DeSantis não temos muita coisa em comum, mas existe uma oposição semelhante ao desenvolvimento desse tipo de data center", disse, em referência ao governador republicano da Flórida. Para o prefeito, a insatisfação reflete uma preocupação crescente com os custos da infraestrutura necessária para alimentar os sistemas de IA. "O que estamos vendo é uma oposição ao que esses data centers significariam para a vida cotidiana das pessoas, para suas contas de eletricidade e para o meio ambiente", afirmou. Mamdani, que já manifestou apoio a uma suspensão de um ano na construção de novos data centers no estado de Nova York, também criticou a falta de transparência das empresas de tecnologia sobre o consumo energético de seus sistemas. Segundo ele, a escassez de informações dificulta avaliar os custos reais da inteligência artificial para a sociedade. O prefeito resumiu sua crítica à política adotada para o setor nos últimos anos com uma expressão: "Nosso risco, a recompensa deles". Na avaliação de Mamdani, a população acaba exposta aos impactos da expansão da IA, enquanto os benefícios econômicos ficam concentrados nas empresas responsáveis pela tecnologia. As críticas também se estendem à sustentabilidade financeira da corrida pela inteligência artificial. Questionado sobre a possibilidade de o setor estar vivendo uma bolha, Mamdani respondeu afirmativamente e comparou o atual momento da indústria à bolha imobiliária que antecedeu a crise financeira de 2008. O prefeito ainda questionou a capacidade das próprias empresas de tecnologia de estabelecer limites para o setor. Ao ser perguntado se confiava em executivos como Sam Altman, CEO da OpenAI, respondeu simplesmente: "Não". Para Mamdani, o avanço da inteligência artificial exige uma resposta mais firme do poder público, especialmente diante do que considera uma ausência de regulação adequada em nível federal.

artigo.texto: Google deu um passo importante rumo aos data centers espaciais: acaba de executar IA em órbita Com o Project Suncatcher, a gigante das buscas deu início aos testes para operar seus próprios chips de inteligência artificial diretamente no espaço O Google deu um passo rumo aos data centers espaciais ao executar com sucesso um modelo de IA em órbita. Por meio do Project Suncatcher, em parceria com a Planet e a SpaceX, a empresa utilizou um chip TPU em um satélite para rodar o modelo Gemma e gerar uma resposta enviada à Terra. O teste pioneiro valida a viabilidade técnica de transferir o processamento de inteligência artificial para o espaço, aliviando a infraestrutura terrestre de alto consumo de energia e resfriamento contínuo. Nós nos acostumamos a utilizar a inteligência artificial em tarefas cotidianas, como tirar dúvidas rápidas ou traduzir um texto. Fazemos isso diretamente do celular ou do computador, quase sem pensar na colossal infraestrutura que viabiliza cada uma dessas respostas. Por trás dessa facilidade aparente, opera uma cadeia física complexa que exige energia constante, resfriamento robusto e conectividade contínua. Enquanto essa capacidade se expande em solo terrestre, surge um novo horizonte computacional: transferir parte dessa carga de processamento para o espaço. O Google deu um primeiro passo concreto nessa direção. Em 30 de outubro, a empresa anunciou ter recebido, diretamente da órbita da Terra, uma resposta gerada pelo seu modelo aberto Gemma 4 por meio de uma unidade de processamento neural (TPU) — um chip dedicado com especificações de data center. O satélite, desenvolvido em parceria com a Planet e lançado em 1º de outubro em uma missão da SpaceX, integra o Project Suncatcher, programa voltado a pesquisas em computação orbital. Embora ainda não represente um data center espacial em pleno funcionamento, a validação técnica cumpriu seu papel: solicitou-se à IA a criação de um haikai temático sobre o cosmos. Durante uma janela de comunicação com a estação em solo, a equipe enviou o comando: escrever um haikai sobre a experiência no espaço. O haikai é um poema curto tradicional de origem japonesa, estruturado em três versos. A resposta foi transmitida quando o satélite ... artigo.texto: FILE PHOTO: A smartphone with a displayed AMD logo is placed on a computer motherboard in this illustration taken March 6, 2023. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/ File Photo Nov 4 (Reuters) - Advanced Micro Devices rose 7.3% in premarket trading after the US chipmaker forecast faster growth through 2027, reassuring investors that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong. AMD, which recently joined the ranks of trillion-dollar companies, has gained about 126% this year and is poised to add about $58 billion in market value if premarket gains hold. The company's strong outlook highlighted growing momentum in its server processor business, signaling that spending on AI computing was extending beyond Nvidia's accelerators, which dominate the market. "We see demand across the data-center business, across our CPU business, as well as our data-center AI business," CEO Lisa Su said, adding the company had been preparing for that growth for several years. Su said on Tuesday that the company expects overall revenue to rise more than 80% in 2027, which is higher than the 77% growth analysts estimate, according to LSEG data. AMD's product roadmap and expanding software ecosystem position it to capture a meaningful share of the AI market, while strengthening its role as the leading alternative to Nvidia and supporting further gains in server CPUs, said analysts at TD Cowen. Last week, rival Intel's shares plunged more than 20% after the company reported weak PC demand, fueling concerns about its reliance on the PC market and relatively limited exposure to AI. Analysts at Morgan Stanley are cautious about assuming current growth in the CPU server business will continue indefinitely amid an industry-wide shortage, but they believe AMD is executing better than competitors and could continue to capture a larger share of the market. The company's third-quarter data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion, topping analysts' expectations of $8.20 billion. The Santa Clara, California-based company trades at about 31 times forward earnings, compared with 14 times for Nvidia and 16.5 times for Broadcom. (Reporting by Kanishka Ajmera in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

artigo.texto: Energy storage in Italy continues to gain capacity, approaching 20 GWh cumulatively, at the same time, the country added 4.83 GW of new photovoltaic capacity between January and September 2026, according to data compiled by ITALIA SOLARE from Terna records. The expansion of the solar market continued during the third quarter, with 1.74 GW of new photovoltaic capacity connected, representing a 37% increase compared to the 1.269 GW registered in the same period of 2025. In the first nine months of the year, new solar installations reached 4,834 MW, distributed among 147,632 newly connected systems, as a result, Italy’s cumulative photovoltaic capacity reached 48,347 MW at the end of September. The data comes from ITALIA SOLARE and is based on records from the Gaudì database in Terna, with a cut-off date of September 30, 2016. Italy accelerates new photovoltaic installations The sector’s growth is also reflected in the number of installations connected to the grid, during the third quarter, 58,459 new photovoltaic systems were added, compared to 38,660 in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, connected capacity increased by 5% compared to the second quarter, this trend demonstrates greater activity across the various segments of the Italian solar market, however, large-scale plants and commercial and industrial projects accounted for the majority of the new capacity added during the period. Large-scale projects are leading solar growth The photovoltaic installations systems of 1 MW or more contributed 2,241 MW between January and September 2026. This capacity corresponded to 473 plants and represented 46 % of the country’s new solar additions. The commercial and industrial (C&I) segment, comprised of systems with capacities between 20 kW and 1 MW, added 1,697 MW through 11,905 installations. Its share reached 35 % of the new photovoltaic capacity. Meanwhile, residential installations up to 20 kW added 897 MW through 135,254 connections, equivalent to 19% of the growth recorded during the first nine months of the year. This distribution highlights the weight of higher power projects in the expansion of the Italian market, while the residential segment continues to contribute a significant volume of new installations. The third quarter maintains the momentum of solar projects Between July and September, the photovoltaic plants large-scale projects added 858 MW of new capacity. Of this total, 394 MW came from projects between 1 MW and 10 MW, while the remaining 464 MW came from installations larger than 10 MW. During the same period, commercial and industrial projects added 543 MW, while the residential segment contributed another 341 MW. These results confirm the leading role of large-scale installations in the growth of Italian photovoltaic power and also show that commercial and industrial projects continue to make a significant contribution to the expansion of solar generation. Energy storage in Italy is approaching 20 GWh Electricity storage also saw progress during 2016. As of September 30, Italy had 984,829 connected electrochemical systems, with a cumulative energy capacity of 19,983 MWh and a total capacity of 8,338 MW. According to the published data, 12,552 MWh corresponded to storage systems associated with photovoltaic installations, while the remaining 7,368 MWh belonged to independent installations. Between January and September, 1,953 MWh of new storage capacity was connected. Of this volume, 1,486 MWh were linked to solar installations and 467 MWh corresponded to independent systems. During the third quarter, the systems associated with photovoltaic installations incorporated 480 MWh of energy capacity and 252 MW of power. These new connections comprised 31,039 systems and represented a 15% growth in capacity compared to the same period in 2025. The evolution of photovoltaic generation and energy storage reflects the expansion of both segments within the Italian electricity system. As installed solar power increases, so do the resources available to store electricity and manage its availability. This combination is becoming increasingly important in the evolution of the country’s energy infrastructure. Source: Solar Quarter Photo: Shutterstock

Please enter the email address you use for your account so we can send you a link to reset your password: Early signs point to a rough election for AI infrastructure. We’ve seen enough: If this was the data center election, it was a really bad night for the industry. Democratic campaigns and their affiliated Super PACs spent bigly on data center-themed attack ads. The ads came in various flavors. Some ads painted a vote for tax cuts as aiding data center developers. Others brought up candidates’ previous support for data centers or stock the candidate may have held in the tech industry or AI infrastructure developers. As Election Day approached, the data center industry sought to bat back claims that their sector’s poor reputation with the electorate would sway the results. People may have soured on their industry, they argued, but people weren’t going to vote based on that position. Results are still coming in, but so far congressional races heavily featuring these data center attacks are heavily going in Democrats’ favor. In addition, these races have so profoundly shifted that it’ll be challenging for the industry to argue they played no role in the outcome. Some of the most illustrative examples are obvious. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms campaigned on a statewide data center moratorium and won control of the governor’s mansion, becoming the first black woman to ever lead a U.S. state. Similar results in Ohio where Amy Acton flipped party control of the governor’s seat with a campaign that included going hard against data centers. In Pennsylvania, two Democrats who focused on data centers in their races have flipped Republican districts: Scranton mayor Paige Cognetti and firefighter Bob Brooks. In New Jersey, Cape May mayor Zack Mullock rode data center attacks to defeat Rep. Jeff Van Drew, the biggest opponent of the offshore wind industry. In Virginia, Democrat Shannon Taylor rode data center-laden attacks to take control of the Richmond area congressional seat from Rep. Rob Wittman. If you’re arguing this election was decided by data centers, your best proof point: Democrat Gina Hinojosa has taken control of the governor's mansion in Texas, defeating incumbent Greg Abbott, who’d sought recently to take a hard line against the industry. Hinojosa ran on going further, calling to pass a law completely pausing data center development across one of the industry’s favorite states. She won a decisive victory. So did Democratic Texas Agriculture Commissioner candidate Clayton Tucker, who I explained months ago became one of anti-data center Facebook’s favorite online personalities. But it makes sense that data centers would matter a lot in Texas, which could be compared to Virginia in terms of their buildout. When you inspect the election results more closely, they tell a more complicated story about the upper boundaries of these data center attacks. For decades, Greenville and Spartanburg County have been GOP vote strongholds and reliable for both Republican congressional candidates and statewide campaigns. The congressional district gave Donald Trump at least a 20-point cushion in the 2024 presidential election, according to Decision Desk HQ. Last week, I explained for subscribers to The Fight how Courtney McClain, a novice candidate living one mile from a controversial data center proposal, was running against incumbent Rep. William Timmons. I couldn’t find much in the way of online ad spending on either side in this race and it’s never been on the radar of most political observers as a campaign that could somehow flip party control. But the data center debate in Spartanburg County has been immense. Tonight, Timmons kept his ordinarily ruby red district by slim single digits after running even for most of the night. But this swing was essentially the same as the national margin. And because Timmons didn’t lose, this actually feels like a crucial distinction – data centers were not deciding races themselves in all cases. Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darlene Graham in a result driven by Democratic overperformance and GOP underperformance in this area, but it’s challenging to tie this result to the data center issue at all. Anything from the economy and the Iran War to Graham’s deceased brother and his baggage could be blamed for this result from this heavily evangelical region. However, it will be challenging for the data center sector to differentiate themselves from this outcome, especially since a pro-data center Super PAC – Building the Future – publicly waded into the race in support of Graham only to lose. “Darlene Graham’s loss is a black eye for the data center industry,” wrote Teddy Schleifer of The New Yor

artigo.texto: Preocupações com as fontes de renda Para quem planta acácias para fins de produção, leva de 4 a 5 anos até que possam começar a colher e recuperar o investimento. Muitas pessoas que possuem terras florestais desejam participar do plantio de grandes florestas de madeira no âmbito da política de apoio da cidade de Da Nang, abrindo assim fontes adicionais de renda, melhorando a eficiência econômica e criando impulso para a manutenção e o desenvolvimento sustentável das florestas. A Sra. Tran Thi Phuong (moradora do bairro residencial Ta Lang - Gian Bi, distrito de Hai Van) relatou que, há muitos anos, os moradores da região plantam acácias, mas levam cinco anos para colher os frutos e obter renda. Durante esse período, as pessoas cuidam das florestas plantadas e trabalham para outros (plantando, cuidando das florestas, descascando as acácias, etc.) para complementar a renda e cobrir as despesas enquanto aguardam a colheita. No entanto, como as acácias têm raízes pivotantes que não penetram profundamente no solo, elas frequentemente caem durante tempestades e não impedem a erosão. Os moradores locais querem converter suas plantações de acácia existentes em florestas de madeira madura ou plantar novas florestas de madeira madura para receber incentivos do governo da cidade de Da Nang , mas estão muito preocupados com o fluxo de caixa necessário para manter e cuidar das florestas, bem como para cobrir as despesas familiares a partir do quinto ano. Para o sub-bosque, especialmente plantas medicinais, a colheita só pode começar após o quinto ano, quando as árvores atingem a maturidade. “Minha família possui 1 hectare de área florestal e queremos muito nos cadastrar para o plantio de madeira em larga escala, a fim de receber apoio da prefeitura. No entanto, ainda estamos preocupados com a manutenção da floresta a partir do quinto ano. Esperamos que a prefeitura apoie a certificação e a venda de créditos de carbono para essa floresta plantada, para que as pessoas tenham mais recursos para manter e cuidar da floresta, bem como garantir seu sustento, principalmente enquanto aguardam a colheita das plantações sob a copa das árvores”, solicitou a Sra. Phuong. O Sr. Nguyen Van Trung, chefe da Associação de Idosos da área residencial de Ta Lang - Gian Bi (bairro de Hai Van), disse: "Para as pessoas, o fluxo de caixa para manter e cuidar das árvores a partir do 5º ano é o 'gargalo' do plantio de grandes florestas de madeira, especialmente para famílias que tomaram empréstimos de bancos." Os moradores esperam que a cidade apoie a certificação e a venda de créditos de carbono florestal para que os grandes produtores de madeira possam ter uma renda regular, sem a pressão de pagar empréstimos bancários, e assim as florestas possam ser usadas a longo prazo para o turismo quando a cobertura vegetal estiver baixa, para apicultura quando a cobertura vegetal estiver média e para o cultivo de plantas medicinais quando a cobertura vegetal estiver alta. Só assim as grandes florestas serão preservadas a longo prazo, garantindo ao mesmo tempo a estabilidade econômica das famílias. Segundo especialistas, a cidade de Da Nang precisa coordenar-se com a cidade de Hue e a província de Quang Ngai para desenvolver um projeto de crédito de carbono florestal que facilite as negociações por meio do Centro Financeiro Internacional do Vietnã em Da Nang. Isso proporcionaria apoio financeiro para famílias envolvidas na produção madeireira em larga escala, bem como para os esforços de conservação e proteção florestal da cidade. O Dr. Luong Quang Huy, Chefe do Departamento de Gestão de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa e Proteção da Camada de Ozono (Departamento de Alterações Climáticas, Ministério da Agricultura e do Ambiente ), informou que o Governo acaba de publicar o Decreto n.º 180/2026/ND-CP, de 21 de maio de 2026, que regulamenta os serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono em florestas. Este Decreto especifica os sujeitos, as formas de pagamento, os níveis de pagamento e a gestão e utilização dos fundos para os serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono em florestas; projetos de carbono florestal; determinação dos resultados da redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa; e créditos de carbono florestal concedidos. "O decreto permite que os proprietários de florestas colaborem no desenvolvimento de projetos de crédito de carbono. Isso exige que as autoridades locais em nível municipal, bem como os departamentos provinciais e municipais de agricultura e meio ambiente, elaborem planos de implementação", disse o Sr. Huy. Segundo o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, a participação no mercado de carbono é uma estratégia inovadora para consolidar a posição da cidade e criar capital verde para ela. Em agosto de 2026, o Comitê Popular da Cidade de Da Nang aprovou o Projeto de Desenvolvimento e Gestão de Créditos de Carbono Florestal na Cidade de Da Nang para o período de 2026 a 2030, com uma visão para 2035. Da Nang está implementando soluções para desenvolver uma oferta de créditos de carbono florestal, incluindo a coordenação com a cidade de Hue e a província de Quang Ngai para melhorar a qualidade da gestão florestal, criar uma oferta de créditos de carbono de alta qualidade e conectar-se gradualmente aos mercados nacional e internacional por meio do ecossistema do Centro Financeiro Internacional do Vietnã em Da Nang. Simultaneamente, está pesquisando um programa piloto para uma troca voluntária de créditos de carbono dentro do Centro Financeiro Internacional. A cidade também se concentra no desenvolvimento de uma economia circular e de múltiplos valores, como: mecanismos para arrendamento de terras florestais; desenvolvimento da economia sob a copa das árvores; plantio de grandes florestas de madeira em áreas concentradas, vinculadas à certificação florestal sustentável (FSC) e aos padrões EUDR; e integração do ecoturismo florestal com o turismo comunitário... tudo com o objetivo de melhorar os meios d

artigo.texto: - The second-generation BYD Seal 07 features a larger body and a lower starting price of 139,900 yuan ($20,830). - The all-electric version's range increases to 775 kilometers, while the plug-in hybrid's electric range reaches 330 kilometers. BYD (HKEX: 1211) launched the second-generation Seal 07 in China on Thursday, refreshing both the all-electric and plug-in hybrid versions with lower starting prices and longer range. The new model is available in 5 trims, with official guide prices ranging from 139,900 yuan ($20,830) to 172,900 yuan, comprising 2 DM-i plug-in hybrid variants and 3 all-electric variants. The 2 DM-i plug-in hybrid variants are priced at 139,900 yuan and 149,900 yuan, respectively, and both feature a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine. The 3 all-electric variants are priced at 149,900 yuan, 159,900 yuan, and 172,900 yuan, respectively, and share the same powertrain and range specifications. BYD is offering trade-in prices ranging from 135,900 yuan to 168,900 yuan, a reduction of 4,000 yuan from each variant's guide price, subject to trade-in eligibility requirements. The all-electric version's starting guide price is 20,000 yuan, or about 12%, lower than that of the Seal 07 EV launched on March 5 this year. The generational update comes only about 8 months after that model's launch. The plug-in hybrid's starting guide price is 9,900 yuan, or about 7%, lower than that of the 2026 Seal 07 DM-i launched in September 2025, with the lineup streamlined from 4 variants to 2. The outgoing 2026 DM-i had launch guide prices ranging from 149,800 yuan to 186,800 yuan, offering electric ranges of 135 kilometers and 230 kilometers, with 2 trims for each. The new model adopts the Ocean Aesthetics 2.0 design language. Both the all-electric and plug-in hybrid versions measure 5,080 mm in length, 1,960 mm in width, and 1,495 mm in height, with a wheelbase of 2,960 mm. Compared with their respective outgoing models, both versions are 85 mm longer and have a 60 mm longer wheelbase, while their widths increase by 50 mm and 60 mm, respectively. All new-generation DM-i variants feature a 38-kWh battery, delivering a CLTC electric range of 330 kilometers (205 miles), an increase of 100 kilometers from the outgoing model's maximum of 230 kilometers. All all-electric variants offer a CLTC range of 775 kilometers, up 70 kilometers from the 705 kilometers offered by the model launched in March, and feature a 76.744-kWh second-generation Blade Battery supporting flash charging. All 3 all-electric variants use a single rear-mounted motor and rear-wheel drive, with a maximum output of 245 kW (329 hp) and peak torque of 365 Nm. The all-electric version accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 5.5 seconds, 1 second quicker than the model launched in March, and has a top speed of 240 km/h. A heat pump system is standard across the all-electric lineup. All new-generation DM-i variants use front-wheel drive, pairing a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine producing up to 115 kW with a 160-kW front motor. Acceleration from 0 to 100 km/h takes 7.7 seconds. The outgoing DM-i's entry-level variant paired a 74-kW 1.5-liter naturally aspirated engine with a 160-kW motor, accelerating from 0 to 100 km/h in 8 seconds. The outgoing model's other 3 trims paired a 115-kW 1.5-liter turbocharged engine with a 200-kW motor and completed the sprint in 6.9 seconds, meaning the generational update does not improve performance across all versions. The new-generation DM-i's main improvement is its electric range, while powertrain specifications have been standardized across the lineup. Its NEDC fuel consumption with a depleted battery is 3.3 liters per 100 kilometers. Driver-assistance equipment has also been adjusted. The 2 higher-priced all-electric variants and the higher-priced DM-i variant come standard with God's Eye C, supporting highway and urban expressway navigation assistance (HNOA). These 3 variants offer the LiDAR-equipped God's Eye B driver-assistance system as an option, adding city navigation assistance (CNOA), rather than making the LiDAR-based system standard across the lineup. The entry-level trims of both the all-electric and DM-i versions feature conventional cruise control but do not offer God's Eye C or the option to add God's Eye B. They lack the city, highway, and urban expressway navigation assistance functions mentioned above. By comparison, the outgoing DM-i's 3 lower-priced variants came standard with God's Eye C, while the top trim featured LiDAR-equipped God's Eye B as standard, meaning the new model's lower starting price comes alongside changes to driver-assistance equipment. For the chassis, all all-electric variants feature front double-wishbone and rear five-link independent suspension, with the lower-priced variants equipped with the DiSus-C intelligent damping body control system. The flagship all-electric variant instead features the DiSus-M intelligent magnetorheological body control system. Both DM-i variants feature DiSus-C, which was absent from the outgoing DM-i's entry-level version. Storage space differs by powertrain. The all-electric version offers a 618-liter trunk and a 160-liter frunk, while the DM-i has a 595-liter trunk. The generational update comes as sales of the Seal lineup remain under pressure. The lineup sold 46,834 vehicles in October, down 19.32% year-on-year but up 0.25% from September, according to data compiled by CnEVPost. In the first 10 months of this year, Seal lineup sales totaled 351,557 vehicles, down 14.85% year-on-year. These figures cover the Seal 07 and several other models, rather than the Seal 07 alone. ($1 = 6.7156 yuan)
