artigo.texto: A “blunami” swept the nation last night as Democrats defeated Republicans to gain control of the House and Senate in a historic midterm landslide. And it looks like data centers played a key role in the outcome. A lot was on Americans’ minds as they went to the polls. The war on Iran. Cost of living. Brutal immigration policies. Healthcare cuts. Culture wars. For a small number of online weirdos, Anakin Skywalker. Among the hottest issues, though, was one that would’ve barely registered in 2024: AI data centers. Exit polls conducted by NBC showed that almost a full quarter of voters surveyed counted “AI data centers” as “crucial” to their vote, with over half listing the issue as a “crucial” or “major” factor in their decision. Only a minute 13 percent of voters said data centers were a non-issue. Asked about the importance of “AI and data centers” to their vote, an overwhelming 56 percent of Americans responded that the issues played a “crucial or major factor” in their ballot. Opposition to data centers, particularly the massive hyper-scale facilities associated with powering AI, has emerged as a powerful bipartisan issue across the country. The structures have drawn intense pushback from many locals concerned about pollution, loss of natural land, noise — large data centers emit constant, awful screeching — and hikes in energy prices. Local and state lawmakers have faced scrutiny over revelations that many signed non-disclosure agreements with AI companies to keep quiet about the projects, keeping voters in the dark about huge infrastructure deals standing to radically transform their region. Data center fights have also been playing out largely in rural areas, which traditionally skew conservative, making for cross-party coalitions uniting against the AI-powering infrastructure. As Bloomberg notes, surprise Democratic swings will likely lead to uncertainty for many planned data center projects. The now-former Republican governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, welcomed data centers back in 2025, then in August suddenly moved to implement new regulations on the sites as his re-election race against his opponent, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, tightened. On the campaign trail, Hinojosa called for a moratorium on data center builds until the state held a “legislative session that puts Texans first so that we don’t have any more communities in Texas who are powerless against these global corporations.” Hinajosa won last night in a surprise upset, and while the blue wave in Texas can be chalked up to several issues — immigration, affordability, war — the data center battle seems to epitomize the backlash to establishment politics that pushed Democrats back into power across the country. Overall, the midterm results were a massive hit to some of the most powerful players in tech and AI. Billionaire tech megadonors including world’s richest man Elon Musk, the investors Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, and OpenAI president Greg Brockman, among others, poured an extraordinary amount of money into the midterms on behalf of Republicans. Now that those efforts failed, data center moratoriums, congressional investigations, and assertive new efforts at regulation are looming large. artigo.texto: The Korea Consumer Agency (KCA) on the 4th ordered Mercedes-Benz Korea to pay 4 million won per owner, saying the company failed to properly disclose the manufacturer of its electric vehicle batteries. On this day, the Consumer Dispute Settlement Commission of the agency said that although Chinese Farasis battery cells were installed in five EQE and EQS models, the company explained them as if only CATL batteries were installed, and found it liable for damages. The compensation covers 142 buyers of the EQE 500 4MATIC SUV, EQE 53 4MATIC+, EQE 350+, EQE 350 4MATIC, and EQS 350 who applied for group dispute mediation in May. The panel considered that EV batteries are a core component directly tied not only to driving performance but also to safety, and a key factor that determines an electric vehicle's value. It also acknowledged that Farasis and CATL differ significantly in market share, recognition, and technological prowess. After receiving the decision from the agency, Mercedes-Benz Korea must notify the commission within 15 days whether it accepts the terms. If Mercedes-Benz Korea accepts, the decision takes effect as a judicial settlement. If it does not accept, Mercedes-Benz Korea does not have to compensate. In that case, consumers can file individual civil lawsuits. Han Yong-ho, chair of the agency's dispute mediation commission, said, "We hope Mercedes-Benz Korea will take a more proactive stance in resolving the dispute so that trust in German imports among Korean consumers can be restored."

artigo.texto: Midterms Could Deepen the K-Shaped AI Trade as Data Center Curbs Favor Big Tech Companies Democratic gubernatorial victories and data-center restrictions could benefit financially stronger technology companies by making it harder for smaller companies to compete. The midterm elections could hand America's biggest technology companies an unexpected advantage from the restrictions on the data centers powering artificial intelligence, making their existing infrastructure more valuable while making expansion harder for smaller, heavily indebted rivals. Democratic victories in gubernatorial races have sharpened concerns about permitting delays, electricity demands and the cost of building AI capacity. For investors, those pressures could deepen a K-shaped trade, with financially stronger companies advancing as more vulnerable operators struggle. Wednesday's trading illustrated that divide. Microsoft and Amazon each gained more than 6%, while specialized AI cloud provider CoreWeave dropped about 10%. Micron fell 7%, and Nvidia declined 3.17%. Texas has become a central test as Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to stop new data center approvals until lawmakers establish protections for residents. Projects already under construction would be exempt, potentially giving operators with facilities underway an advantage over developers still seeking permission. Hinojosa's proposal follows restrictions imposed under Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, including a halt to new grid connections and an audit of projects. Her victory increases uncertainty about how long those constraints could last. The investment implications extend beyond construction schedules. Companies with operating facilities can keep selling computing services while competitors wait for approvals. If demand remains strong and supply arrives more slowly, access to existing capacity could become more valuable. James Sullivan, JPMorgan's managing director and co-head of global fundamental research, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Thursday that financing costs help explain the split. "The fact that you're seeing this bifurcation in equity performance is largely driven by the view that existing capacity is significantly more valuable now because of incremental supply constraints," Sullivan said. He said borrowing spreads have widened substantially for neoclouds, specialized providers of AI computing infrastructure. That leaves them facing higher costs for additional capital than hyperscalers, the large cloud operators with broader businesses and more diverse revenue. For debt-funded developers, delays can compound financial pressure. Equipment and construction require money before facilities generate revenue. A longer wait for permits or power can postpone customer deliveries while financing obligations remain. The strain predates the election as CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren each lost at least 30% in October. CoreWeave's five-year credit default swap spread climbed above 1,100 basis points, signaling a higher price for protection against default. In a research note, JPMorgan Asset Management said lower-rated neoclouds were particularly exposed to borrowing costs, energy prices and refinancing conditions. Hyperscalers have more internally generated cash and stronger access to credit, giving them greater room to absorb setbacks. Much of the capacity scheduled to open in 2027 is already being built, limiting the immediate effect. Projects targeting 2028 are more exposed to permitting uncertainty, Nomura said in a Wednesday note cited by the outlet. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: BYD India, a subsidiary of BYD, the world’s No. 1 New Energy Vehicle (NEV) manufacturer,today announced that the BYD SEALION 7 has crossed 5,000 customer deliveries in India since its launch in February 2025. The SEALION 7 brings together ocean-inspired design and BYD’s battery and vehicle technologies, including Blade Battery technology and Cell-to-Body architecture. Its Premium variantpairs an 82.56 kWh battery with a claimed NEDC range of 567 km, while the dual-motor Performance variant delivers 390 kW of power and 690 Nm of torque, accelerating from 0–100 km/h in 4.5 seconds. Both variants feature a panoramic glass roof and a 15.6-inchrotating touchscreen. Commenting on the milestone, Mr. Rajeev Chauhan, Head of Electric Passenger Vehicle Business, BYD India, said, “The SEALION 7 has been one of our strongest-performing models in India, and we are proud of the response it has received from customers. This reflects the growing interest in electric SUVs that combine performance, technology and premium comfort.As we look ahead, our focus is on building on this momentum, strengthening the ownership experience and bringing more of BYD’s technology to Indian customers through a product portfolio that responds to their evolving needs.” In August 2026, BYD India introduced the SEALION 7 Dynamic at an introductory ex-showroom price of INR 41.90 lakh. Its 71.8 kWh Blade Battery offers a claimed NEDC range of 520 km, bringing a new entry point to the SEALION 7 range while retaining features such as the panoramic glassroof and rotating touchscreen. The SEALION 7 Festive Edition, launched in October 2026 at INR 50.60 lakh (ex-showroom), adds a Tan and Black interior to the Premium variant. Limited to 150 units, it also features quilted Nappa leather seats, a panoramic glass roof with an electric sunshade and a head-up display. The edition is part of BYD India’s Celebrate Your Dreams with BYD festive campaign. The SEALION 7 has also earned recognition across the automotive industry, including a maximum 5-Star safety rating from Euro NCAP, Luxury Mid-size SUV of the Year at the ACKO DriveTOTM 2026, Premium EV of the Year at the car&bike Awards 2026, Premium SUV of the Year at the TV9 Awards, and Best EV Design at the CarBike360 Auto Excellence Awards 2026. Reinforcing BYD’s broader leadership in electric mobility and battery technology, its Blade Battery was recognised as the Best New EV Battery Technology at the CarBike360 Auto ExcellenceAwards 2026, while BYD was honoured as the Pioneer in Battery Technology by Jagran Hi-Tech. The company also ranks No. 91 on the 2026 Fortune Global 500 list, marking its fifth consecutive year on the prestigious index.

artigo.texto: O rápido crescimento da inteligência artificial (IA) aberta, aliado à demanda crescente por novos centros de processamento de dados (data centers) para dar suporte a essa tecnologia, constitui uma clara demonstração dos avanços na utilização de novas tecnologias. No entanto, essa visão positiva frequentemente encobre os impactos que essas inovações exercem sobre a sociedade e o meio ambiente. O elevado consumo de energia e de água são dois exemplos importantes que precisam ser considerados em uma avaliação justa e detalhada do papel dessas tecnologias e dos custos que representam para a sociedade e o meio ambiente. O artigo dos professores Francisco Antônio R. Barbosa e Francisco César Sá Barreto, este último membro titular da ABC, propõe uma análise aprofundada dos impactos e das consequências dessas novas tecnologias para a sociedade e o meio ambiente, particularmente no que diz respeito à conservação e ao uso sustentável da água e da energia. Espera-se que essa análise, publicada nos Anais da ABC (AABC), contribua para estabelecer parâmetros e identificar limites para a expansão e a utilização dessas infraestruturas tecnológicas, além de promover maior clareza quanto às regulamentações existentes, de modo a garantir que seu desenvolvimento não agrave ainda mais a ultrapassagem dos limites planetários, já comprometidos pelas atividades humanas. Leia o artigo original completo na página dos Anais da ABC na SciELO

artigo.texto: - The all-electric Denza N9 features a tri-motor all-wheel-drive system with a combined peak output of 890 kW (1,194 hp). - The Denza N9 is currently available only as a PHEV, with a starting price of 409,800 yuan ($61,000). An all-electric version of the N9, the flagship SUV from BYD's (HKEX: 1211) premium brand Denza, has appeared in a Chinese regulatory filing, adding a new powertrain option to a model currently sold as a plug-in hybrid. China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published batch 413 of its new vehicle catalog for public comment on Wednesday, revealing key specifications of the large SUV. The public comment period runs from November 4 to November 10. Inclusion in the catalog is a regulatory step before a vehicle can go on sale and does not mean it has received final approval. The all-electric N9 features a tri-motor all-wheel-drive system with a combined peak output of 890 kW (1,194 hp), exceeding the 680 kW of the N9 plug-in hybrid flash charging edition launched in May. Its front motor has a peak output of 270 kW, while the rear left and rear right motors each deliver 310 kW. The filing lists a top speed of 240 km/h (149 mph). The catalog includes 2 model codes, QCJ6530ABBEV1 and QCJ6530ABBEV2, with identical dimensions, seating options and motor outputs. Both entries list 5- and 6-seat layouts. The vehicle measures 5,270 mm in length, 2,030 mm in width and 1,830 mm in height, with a wheelbase of 3,125 mm. Images in the filings show that the all-electric version retains the N9's overall exterior design and features a roof-mounted LiDAR sensor. A panoramic glass roof and power side steps come standard, while options include a two-tone body. The new vehicle uses a lithium iron phosphate battery with cells produced by FinDreams Battery, BYD's battery division. The filings do not disclose battery capacity, driving range or charging performance. Denza first launched the N9 in March 2025, entering the large luxury SUV market with the flagship model, initially offered as a 6-seat plug-in hybrid. On May 18 this year, Denza launched the N9 flash charging edition with a starting price of 409,800 yuan ($61,000), featuring BYD's second-generation Blade Battery and flash charging technology. The plug-in hybrid has a 75.3 kWh battery that delivers a CLTC electric range of 420 km (261 miles). Denza said at the time that charging from 10% to 97% takes just 9 minutes. ($1 = 6.7180 yuan)

artigo.texto: A provedora de serviços de data center Ascenty anunciou nesta quarta-feira, 4, a inauguração de um laboratório especializado em infraestrutura de Inteligência Artificial (IA) em seu campus em Vinhedo, no interior de São Paulo. Na prática, clientes poderão testar, validar e otimizar soluções de diferentes fornecedores antes de implantá-las em escala. A iniciativa chamada Digital Realty Innovation Lab (DRIL) é a primeira do tipo na América Latina. A empresa mantém laboratórios semelhantes na Virgínia (Estados Unidos), em Tóquio (Japão) e Londres (Reino Unido). Novos espaços devem ser inaugurados ainda neste ano em Singapura e Joanesburgo (África do Sul). Segundo a Ascenty, a unidade paulista combina infraestrutura de alta densidade, tecnologias avançadas de refrigeração, conectividade resiliente e soluções de parceiros. O DRIL São Paulo foi projetado para testar cargas de trabalho com racks que utilizam liquid cooling preparados para densidades de 150 quilowatts (kW) ou mais. Em linhas gerais, usando o laboratório, os clientes poderão avaliar como componentes e aplicações funcionam em conjunto e identificar a arquitetura mais adequada para as suas necessidades operacionais. Inclusive, para os testes em condições reais de operação, o sistema de conectividade conta com duas entrada de fibra óptica por rotas distintas e uma infraestrutura neutra, abrindo espaço para diferentes provedores. "Trazer o DRIL para São Paulo significa investir diretamente no futuro da IA na América Latina. Nosso compromisso com a região é sustentado por anos de construção e operação de infraestrutura, o que nos possibilita entender o que nossos clientes precisam e apoiá-los no seu desenvolvimento", afirma Chris Torto, fundador e CEO da Ascenty, em nota.

artigo.texto: India has announced a new VGF scheme to support 92 GWh of energy storage, including 30 GWh of BESS The VGF scheme introduces a minimum domestic content requirement to encourage local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports The government will also support lithium and nickel processing plants through a 30% capital subsidy under another scheme India is stepping up efforts to build a domestic battery supply chain, with the Union Cabinet approving two schemes to support grid-scale energy storage deployment and critical mineral processing. The government has allocated INR 14,500 crore in viability gap funding (VGF) for 92 GWh of energy storage capacity and INR 2,814 crore to develop domestic lithium and nickel processing capabilities. A lion’s share of the total ESS capacity, 60 GWh, to be supported under VGF will come from pumped storage projects (PSP), while 30 GWh will come from battery energy storage systems (BESS), and 2 GWh from emerging storage technologies. VGF, the Ministry of Power (MoP) explained, will improve the financial viability of the projects that together will attract an investment of approximately INR 97,600 crore. Public and private sector companies will be eligible for VGF support for both PSP and BESS projects, which will be awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding. Alternative storage technologies will be implemented by public and private sector companies. Funding will be provided over five years, from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. According to the MoP, the scheme aims to add capacity equivalent to 170% of India’s existing grid-scale energy storage capacity to help meet the projected requirement of 411 GWh by FY 2031-32. A highlight of the VGF Scheme for the Development of Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems is its focus on local BESS manufacturing. The government has made it mandatory for eligible projects to ensure a minimum domestic content requirement (DCR) of 40%. This 'demand-side' financial support will encourage domestic manufacturing and reduce reliance on imported components, stated the MoP. “The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing,” added the ministry. Alongside creating demand for domestic BESS component production, the government is also offering funding support for local manufacturing. The INR 2,814 crore Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing aims to develop India’s processing facilities for critical minerals – lithium and nickel. Lithium-ion technology currently dominates the BESS space. The scheme will provide a 30% capital subsidy on eligible investments to set up four processing plants: two lithium facilities with a minimum capacity of 30,000 tons each and two nickel facilities with a minimum capacity of 50,000 tons each. Support is capped at INR 500 crore per lithium plant beneficiary and INR 900 crore per nickel plant beneficiary. These facilities will process lithium and nickel ores and intermediate products into high-purity compounds, with cobalt expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel processing. Beneficiaries will be selected through two-phase techno-commercial bidding, based on the lowest CapEx support sought. Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches. These measures come as India seeks to reduce its dependence on China for battery materials, components, and technology. The Asian giant dominates the global battery supply chain, particularly in processing critical minerals and manufacturing battery cells and components. Compared to landed Chinese benchmark prices, Indian manufacturers face cost disability ranging from 18% for Cathode Active Material and Nickle Manganese Cobalt (CAM-NMC) to 61% for Anode Active Material-Synthetic Graphite (AAM-SG), as per a Ministry of Heavy Industries study. Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) comprises CAM, AAM, electrolyte, separator, and current collectors. ACC components account for about 76% of total cell manufacturing cost, with the cathode at 34% and the anode at 25%, according to the study. According to The Economic Times, the Ministry of Heavy Industries is considering capital subsidies of up to 50% and sales-linked incentives to boost domestic manufacturing of battery materials and components. The proposed incentives would implement existing government support for battery manufacturing, including the INR 18,100 crore Production Linked Incentives (PLI) scheme for ACC battery manufacturing.

artigo.texto: advertisement Ohio Voters Push Back Against The AI Data Center Boom On Election Day, the AI infrastructure boom met the ballot box. In nearly every community where data centers were put to a vote, opposition prevailed. The vote in Trenton wasn’t close. About 80 per cent of voters in the Butler County city backed a ban on large data centres, according to unofficial results reported by WVXU. Trenton was among at least 14 Ohio municipalities that approved bans or new restrictions on November 3, in what emerged as one of the most concentrated local tests yet of public sentiment towards the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence. advertisement Ohio accounted for 21 of the 41 data centre measures on ballots nationwide, spread across 18 municipalities, Fortune reported. CNBC’s headline put the national result bluntly: voters rejected data centers in every ballot measure except one. Stateline reported that 33 local measures restricting data centers had passed or were leading late Tuesday, with North Dakota the only state where a result favoured the industry. The number of measures varies by outlet, from 41 to 45. Results also remain unofficial until certified by county authorities. What the votes did, and didn’t, do advertisement In Sunbury, voters appeared to approve a charter amendment banning data centers with capacity of 25 megawatts or more. The measure was aimed at a possible hyperscale Amazon project, although its future remains unclear. Pataskala approved a similar ban. In Perry, more than 87 per cent of voters backed a requirement that developers seeking tax breaks provide financial guarantees. In Wilmington, about 80 per cent rejected proposals to rezone land for a data center across four referendums. Some outcomes, however, may have limited practical effect. advertisement In Ashville, about 82 per cent of voters supported reversing the village’s agreement with EdgeConneX to build two data centers. But construction has already begun, and NBC4 reported that the vote would not stop the projects. Trenton’s ban puts a 250-megawatt data center under construction in its industrial park in question. It does not affect a separate Amazon campus just outside the city. Trenton abandoned its bid to annex that land in September, the Cincinnati Enquirer reported. Amazon declined to say whether the measures would change its plans, but said its commitment to host communities remained unchanged. Why electricity bills matter The public opposition is closely tied to household energy costs. A Gallup survey in May found that about 70 per cent of Americans opposed having data centers in their local communities. A Heatmap poll published the week before the election found that rising electricity prices were the leading reason for opposition. In PJM Interconnection, the grid operator serving 13 states from New Jersey to northern Illinois, capacity prices rose from $28.92 per megawatt-day in 2024-25 to $329.17 for 2026-27. The grid’s independent market monitor estimated that data centers accounted for 63 per cent of the increase in the 2025-26 auction, adding $9.3 billion in charges, according to the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). IEEFA estimated that the increase would add about $16 a month to the average residential electricity bill in Ohio and $18 in western Maryland. The extent to which data centers are responsible for higher bills remains contested. Brookings notes that experts disagree over how much of the increase should be attributed to data centers, compared with weather, infrastructure constraints and other factors. “Ohio does not have a data center cost crisis,” the Ohio Manufacturers’ Association said. The candidates The debate also reached statewide and national races. In Ohio’s Senate race, Democrat Sherrod Brown defeated Republican Senator Jon Husted. Brown campaigned on ending tax breaks for data centers and requiring companies to pay for the utility infrastructure their campuses need. He also called Husted “the face of data centers”. Husted defended the tax incentives, citing their potential economic benefits. In Michigan, NBC News projected Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as the winner. At a July event, he said, “People really effing hate data centers”, E&E News reported. His opponent, Mike Rogers, said in August that he supported a one-year moratorium. Both candidates in Ohio’s governor’s race, Democrat Amy Acton, who won, and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, proposed moratoriums. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds, who won, proposed restrictions. In Georgia, Democrats won both Public Service Commission seats, securing a 3-2 majority on the board that sets utility rates for the first time in about 30 years, according to Inside Climate News. Peter Hubbard won by 12.8 percentage points, while Sheila Edwards won by 10.6 points. Georgia Power customers have seen their monthly bills rise by about $44 across six increases since 2023. The costs of gas-fired power plants built to serve data centers have also been added to customer bills. “The results show that people are very angry about data centers and climate emissions,” said Patty Durand of Georgians for Affordable Energy. The industry’s money The industry mounted its own campaign ahead of the votes. Build American AI, which is linked to the Leading the Future super PAC, spent at least $2.54 million on television advertisements in Ohio promoting the economic benefits of data centers, DeSmog reported. The advertisements cited $40 billion in investment and more than 95,000 jobs, although they did not endorse individual candidates. AI-focused super PACs spent an estimated $72 million to $79 million nationally, depending on the tracker. Fortune reported that most of the Republicans they backed in competitive races lost, including Darline Graham in South Carolina, who received more than $4.8 million in support. Pete Ricketts won in Nebraska. Democrats won both chambers of Congress, Gizmodo reported. There is no evidence t

artigo.texto: With the expansion of renewable energy, the global demand for high-performance battery energy storage systems (BESS) is growing. They compensate for fluctuations in electricity generation from wind and solar energy, stabilise electricity grids and create the conditions for a flexible and reliable energy supply. In modern containers, power supply, data and fire protection systems operate together in a very confined space, often at high temperatures and in a humid environment. High-voltage cables and data cables must function reliably side by side, withstand mechanical stresses and deliver consistent signal quality over the long term. A leading global manufacturer of battery energy storage systems, based in Korea, also faced this challenge. For a large-scale BESS project, the company was seeking high-performance and reliable connectivity solutions for various applications within the storage architecture. The requirements included robust products for power and data transmission, as well as comprehensive technical support for planning and implementation. This is where LAPP, the global market leader in integrated solutions for cable and connection technology, came into the picture. Complexity in a confined space The user required end-to-end connection technology for different areas within its BESS platform. In addition to the main power transmission, auxiliary power supply, internal wiring, signal and bus communication, as well as Industrial Ethernet applications, also had to be supported reliably. Furthermore, fire-resistant cables and cable assemblies were used for the integration of the systems. The challenge was to integrate these different requirements into a consistent and reliable infrastructure. The project was further complicated by demanding operating conditions. The selected components had to deliver reliable performance in high-temperature and humid environments. In addition, the customer required highly flexible cable solutions to facilitate installation within the systems. Since modern battery energy storage systems depend on continuous communication between sensors, control units, and energy management systems, maintaining consistently high signal and data integrity was equally critical. In addition to the technical requirements, the time factor also played a decisive role. The customer expected rapid project implementation and close technical support during qualification and integration. Rather than a mere supplier of individual components, they were therefore looking for a partner who understood the application and could provide the appropriate solution for every aspect of the battery storage system. Connectivity solutions for all levels of the battery storage system To meet the project’s diverse requirements, LAPP Korea worked closely with the customer to develop a customised connectivity concept. The goal was to equip the various areas of the battery energy storage system with a seamless and reliable connectivity infrastructure.Rather than supplying individual components, LAPP adopted a holistic approach and provided integrated solutions which, in many cases, replaced conventional cabling methods. This enabled higher standards of robustness and signal quality, whilst simultaneously reducing complexity and ensuring high operational reliability and resilience. This comprehensive approach was made possible through close technical collaboration throughout the project. From the early analysis phase onwards, LAPP Korea’s team tailored cables, connectors, and cable assemblies to the specific requirements of each application area. During qualification and integration, the team maintained direct collaboration with the customer’s engineers, helping to streamline specifications and accelerate testing activities. Within LAPP Korea, too, the sales, technical and operational departments worked closely together: queries were resolved immediately and qualification steps were processed swiftly. This enabled the project to move quickly into the integration phase and meet the customer’s schedule. A blueprint for future projects The successful course of the project highlights how important it is to take a holistic view of connection technology in modern battery energy storage systems. Power transmission, data communication and safety technology must work together reliably to ensure that BESS systems can be operated efficiently and safely in the long term. This was made possible by a combination of application-specific advice, tailored products and technical support, which enabled even the most demanding requirements within modern storage architecture to be reliably implemented during the project. As the market continues to grow, the importance of such end-to-end solutions will only increase, as larger and more complex energy storage systems require integrated concepts rather than individual components. “Solution-oriented offerings that are precisely tailored to customers’ requirements remain the key to taking the lead in the ESS market,” emphasises Chenjie Gu, Industry Manager for Battery Manufacturing at LAPP. After all, when the sun goes down and the wind dies down, the connection technology must be in place so that battery storage systems can step in.

artigo.texto: Euforia com data centers no Brasil esbarra em regras A aprovação do Redata gerou euforia inicial com uma potencial onda de investimentos em data centers no País, mas a demora na regulamentação da lei está acendendo um sinal de alerta. Até o momento, nenhum novo projeto foi anunciado – e a consultoria Rystad Energy mapeou riscos que podem reduzir drasticamente as expectativas. A indefinição sobre regras para enquadramento de fontes de energia e acesso à rede elétrica preocupa empresários e investidores do setor. Regulamentação pendente gera incertezas A proposta original do Governo para o Redata beneficiaria apenas data centers que contratassem 100% de sua energia com fontes renováveis. No Congresso, o texto foi alterado para contemplar projetos com fontes “de baixa emissão”. O Ministério de Minas e Energia defendeu publicamente que instalações movidas a gás pudessem ser enquadradas na lei, com essa nova redação. Mas o Ministério da Fazenda tem defendido limitações ou compensações para o uso do combustível fóssil, fontes a par do assunto disseram ao Brazil Journal. Um decreto presidencial detalhando as regras para enquadramento não foi publicado até o momento. Essa indefinição trava decisões de investimento e adia anúncios de novos empreendimentos. Gás natural divide ministérios “Ainda está pendente uma decisão do Poder Executivo sobre se a geração a gás natural se qualifica como energia de baixa emissão, além de detalhes críticos sobre métricas de eficiência energética, conteúdo local e verificações de compliance”, disse a VP e chefe de Novas Energias da Rystad Energy para a América Latina, Camila Ramos. Em sua análise sobre o Redata, ela também citou a concorrência por espaço na rede elétrica para conexão dos data centers e potenciais limitações no acesso a energia firme como fatores que aumentam o risco para o desenvolvimento de projetos no País. A divergência entre os ministérios reflete a complexidade de equilibrar segurança energética e metas ambientais. Enquanto o MME vê o gás como alternativa viável para garantir energia firme, a Fazenda busca evitar incentivos a combustíveis fósseis. Essa disputa atrasa a publicação do decreto e mantém o setor em compasso de espera. Potencial de 20,8 GW pode encolher A Rystad mapeou 20,8 GW em potenciais data centers previstos inicialmente para implantação no Brasil até 2035. Um número que despenca para uma estimativa de 6,7 GW quando ponderados todos os riscos. Nas contas da consultoria, mais de 10 GW em projetos são “de alto risco” e quase uma dezena de GW são de “médio risco”. Essa redução de cerca de dois terços na capacidade esperada evidencia o impacto das incertezas regulatórias e de infraestrutura. Para o interior paulista, onde cidades como Araçatuba e Birigui buscam atrair investimentos em tecnologia, a indefinição pode adiar a chegada de empregos qualificados e dinamização do comércio local. A fonte não detalhou quais projetos específicos estão em risco, mas o cenário geral exige cautela. Impacto para negócios do noroeste paulista A eventual implantação de data centers na região poderia gerar demanda por serviços de construção, manutenção, alimentação e hospedagem, beneficiando pequenas e médias empresas. No entanto, a falta de clareza sobre as regras do Redata mantém os investidores em compasso de espera. Empresários locais acompanham o desenrolar da regulamentação, cientes de que a atração desses empreendimentos depende de um ambiente jurídico estável. Além disso, a concorrência por espaço na rede elétrica pode afetar o fornecimento de energia para outras atividades produtivas, elevando custos ou exigindo investimentos em infraestrutura. A indefinição sobre o uso de gás natural também pode influenciar a matriz energética regional, com reflexos nos preços para o comércio e a indústria. Até que o decreto seja publicado, o potencial de 20,8 GW permanece apenas no papel. Perguntas Frequentes Por que a euforia com os data centers no Brasil está diminuindo? A demora na regulamentação do Redata está acendendo um sinal de alerta, e até o momento nenhum novo projeto foi anunciado. Qual é a divergência entre os ministérios sobre o enquadramento de data centers a gás no Redata? O Ministério de Minas e Energia defende que instalações movidas a gás possam ser enquadradas como ‘baixa emissão’, enquanto o Ministério da Fazenda defende limitações ou compensações para o uso do combustível fóssil. Qual é a estimativa da Rystad para a capacidade de data centers no Brasil até 2035? A Rystad mapeou 20,8 GW em potenciais data centers, mas a estimativa cai para 6,7 GW quando ponderados todos os riscos, com mais de 10 GW considerados de alto risco.

artigo.texto: O Bitcoin hoje (5) recuava 5,17%, cotado a US$ 76.268,30 por volta das 16h18. A principal pressão vinha da forte aversão ao risco nos mercados internacionais, com investidores reduzindo a exposição a empresas de tecnologia, fabricantes de chips e operadoras de data centers. O BTC começou a sessão acima de US$ 80,5 mil e permaneceu próximo desse patamar durante a manhã. A queda ganhou força depois das 14h, quando o ativo perdeu sucessivamente as faixas de US$ 79 mil, US$ 78 mil e US$ 77 mil. Na mínima registrada durante a tarde, o Bitcoin se aproximou de US$ 75,6 mil. A cotação ensaiou uma recuperação até a região de US$ 76,8 mil, mas devolveu parte do avanço e permanecia pouco acima de US$ 76 mil no fim da tarde. A pressão sobre os ativos de maior risco também aparecia nas bolsas americanas. Por volta das 15h47, o Nasdaq caía 5,10%, enquanto o S&P 500 perdia 3,92% e o Dow Jones recuava 3,09%. O VIX, indicador acompanhado como termômetro da incerteza, disparava 59,69%, para 26,46 pontos. Tecnologia e data centers lideram aversão ao risco A queda do Bitcoin acompanhava uma forte venda de ações ligadas à inteligência artificial e à expansão dos data centers. A AMD despencava 15,59%, enquanto CoreWeave (CRWV), Qualcomm (QCOM; QCOM34), Broadcom (AVGO; AVGO34) e Nvidia (NVDA; NVDC34) registravam perdas entre 8,60% e 12,60%. O setor era pressionado pelo receio de que o novo Congresso americano amplie a fiscalização sobre a construção de data centers. A vitória dos democratas nas eleições de meio de mandato aumentou as dúvidas sobre possíveis restrições à expansão dessa infraestrutura, especialmente nos estados onde cresce a oposição aos projetos. A Qualcomm acrescentava pressão ao segmento após divulgar vendas de chips para celulares abaixo das expectativas. As perdas alcançavam ainda Meta, Microsoft e Alphabet, indicando uma redução mais ampla da exposição às empresas associadas ao avanço da inteligência artificial. O Bitcoin foi atingido por essa busca por menor risco. Embora não acompanhe as bolsas em todos os pregões, a criptomoeda permanece sensível a sessões de forte volatilidade, especialmente quando a retirada de recursos alcança ativos tecnológicos e investimentos mais sujeitos a oscilações. A queda desta quinta-feira retirou o BTC da região de US$ 80 mil e levou a cotação ao menor patamar do dia perto de US$ 75,6 mil. A recuperação observada posteriormente ainda não havia sido suficiente para devolver a criptomoeda à faixa dos US$ 77 mil até as 16h18. Leia também:

artigo.texto: Vendedor misterioso coloca US$ 500 milhões em dívidas de data centers à venda em meio a dúvidas sobre IA Operação reúne dívidas de projetos ligados à OpenAI e outras empresas e reflete cautela crescente de investidores de Wall Street sobre o retorno dos projetos Um investidor cuja identidade não foi revelada colocou à venda um conjunto de empréstimos de cerca de US$ 500 milhões concedidos a empresas de data centers. A operação é incomum por reunir, em um único leilão, dívidas de diferentes projetos do setor. - Efeito: Derrota de Trump nas eleições para o Congresso dos EUA põe em xeque boom de data centers nos EUA - Trump não foi o único perdedor das eleições nos EUA: big techs e seus bilionários também saíram derrotados O leilão ocorre poucos dias após a vitória expressiva dos democratas nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos levantar dúvidas sobre o futuro de diversos projetos. Segundo pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto, o vendedor está recebendo propostas para doze empréstimos por meio de um processo conhecido como bids-wanted-in-competition (BWIC), segundo fontes. O processo funciona como uma concorrência entre interessados, que apresentam ofertas para adquirir os créditos. Projeto da OpenAI está na lista Entre os créditos à venda está uma participação de US$ 25 milhões em um financiamento destinado a um gigantesco complexo de data centers no Novo México, que integra o projeto Stargate, uma iniciativa conjunta de OpenAI, SoftBank e Oracle. Foi nesse local que a Oracle enviou ao desenvolvedor uma notificação alegando força maior (force majeure). O vendedor também pretende se desfazer de dívidas ligadas a operadoras como Vantage Data Centers e CyrusOne, disseram as fontes, que pediram anonimato porque as informações são privadas. As propostas pelos empréstimos devem ser apresentadas até 19 de novembro e precisam ter valor mínimo de US$ 10 milhões, acrescentaram. - Quem era Adam Robinson, magnata da tecnologia que morreu com a mulher e os filhos em queda de avião na Flórida O leilão, um dos primeiros do tipo a reunir exclusivamente dívidas ligadas a data centers, reflete o pessimismo mais amplo do mercado em relação à expansão da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial após as eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos. No Texas, onde diversos desenvolvedores atuam, o governador eleito democrata defendeu uma moratória imediata na construção desses empreendimentos. O índice Nasdaq 100 chegou a cair 6,4% na quinta-feira, em um recuo acentuado que prolonga semanas de preocupação entre investidores de Wall Street. Eles vêm reduzindo sua exposição ao setor de inteligência artificial diante de questionamentos sobre a capacidade de as receitas justificarem os investimentos extraordinariamente elevados. No mercado de títulos de alto rendimento, os chamados junk bonds (papéis de empresas com maior risco de crédito) ligados a desenvolvedores ou projetos de data centers, incluindo CoreWeave e Galaxy Digital, registraram algumas das maiores desvalorizações. Wall Street também enfrenta, de forma mais ampla, o risco de que o mercado de crédito esteja próximo do limite de sua capacidade de absorver dívidas relacionadas à inteligência artificial. Goldman Sachs e Apollo Global Management tentam distribuir a investidores partes do maior financiamento já estruturado para a compra de chips, ligado à SpaceX, informou a Bloomberg nesta semana. As instituições se comprometeram com a operação em outubro, antes da definição de seu preço, e agora enfrentam a possibilidade de o mercado se voltar contra o negócio.

artigo.texto: Egypt’s Battery Manufacturing Industry Targets EVs and Energy Storage as Investment Plans Advance – Expert View by Spherical Insights RELEASE DATE: Nov 2026 Author: Spherical Insights Request Free Sample Speak to Analyst Egypt has announced a series of battery-manufacturing and energy-storage projects in 2026, led by a BME–CATL plant targeting 1 GWh of annual capacity and a US$200 million Kemet–Cornex storage-battery facility planned at 5 GWh. Together they link electric mobility with renewable-energy storage. Egypt’s battery-manufacturing ambitions moved forward on 13 September 2026, when BME Battery Manufacturing and China’s CATL signed a contract, witnessed by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, to establish an electric-battery plant. The project carries an initial investment above EGP 2 billion, about US$39 million, and a first-phase capacity of 1 GWh a year, with batteries for heavy commercial vehicles as the initial focus. The agreement forms part of a broader series of developments announced in 2026. In January, Kemet Industries agreed to a US$200 million energy-storage battery facility with a Chinese technology partner. In June, AMEA Power and its partners signed contracts covering 1,500 MWh of storage projects and a separate factory designed to produce 3,000 MWh of storage systems annually. Sungrow broke ground on a storage-systems plant with planned annual capacity of 10 GWh in August, while Mansour Group and Tianneng signed a memorandum of understanding in September to explore battery-manufacturing opportunities. These developments connect two markets: batteries for electric mobility and battery systems for renewable-energy storage. The projects remain at different stages, ranging from signed agreements and construction starts to exploratory partnerships. What Is Driving Egypt’s Battery Manufacturing Push? Two policy priorities are supporting Egypt’s battery-manufacturing ambitions. In the automotive sector, the National Automotive Industry Development Programme aims to raise local value-added content to 60 per cent, strengthen domestic component production and attract international manufacturers. Industry Minister Khaled Hashem described the BME–CATL agreement as a step towards developing local battery capabilities as demand grows for electric vehicles and energy-storage technologies. In the power sector, battery storage can help integrate renewable electricity and improve grid flexibility. Egypt commissioned its first utility-scale battery energy-storage system, a 300 MWh facility connected to the 500 MW Abydos solar plant in Aswan, in July 2025. The government subsequently announced a target of 14,320 MWh of battery-storage capacity, with official reports citing both 2028 and 2029 as the deadline. AMEA Power’s two contracted projects total 1,500 MWh, equivalent to approximately 10.5 per cent of that target; the comparison reflects planned project capacity, not completed national progress. How Does the BME–CATL Partnership Support Local Production? BME (Battery Manufacturing Egypt) was established by commercial-vehicle manufacturer MCV and Auto D. The contract was signed by BME chairman Maged Wahib and CATL international investment director Luo Haining. CATL will provide battery technology licensing, production equipment and training, while BME builds and funds the plant and sources battery cells from CATL. The first phase targets 1 GWh a year for heavy commercial vehicles. A second phase would lift capacity to 5 GWh, five times the initial level, and extend into passenger-car batteries and storage systems for solar and wind power. The project targets 40 % local content, covering assembly, battery-management-system integration, thermal management and final system integration in Egypt, and it is planned to serve domestic and international markets. Prime Minister Madbouly said the government wants to accelerate implementation and move quickly to the next executive steps. Ready to lead the Egypt’s Battery Manufacturing Industry Targets EVs ? How Are Battery-Cell Manufacturing and Systems Assembly Developing? Egypt’s planned battery projects cover different stages of the battery value chain, from battery-pack assembly to cell manufacturing and stationary energy-storage systems. The BME–CATL partnership will use CATL-supplied cells for locally assembled battery packs, while Sungrow and AMEA Power are advancing storage-system manufacturing plans. The Kemet–Cornex agreement adds another stage through a proposed US$200 million battery-cell facility targeting an annual capacity of 5,000 MWh (5 GWh). The project also aims to use locally sourced materials and components while transferring manufacturing technology to Egypt. Announced in January 2026 during Electricity Minister Mahmoud Esmat’s visit to China, the Kemet agreement formed part of a broader US$700 million investment package, including a separate US$500 million solar-cell manufacturing complex involving GCL Group. Together, these projects reflect Egypt’s efforts to expand domestic renewable-energy equipment production, attract international investment and develop technical capabilities through technology partnerships. artigo.texto: A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) alertou o governo federal para o risco de não conseguir pagar todos os seus compromissos até o fim de 2026. A preocupação inclui R$ 30,76 milhões em notas fiscais pendentes relacionadas à aquisição do próprio data center, em Brasília, estrutura que sustenta sistemas digitais usados por cidadãos, operadoras e pela fiscalização do setor. O alerta foi revelado pela Folha de S.Paulo nesta terça-feira (3). O problema está relacionado a um bloqueio de R$ 51,83 milhões no orçamento da agência, que reduziu em aproximadamente 19% os recursos disponíveis para custeio e investimentos. Resposta rápida: a Anatel enfrenta um problema de recursos para honrar despesas, mas não há informação de desligamento do data center ou de interrupção nacional da internet e da telefonia por esse motivo. O risco relatado até agora diz respeito aos compromissos financeiros e à possibilidade de precisar reprogramar atividades e pagamentos. A falta de dinheiro da Anatel pode deixar o Brasil sem internet ou celular? Não há indicação de que isso vá acontecer. A Anatel regula e fiscaliza os serviços de telecomunicações; as redes que levam internet fixa, 4G e 5G ao consumidor são operadas pelas prestadoras. O data center citado na reportagem sustenta sistemas da própria agência, não toda a infraestrutura de conectividade do país. Por isso, é importante não confundir risco orçamentário com uma falha técnica confirmada. Até a divulgação das informações, não foi anunciado um apagão da internet, a paralisação das redes móveis ou o desligamento do centro de dados em decorrência dos pagamentos pendentes. Se as restrições financeiras persistirem, poderão surgir consequências para contratos e atividades administrativas e digitais da agência. Mas afirmar que um serviço específico ficará fora do ar exigiria uma confirmação que ainda não foi apresentada. O que faz o data center da Anatel e por que ele é importante? Um data center reúne equipamentos e sistemas que armazenam, processam e disponibilizam informações. No caso da Anatel, o centro de dados de Brasília dá suporte a serviços públicos digitais, a operações utilizadas pelas empresas de telecomunicações e a ferramentas de fiscalização, segundo a apuração da Folha. Entre as atividades relacionadas à infraestrutura de tecnologia da agência estão: - Atendimento ao consumidor: sistemas para registrar e acompanhar reclamações contra operadoras, como o Anatel Consumidor; - Atividades regulatórias: procedimentos digitais usados pelas prestadoras e no licenciamento de estações; - Fiscalização: ferramentas de trabalho e processamento de informações usadas para acompanhar o cumprimento das regras do setor. A existência de pagamentos pendentes não comprova, por si só, indisponibilidade desses serviços nem comprometimento de dados pessoais. Também não foi relatado um incidente de segurança ou vazamento decorrente do bloqueio de verba. Por que a Anatel tem R$ 30,76 milhões em pagamentos pendentes? O valor está associado à aquisição de um novo data center, contratada em dezembro de 2025 por R$ 44,95 milhões, com vigência até dezembro de 2030. O acordo abrange equipamentos, sistemas de gerenciamento, conectividade, implantação, migração, manutenção, suporte e garantia. Segundo a reportagem, os R$ 30,76 milhões ainda pendentes são classificados como restos a pagar, expressão usada para despesas de exercícios anteriores que continuam sem quitação. Isso não significa que todo o valor contratado tenha vencido de uma só vez, nem comprova que o fornecedor tenha suspendido o serviço. Na semana passada, o presidente da Anatel, Carlos Baigorri, pediu ao Ministério do Planejamento o desbloqueio de R$ 30 milhões. Em agosto, a agência havia solicitado antecipar R$ 23,3 milhões previstos para dezembro, mas o pedido não foi atendido pelo Tesouro Nacional, de acordo com a Folha. Quanto foi cortado do orçamento da Anatel em 2026? A Anatel atribui o aperto financeiro a um bloqueio de R$ 51,83 milhões, definido pelo governo federal em maio. A restrição atingiu o orçamento discricionário, destinado às despesas de funcionamento e a investimentos. Os dados expõem duas situações distintas: a redução do espaço orçamentário para custeio e investimentos e a necessidade de recursos financeiros para cumprir compromissos assumidos. A Anatel publica seu plano orçamentário no portal oficial, enquanto a restrição financeira relatada nesta semana foi detalhada pela Folha. O que dizem a Anatel e o Ministério da Fazenda? Questionada sobre o assunto, a Anatel informou à Folha que revisou contratos, projetos e despesas para reduzir o impacto do bloqueio e evitar custos adicionais, como multas e juros. A agência alertou, porém, que a continuidade das restrições poderá levar a novas mudanças na programação de gastos. O Ministério da Fazenda explicou que os limites de despesas integram a gestão do Orçamento federal e são reavaliados periodicamente. A pasta também afirmou que os pedidos de antecipação de recursos precisam considerar a capacidade de pagamento futura dos órgãos, para não comprometer os meses seguintes. Quando o governo vai decidir se libera mais dinheiro? A próxima avaliação das restrições orçamentárias está prevista para 24 de novembro de 2026, quando a Junta de Execução Orçamentária deverá reexaminar o espaço fiscal para eventual redução dos bloqueios. Isso não é garantia de liberação dos R$ 30 milhões pedidos pela Anatel. A decisão dependerá da avaliação do governo e das condições do Orçamento. Enquanto isso, a agência afirma estar ajustando suas despesas para reduzir impactos. Como reclamar de problemas com internet ou celular na Anatel? Para quem enfrenta um problema real de conexão ou cobrança, o procedimento continua sendo procurar primeiro a operadora, guardar o protocolo de atendimento e, se necessário, recorrer à ouvidoria da empresa. Se a questão não for resolvida adequadamente, o consumidor pode registrar uma reclamação na Anatel. - Entre em contato com a sua

artigo.texto: Vitória democrata na eleição de meio de mandato aumenta pressão sobre empresas e data centers de IA nos EUA Novo controle do Congresso abre espaço para exigências de transparência, mecanismos de interrupção de sistemas e regras mais duras para a infraestrutura tecnológica Atualizado A vitória democrata nas eleições legislativas dos Estados Unidos pode tornar mais difícil a vida das empresas de inteligência artificial. Com o controle da Câmara e do Senado, o partido terá mais poder para investigar as gigantes de tecnologia, impor exigências de transparência e dificultar a expansão de data centers. A mudança ocorre depois de quase dois anos de aproximação entre Donald Trump e executivos do setor. O governo acelerou licenças, incentivou a construção de infraestrutura e favoreceu compromissos voluntários das empresas em lugar de regras obrigatórias. Análise do VentureBeat destaca que a nova composição do Congresso deve concentrar a pressão em três frentes: segurança dos modelos, mecanismos capazes de interromper sistemas avançados e impactos dos data centers sobre energia, água e comunidades. Do modelo ao contrato Um dos projetos com apoio de democratas e republicanos obrigaria grandes desenvolvedores a divulgar informações sobre privacidade, proteção de crianças, riscos cibernéticos e possibilidades de perda de controle humano. As declarações seriam fiscalizadas pela Comissão Federal de Comércio, a FTC. Outra proposta exige que empresas mantenham mecanismos capazes de desligar modelos em determinadas situações. O texto alcançaria inicialmente companhias com pelo menos R$ 2,7 bilhões (US$ 500 milhões) em receita anual na atividade e sistemas cujo desenvolvimento custasse mais de R$ 549 milhões (US$ 100 milhões) em capacidade computacional. Para quem compra esses serviços, a discussão chega aos contratos. Uma eventual suspensão pode interromper aplicativos e processos internos dependentes de um único fornecedor, aumentando a importância de sistemas alternativos e procedimentos para retomar decisões humanas. As propostas mais restritivas, como a suspensão temporária do desenvolvimento de sistemas avançados, ainda não representam uma posição unificada dos democratas. Trump também poderá vetar projetos aprovados pelo Congresso. Data centers viram questão política A pressão mais imediata recai sobre os data centers. A resistência às instalações cresceu entre moradores preocupados com consumo de água, demanda por eletricidade e aumento das contas residenciais. Uma pesquisa citada pelo VentureBeat mostra que 60% dos americanos se sentiriam desconfortáveis com um novo data center em sua região. A rejeição alcançava 68% entre democratas e 54% entre republicanos. O tema ajudou candidatos que prometiam impor limites ao setor. No Texas, Gina Hinojosa venceu a eleição para governadora defendendo a suspensão de novos projetos até a aprovação de regras sobre água, energia e custos de infraestrutura. O estado concentra instalações bilionárias ligadas a OpenAI, Oracle, Microsoft, Google e Anthropic. O aumento das exigências pode atrasar projetos e encarecer a capacidade computacional necessária para treinar e operar sistemas de IA. A pressão também alcança empresas que usam a tecnologia para contratar trabalhadores, definir preços ou monitorar funcionários.

artigo.texto: *This content was translated by AI.View Original In the global electric vehicle battery market, Chinese battery manufacturers have surpassed a 50% share of overseas markets with a 56.4% stake, rapidly expanding their influence, while the overseas positions of South Korea's top three battery companies have significantly shrunk. According to energy research firm SNE Research, from the first quarter to the third quarter this year, the total installation volume of major Chinese battery companies in global markets excluding China reached 426.7 gigawatt-hours, a 24.7% increase year-on-year. artigo.texto: - CATL and BYD's combined share rises to 44.5%, while the 6 Chinese makers in the top 10 hold 56.4%. - Battery usage for South Korea's 3 major suppliers falls 13.5%, with their North American volumes roughly halving. CATL (HKEX: 3750) and BYD (HKEX: 1211) continued to gain share in the EV battery market outside China in the first 9 months of 2026, while South Korea's 3 major suppliers were weighed down by weak North American demand. Battery usage outside China reached 426.7 GWh during the period, up 24.7% year-on-year, according to data released Wednesday by South Korean research firm SNE Research. That outpaced global growth of 19.7%, as rising demand in Europe and Asia offset weakness in North America. The figures cover battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids and hybrids. The 6 Chinese companies in the top 10 increased their combined market share to 56.4% from 43.1% a year earlier, with CATL and BYD together accounting for 44.5%. CATL remained first with 143.7 GWh, up 46.7% year-on-year, as its market share rose to 33.7% from 28.6%. Its battery usage in Europe grew 35.4% to 96.8 GWh, while usage in Asia excluding China more than doubled to 27.1 GWh. CATL's Debrecen plant in Hungary began trial production on its first 2 production lines on September 22, a move SNE Research expects to strengthen its local supply capabilities for European customers. BYD held third place with 45.9 GWh, up 66.8% year-on-year, as its market share increased to 10.8% from 8.0%. BYD's batteries are mainly installed in its own vehicles. Its battery usage grew 68.8% in Europe, 41.0% in Asia and 135.7% in South America. By contrast, combined battery usage for LG Energy Solution (LGES), SK On and Samsung SDI fell 13.5% to 113.0 GWh, with their market share dropping to 26.5% from 38.2%. The decline for the 3 South Korean companies was concentrated in North America, where usage fell to 28.1 GWh from 56.1 GWh. Growth in Europe and Asia failed to offset that drop. LGES remained second with 69.8 GWh, but its battery usage fell 4.9% and its market share declined to 16.4% from 21.5%. SK On ranked fifth as its battery usage dropped 17.9% to 28.2 GWh and its share fell to 6.6% from 10.0%, with declines in both North America and Europe. Samsung SDI ranked seventh with 15.0 GWh, down 34.4%, the steepest decline among the top 10 suppliers. Its market share fell to 3.5% from 6.7%. Japan's Panasonic ranked fourth with 35.6 GWh, down 0.8%, while its share slipped to 8.4% from 10.5%. Its customer base remained heavily reliant on Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA). Second-tier Chinese suppliers also expanded rapidly. Gotion High-tech (SZSE: 002074) saw battery usage rise 153.8% to 17.6 GWh, overtaking Samsung SDI to rank sixth. Svolt Energy ranked eighth as its battery usage grew 102.3% to 13.1 GWh, while CALB (HKEX: 3931) ranked ninth with growth of 88.5% to 10.6 GWh. Eve Energy (SZSE: 300014) ranked tenth with 9.5 GWh, up 214.6%, the fastest growth among the top 10 suppliers. Meanwhile, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries increased their share of the market outside China to 27.7% from 15.8%, alongside the expansion of Chinese suppliers. SNE Research said growing adoption of LFP batteries in entry-level models in Europe was making price competitiveness a key consideration for automakers selecting battery suppliers. The research firm said North American EV demand had weakened following the end of tax credits, prompting South Korean suppliers to convert some production lines to batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) to tap demand beyond vehicles. In Europe, Chinese suppliers are ramping up production at local plants. SNE Research expects local production capabilities, price competitiveness and supply chain traceability to shape their market positions. Those traceability preparations include meeting Battery Passport requirements set to take effect in February 2027, adding a compliance dimension to competition among suppliers.

artigo.texto: The artificial intelligence data center boom hit a roadblock on election night, further complicating the tech industry's historic expansion plans. There were 41 local ballot measures in 10 states up for a vote on Tuesday that would place restrictions on the construction of data centers in different ways, according to Ballotpedia. Voters sided against data centers in each measure except one in Harwood, North Dakota, according to an analysis by Ballotpedia and additional results gathered by CNBC on Wednesday. The lone exception was Harwood, North Dakota, where voters rejected an added review of industrial projects, including data centers. Ohio alone accounted for more than half of the measures, with 21 on the ballot. The issue also played out at the top of the ticket, where Democrat Sherrod Brown ousted Republican Sen. Jon Husted after casting the incumbent as "the face of data centers." The Buckeye State, which was named America's Top State for Business in 2026 by CNBC, has become a key battleground for the issue. OpenAI announced in August that it secured 8 gigawatts of computing capacity at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, the largest planned AI data center campus in the world. The first phase of construction is slated to begin this year, and capacity is expected to come online in phases starting in 2028, according to the project's website. SoftBank and SB Energy are developing the Ohio data center campus in partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy. SoftBank is a major investor in OpenAI, and the two companies announced plans to invest $1 billion in SB Energy earlier this year. Nvidia is backstopping the project, which could cost more than $500 billion in total. Those plans could now run into resistance from the governor's mansion. Ohio's top office flipped blue on Tuesday, as Democrat Amy Acton, a physician, defeated Republican businessman Vivek Ramaswamy. Acton supports a "conditional moratorium" on data centers to ensure they cover 100% of utility costs and "exclusively build with union labor." Backlash at the ballot box Heading into the election, the AI trade was already faltering on Wall Street, with chipmakers, neoclouds and other data center-related companies selling off in October on concerns about rising interest rates and overspending. The hyperscalers — Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta — are each spending hundreds of billions of dollars a year on AI infrastructure to meet what they say is insatiable demand. All of those companies except Microsoft have turned cash flow negative in the process. Getting data center projects off the ground may have just gotten a lot harder. Communities in California, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Maine, New Jersey, Nevada and Wisconsin also went to the polls to weigh in on the issue, according to Ballotpedia, and data centers were a key motivating factor for voters in matters up and down the ballot. In a CNBC Voter Poll, 56% of voters said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their decision, with Democrats ranking the issue higher than Republicans. Democrats who campaigned on pausing or regulating new projects won key races in Ohio, Wisconsin, Georgia and Texas, which is on track to become the world's largest data center market by 2030. In one of the most significant results of the night for Democrats, Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Greg Abbott after blaming the Republican incumbent for the rapid buildout of data centers across Texas, saying he put the tech industry's interests ahead of local communities. The losses came despite record spending from Silicon Valley to shape the 2026 midterms, with the GOP boasting a commanding advantage among the election's biggest donors. According to a CNBC analysis of Federal Election Commission records, 14 of the 20 largest donor groups backed Republicans almost exclusively. Crypto, AI and online gambling interests poured in more than $377 million. Elon Musk, the cycle’s largest individual donor, spent at least $474 million, nearly half of it in Texas, and lost both of the state’s marquee races. It was a warning sign for the wave of tech companies and founders who left California for Texas in search of a friendlier business climate. "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," Musk wrote in a post on X. AI accountability Within hours of the polls closing, Democrats were already calling for AI executives to testify under oath. Among the first to seize on the results was Rep. Greg Casar, the Texas Democrat who chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus. "The House Democratic majority must make it a top priority to protect Americans' jobs, freedom, and lives from AI billionaires," Casar said in a statement after Democrats were projected to win the House. "AI company CEOs should be called to testify under oath." Casar also accused Republicans of being "bought and paid for by AI billionaires," arguing that voters had rejected that influence and warning Democrats to "hold them accountable instead of cashing their checks." He said the data center fight is only the beginning. "The revolt against data centers was one of the top issues of the 2026 election," he said. "And in a few years we will look back on it as just the early tremor of a much bigger AI earthquake upending American politics." Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the presumptive next chair of the House Oversight Committee, summed it up in two words: "Lawyer up." — CNBC's Ashley Capoot contributed to this article. artigo.texto: Oregon City adopts 120-day data center moratorium OREGON CITY, Ore. (KATU) — Oregon City on Wednesday night became the latest community in Oregon to place a moratorium on data center and battery energy storage systems development. City commissioners passed a 120-day moratorium that will block applications in five industrial and mixed-use zones while staff audit city codes and draft new regulations. There were no open applications or inquiries from data centers. ALSO SEE: 'Your Voice Your Vote': The two sides of the data center debate On Thursday morning, KATU spoke with Oregon City’s new Mayor-elect Adam Marl, who is currently a city commissioner, about the move. He said it is important for the city to get ahead of the issue, especially since it has some industrial land that it is looking to develop. “I think it could be easily seen for a data center to come in and provide the money to those property owners to get that large piece of property unified for something like a data center, and so I wanted to make sure that instead of being reactive like we've seen a lot of other cities who have been having to deal with this, I wanted us to be proactive in our approach to make sure that we have the regulations in place to protect our community,” Marl said. He said right now if a data center is proposed there would be no public input because city code “does not contemplate the existence of data centers.” There's also a countywide moratorium on data centers that went into effect on Oct. 22 in Clackamas County. It also lasts 120 days unless extended. SEE ALSO: Oregon already has 100+ data centers. Clackamas County wants to be ready if one comes next Gov. Tina Kotek has also directed the Department of Environmental Quality to not issue environmental permits for new or expanding data centers through July of next year.

artigo.texto: Duke Energy uses new solar, battery storage to prepare for electricity demand this winter ASHEVILLE, N.C. (WLOS) — As temperatures drop and people begin to turn up the heat, the demand for electricity is expected to rise across western North Carolina. Duke Energy said new technology at its Asheville Energy Complex is helping the company prepare for increased demand while working to keep electricity reliable and costs down for customers. Duke Energy recently brought a new solar and battery storage facility into service at its Asheville Energy Complex, marking another step in the site's transformation from a coal-fired power plant into a modern energy facility. The complex now uses a combination of natural gas, solar power, and battery storage to provide electricity to more than half a million homes across the region. The solar facility can generate enough electricity to power approximately 5,000 homes. With winter approaching, Duke Energy says energy storage will play an important role in meeting the region's energy needs. WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA EXPANDS SOLAR PROJECTS DESPITE MOUNTAIN TERRAIN CHALLENGES "Energy storage is a battery, so when you think about it, you can actually store energy in these. So if solar panels capture that energy from the sun, or if our combined cycle plant creates energy that we don't use, which happens a lot, we've got this excess energy the battery can store, and so we can use these batteries to deploy extra energy onto our grid in the winter season," said Logan Stewart with Duke Energy. Having multiple energy sources also gives Duke Energy more flexibility in how it generates electricity, particularly when fuel prices fluctuate. "We know that bills and costs are important to customers, and that's something customers are thinking about every day," Stewart said. "So having a diverse mix of energy resources for us to pick and choose what we use across our system, that ultimately drives down cost across the system and helps us operate more reliably, and that can drive down cost for customers." Beyond producing and storing electricity, Duke Energy said it is also using technology to help restore power more quickly when outages occur. One example is what the company calls smart self-healing technology. "For customers on a line that experiences an outage, it can reroute them to another line. We've integrated that across a lot of our grid on our main distribution lines." The technology is designed to limit the number of customers affected by certain outages and help restore electricity without requiring crews to manually switch power to another line. Duke Energy says the natural gas portion of the facility has reduced emissions by approximately 60% since 2020 and operates more efficiently than the former coal plant.

artigo.texto: Após a aprovação do Redata gerar uma euforia inicial com uma potencial onda de investimentos em data centers no País, a demora na regulamentação da lei está acendendo um sinal de alerta. Até o momento, nenhum novo projeto foi anunciado – e a consultoria Rystad Energy acaba de reduzir suas projeções para a instalação de data centers no Brasil em dois terços: de 21 gigawatts para 7 gigawatts até 2035, citando a falta de detalhes sobre os critérios para enquadramento no plano de incentivo fiscal. A proposta original do Governo para o Redata beneficiaria apenas data centers que contratassem 100% de sua energia com fontes renováveis. No Congresso, o texto foi alterado para contemplar projetos com fontes “de baixa emissão”. O Ministério de Minas e Energia defendeu publicamente que instalações movidas a gás pudessem ser enquadradas na lei, com essa nova redação. Mas o Ministério da Fazenda tem defendido limitações ou compensações para o uso do combustível fóssil, fontes a par do assunto disseram ao Brazil Journal. Um decreto presidencial detalhando as regras para enquadramento não foi publicado até o momento. "Ainda está pendente uma decisão do Poder Executivo sobre se a geração a gás natural se qualifica como energia de baixa emissão, além de detalhes críticos sobre métricas de eficiência energética, conteúdo local e verificações de compliance", disse a VP e chefe de Novas Energias da Rystad, Marina Domingues, num relatório. Em sua análise sobre o Redata, ela também citou a concorrência por espaço na rede elétrica para conexão dos data centers e potenciais limitações no acesso a energia firme como fatores que aumentam o risco para o desenvolvimento de projetos no País. A Rystad mapeou 20,8 GW em potenciais data centers previstos inicialmente para implantação no Brasil até 2035. Um número que despenca para uma estimativa de 6,7 GW quando ponderados todos os riscos. Nas contas da consultoria, mais de 10 GW em projetos são “de alto risco” e quase uma dezena de GW são de “médio risco”. Se considerados apenas os data centers de baixo risco, a capacidade do País ficaria praticamente estável na próxima década. Além da regulamentação, que depende do decreto presidencial, o Redata ainda deve exigir algumas definições no âmbito de agências reguladoras, de acordo com a Rystad. “Destravar investimentos em hyperscales exige que o Congresso e o Poder Executivo alinhem os prazos dos incentivos fiscais definidos em lei com definições regulatórias que ainda precisam ser escritas,” disse a consultoria.

artigo.texto: Energy storage provider Return has obtained €835m ($939m) in portfolio financing underwritten by Rabobank and Deutsche Bank to support the expansion of its battery storage capacity in Germany. The funding aims to bolster Return’s Virtual Flexibility Portfolio (VFP), which provides energy flexibility services to customers seeking to manage varying electricity demands and integrate renewable energy. Discover B2B Marketing That Performs Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms. Three German battery storage projects with a total capacity of 117MW are covered under the new financing arrangement. According to Return, if operated with four-hour batteries running two full cycles per day, these sites could deliver enough electricity annually to match the consumption of about 100,000 German households. The framework allows for the inclusion of additional eligible projects as they reach financial close. Return plans to install at least 1GW of battery storage annually in Germany starting from 2027. Annual investment is expected to range between €750m and €1.2bn, subject to market conditions. The company reports increasing customer demand for flexibility as Germany incorporates more wind and solar generation into its electricity system. The VFP model aggregates multiple battery storage assets into one virtual portfolio, giving customers access to scalable flexible capacity through a single platform. Commercial partners in Germany include ENGIE, which recently expanded its contracted flexibility with Return to 400MW, and Centrica Energy with an agreement for 100MW. Return also notes partnerships with energy companies such as Essent, Vattenfall, and Eneco in other European markets. Return chief financial officer Daniel Witvoet said: “As demand for energy flexibility grows, we need to scale not just our battery storage capacity, but also the way we finance it. “By bringing together physical infrastructure financing and our virtual flexibility model, we can expand more efficiently and respond to our customers’ evolving needs. “This is an important step towards our ambition to become a leading independent provider of energy flexibility in Germany.” Rabobank served as financial advisor on the financing, with Hogan Lovells Cadwalader and White & Case advising the borrowers and lenders respectively. Other involved advisors included Baker McKenzie, Baringa, DNV, EY, EY Parthenon, and Marsh.
