artigo.texto: A Riot Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:RIOT) reportou receita de US$ 181,4 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, um aumento de 1% em relação aos US$ 180,2 milhões do ano anterior, e anunciou um contrato de arrendamento de 15 anos para um centro de dados de inteligência artificial avaliado em aproximadamente US$ 28 bilhões. O acordo abrange todo o campus da empresa em Corsicana, no Texas, fornecendo 910 megawatts de capacidade crítica de TI para um laboratório de IA de ponta. A Riot espera que o contrato de locação gere uma receita média anual de aluguel de aproximadamente US$ 1,8 bilhão durante seu prazo inicial. Somando-se aos acordos existentes envolvendo a AMD e o mesmo cliente de IA em Rockdale, a Riot agora possui contratos que abrangem 1.151 megawatts e aproximadamente US$ 38 bilhões em receita prevista para data centers. Acordo com a Córsega expande negócios de infraestrutura de IA O contrato de arrendamento de Corsicana abrange uma área de 332 acres e inclui duas extensões opcionais de cinco anos, que poderiam aumentar o valor total do contrato para aproximadamente US$ 54 bilhões. Nos termos do contrato triple-net, a Riot fornecerá o terreno e a infraestrutura elétrica, enquanto o locatário instalará e operará seus equipamentos de informática e arcará com praticamente todas as despesas operacionais. A Riot estima uma margem de lucro operacional de aproximadamente 99% sob a estrutura de arrendamento, gerando uma receita operacional líquida anual média de cerca de US$ 1,8 bilhão. O projeto requer um investimento de capital de aproximadamente US$ 5,5 bilhões, o equivalente a US$ 6 milhões por megawatt de TI. A Riot espera financiar sua contribuição de infraestrutura de US$ 2 milhões por megawatt com recursos financeiros já existentes, e o restante do investimento será financiado por meio de reembolsos aos inquilinos e financiamento do projeto. A entrega está programada em três fases: 400 megawatts em setembro de 2027, 200 megawatts em janeiro de 2028 e 310 megawatts em julho de 2028. O diretor executivo Jason Les afirmou que o acordo representa uma expansão significativa das operações de infraestrutura da Riot. “Juntamente com nosso contrato com a AMD e o contrato de arrendamento assinado com o mesmo Frontier AI Lab em Rockdale no início deste ano, a Riot contratou 1.151 megawatts e aproximadamente US$ 38 bilhões em receita de data center”, disse Les. Ele acrescentou que a empresa espera que os acordos gerem mais de US$ 2 bilhões em receita operacional líquida anual média, uma vez totalmente implementados. Atualmente, a Riot não prevê emitir novas ações para financiar os projetos anunciados. A receita da mineração de Bitcoin cai apesar do aumento da produção A receita da Riot com mineração de Bitcoin caiu para US$ 116 milhões no terceiro trimestre, ante US$ 160,8 milhões no mesmo período do ano anterior, refletindo principalmente a queda no preço médio do Bitcoin. O preço médio do bitcoin durante o trimestre foi de US$ 70.855, em comparação com US$ 114.361 no mesmo período de 2025. Apesar da queda nos preços, a produção de bitcoin aumentou 16%, passando de 1.406 bitcoins no ano anterior para 1.637. O custo médio para minerar bitcoin, excluindo a depreciação, caiu de US$ 46.324 para US$ 39.265, devido à redução nos custos de eletricidade e ao aumento da produção. A Riot também recebeu US$ 24,7 milhões em créditos de redução de energia, o equivalente a aproximadamente US$ 15.067 por bitcoin minerado. Aumento da receita de data centers e engenharia A receita do Data Center atingiu US$ 18,4 milhões no trimestre, incluindo US$ 7,7 milhões em aluguel base, US$ 0,5 milhão em receita variável de arrendamento e US$ 10,2 milhões em reembolsos de adequação de espaços para inquilinos. Os resultados refletiram o primeiro trimestre completo de operações dos 25 megawatts de capacidade estabilizada entregues à AMD. A receita da área de engenharia aumentou para US$ 47 milhões, ante US$ 19,1 milhões no ano anterior, impulsionada pela demanda por equipamentos elétricos personalizados de operadores de data centers terceirizados. O crescimento nesses negócios compensou a queda na receita da mineração de Bitcoin, permitindo que a receita trimestral total aumentasse ligeiramente em relação ao ano anterior. A liquidez atinge US$ 950,2 milhões A Riot encerrou setembro com US$ 950,2 milhões em reservas combinadas de dinheiro e bitcoin. Isso incluiu US$ 748,2 milhões em dinheiro, dos quais US$ 79,2 milhões estavam restritos, e 2.418 bitcoins avaliados em aproximadamente US$ 202,0 milhões, usando o preço de mercado de 30 de setembro. Durante os primeiros nove meses de 2026, a Riot vendeu 20.264 bitcoins por aproximadamente US$ 1,5 bilhão, principalmente para financiar o desenvolvimento de data centers. A empresa também quitou integralmente e encerrou sua linha de crédito de US$ 200 milhões com a Coinbase, liberando todos os bitcoins anteriormente dados em garantia. Perspectivas para as plataformas da Riot Os resultados do terceiro trimestre da Riot destacaram sua crescente ênfase em infraestrutura de data centers de IA em larga escala, visto que a queda nos preços do bitcoin afetou a receita da mineração. O acordo com a Corsicana expande substancialmente o portfólio de projetos em desenvolvimento da empresa, com a administração projetando uma receita operacional líquida média anual superior a US$ 2 bilhões proveniente dos contratos combinados de data centers quando a operação estiver totalmente concluída. Os investidores acompanharão o financiamento do projeto, os marcos da construção e a entrega programada da capacidade de Corsicana a partir de setembro de 2027. A capacidade da empresa de executar seus projetos de infraestrutura, gerenciando simultaneamente suas necessidades de capital, será fundamental para seu desempenho financeiro a longo prazo. artigo.texto: Key Moments - Microsoft chose not to exercise an option to more than double its current Texas data center agreement with Nscale, according to a person familiar with the matter. - The decision was made several months before Nscale filed for its IPO in September and does not alter the existing Texas contract or the total disclosed contract value of about $103 billion. - Nscale has been in talks with other major customers for remaining Texas capacity and was previously reported to be discussing a roughly $45 billion AI compute deal with Anthropic. Microsoft Holds Line on Texas Capacity Microsoft will not move ahead with an option to significantly expand its existing arrangement with AI cloud provider Nscale for additional computing resources at a Texas data center, a person familiar with the situation said. The option would have allowed Microsoft to more than double the current agreement tied to the Texas facility. The Financial Times, which initially reported on the development on Thursday, said a possible extension of the arrangement could have been worth tens of billions of dollars to Nscale. According to the person, who requested anonymity due to the confidential nature of the discussions, the decision not to proceed with the expansion was reached several months ago, prior to Nscale’s initial public offering filing in September. The person added that the existing Texas contract between the two companies remains in place and unchanged. Existing Global AI Infrastructure Agreement Last year, Microsoft and Nscale entered into a broader agreement under which Nscale would deploy approximately 200,000 Nvidia AI chips as part of an expanded collaboration. That arrangement spans Microsoft-linked data centers across both Europe and the United States. Context: Data Center Projects and IPO Disclosures The move regarding the Texas option follows recent changes in another major project involving the two companies. In recent weeks, Microsoft withdrew from a separate plan to serve as the anchor customer for Nscale’s flagship data center development in Loughton, Essex. That decision came after power connection delays pushed the anticipated supply timeline for that site into the 2030s. In its IPO filing, Nscale stated that between September 2025 and April 2026 it signed statements of work with Microsoft valued at up to about $43.8 billion through December 2033, excluding any optional extensions. The person familiar with the matter said Microsoft’s choice not to exercise the Texas expansion option does not change Nscale’s previously disclosed total contract value of about $103 billion in the IPO filing. Texas Capacity and Customer Pipeline The same person indicated that Nscale was already engaged in talks with multiple large customers regarding the remaining capacity at the Texas data center, suggesting that the company has been seeking alternative buyers for that portion of its infrastructure. Other Strategic Discussions Separately, Reuters and other outlets reported last month that Nscale had been in negotiations to supply AI computing power to Claude-maker Anthropic in a new arrangement that could be worth about $45 billion. Company Responses Microsoft and Nscale did not respond to requests for comment made outside regular business hours.

artigo.texto: Russia is looking for innovative solutions to keep its digital infrastructure functioning amidst the ongoing war with Ukraine in wake of attacks targeting data centers. Rostelecom, a Russian telecommunication company, and Norilsk Nickel, a Russian nickel and palladium mining company, have reportedly started negotiations to build and operate data center facilities underground in order to protect digital services used by government and corporations, as the war continues. The Norilsk Nickel mines would provide safety from Ukraine drone attacks although the financial and technical details have not been disclosed to the public. In late October, Russia’s Digital Development Ministry issued recommendations to protect data centers against aerial attacks. The measures included moving critical infrastructure underground or into bunkers, citing Kommersant. Kemerovo Oblast governor Ilya Seredyuk proposed converting depleted open-pit mines and quarries for this purpose as reported by Russian news publication Meduza. Baxtel reported that Valeriy Ermakov, vice president, Rostelecom, during the RBC Tech forum, said, “A so-called ‘doomsday’ data center is a must-have, because backup is what allows any service provider to recover quickly.” On November 2, Russian President, Vladimir Putin, signed a decree requiring Russian data center operators to reserve 10 percent of their available space and capacity for potential government use. While allowing a special government commission, in consultation with the Federal Security Service, to authorize the use of foreign data centers. This is a notable shift from Russia’s Sovereign Internet Law, which restricted reliance on foreign cloud infrastructure as reported by The Moscow Times. This reflects growing Kremlin concerns about the vulnerability of domestic cloud infrastructure amid the war in Ukraine, as well as the challenges of maintaining Russia’s increasingly centralized and closed Internet, dominated by a handful of domestic technology companies. Rostelecom has outlined three levels of data center protection. The first involves maintaining backup facilities, the second distributes computing capacity across geographically separate sites, and the third places infrastructure underground, according to a company source cited by Vedomosti. Readers would recall that Ukraine and Russia have exchanged numerous attacks on their national digital infrastructure. Ukrainian drone attacks between October 12 and 14 significantly disrupted Russia’s technology sector, damaging three data centers operated by technology giant Yandex and affecting dozens of online services nationwide. Russia’s major technology company VKontakte (VK) also confirmed that its data center in Novosergievka had been struck by a drone, although its services remained operational. A separate attack targeted a data center under construction for Russian state-owned lender Sberbank in Balakovo, Saratov region. The attacks were believed to be retaliatory, following Russian strikes on Ukrainian data center infrastructure in mid-to-late September. These attacks damaged facilities used by internet providers UTELS and Pavutyna, as well as the BeMobile data center, which was hit by a Russian drone strike. The strikes also affected UCloud, a service provider operating from the facility, and De Novo, one of Ukraine’s largest commercial data center operators. Serhiy Petrenko, former head of Yandex Ukraine, has estimated that around 80 percent of Russia’s data centers are concentrated in Moscow and the surrounding region, leaving much of the country’s infrastructure within range of Ukrainian long-range drones as reported by The Kyiv Independent. What Russia is doing now, is similar to what Norway has already done. The Nordic country is home to two notable examples of underground data centers built within former mines. Green Mountain’s facility Rennesøy island and Lefdal Mine Datacenter in western Norway both repurpose underground mine infrastructure to house servers, taking advantage of the natural protection and stable conditions provided by the surrounding rock. Both facilities also use cold seawater from nearby fjords for cooling, reducing reliance on energy-intensive conventional cooling systems. Green Mountain draws water from approximately 100 meters below the surface, where temperatures remain close to 8 °C year-round, while Lefdal pumps cold fjord water directly into its cooling system. These approaches significantly reduce cooling energy consumption and improve overall energy efficiency. Russia also has several geographies that are blessed with a cold climate and thus low ambient temperatures, ideal for data centers.

artigo.texto: SpaceX's construction speed may outpace even Chinese rivals, with some facilities targeting four- to five-month builds. Google and Anthropic's computing agreements carry a combined annual contract value of $26 billion. Power remains a constraint, with SemiAnalysis estimating a possible shortfall exceeding 300MW at Colossus 2. Google spent nearly three decades building the data center infrastructure that supports its cloud and AI ambitions. SpaceX (SPCX) could match that cumulative capacity in just 18 months, according to SemiAnalysis. The Elon Musk-led company could reach 13 GW of data center capacity by 2027, with construction timelines that may outpace even Chinese competitors, the firm said. SPCX stock jumped nearly 4% on Tuesday to $141.31, logging its second straight session of gains. SpaceX's plan to reach 13 gigawatts of data center capacity in 2027 looks achievable, according to SemiAnalysis, which has identified more than 9GW across sites, including 3.6GW already under construction. The company raised its target from 10GW just two months after skeptics questioned whether the earlier plan was possible, the firm said. "We now believe that SpaceX may be the fastest datacenter builder in the world, even more so than Chinese peers," SemiAnalysis said. The projected buildout could match the capacity Google accumulated over nearly three decades in just 18 months. "This would be the largest amount of datacenter capacity ever built by any one company in that timeframe, roughly equivalent to all of Google's datacenter capacity from 1999-2026 in just 1.5 years," the analysts said. In August, SemiAnalysis said SpaceX's 10GW plan could support $300 billion in annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027, assuming half its additional computing capacity was rented to outside customers. SpaceX Races To Break Its Own Records SemiAnalysis said MiniHard, an AI data center expansion in SpaceX's Colossus 2 complex, took about five months to build. Gun Range, another facility on a former police training site in Southaven, Mississippi, is targeting four months. "To our knowledge, this would be the fastest greenfield datacenter ever built at scale," the analysts said, referring to a facility built from scratch. "While most are fighting for 8-12-month build times, SpaceX has cut them in half." Project SPAM could move even faster. Construction began last month, with its first computing systems targeted to start running in December, and potentially beating the first Colossus II deployment's 91-day timeline. SpaceX's initial Colossus cluster, a group of connected AI processors, took 122 days to come online. Starbase And Tesla Fuel The Buildout SemiAnalysis said SpaceX is adapting its Starbase rocket campus in Texas for two data centers that could support well over 1GW. Construction progressed from ground clearing in August to building frames and roofs simultaneously by September. "These are multiple construction processes performed simultaneously, a visual representation of speed," the analysts said. The firm also sees a possible data center serving outside customers at Terafab, Musk's proposed Texas chip factory. Meanwhile, Tesla may help speed construction by supplying prefabricated mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems. "If SpaceX and Tesla can manage their global supply chains appropriately, their partnership can easily construct GWs with far fewer constraints than others," the analysts said. "Tesla will likely become more than a BESS merchant to SpaceX soon," they added, referring to battery storage systems. Google And Anthropic Drive Cloud Push SpaceX expanded into AI through its acquisition of xAI in February and its Colossus computing infrastructure. Anthropic agreed in May to use all of Colossus 1's capacity, covering more than 300 megawatts and 220,000 Nvidia GPUs. Google separately agreed to access about 110,000 GPUs, with payments scheduled at $920 million monthly from October 2026 through June 2029. The two agreements carry a combined annual contract value of $26 billion. Power Supply Tests SpaceX's AI Ambitions However, SemiAnalysis flagged a power supply hurdle. The firm tracks more than 8GW of likely generation capacity supplying SpaceX directly, compared with more than 9GW of upcoming data center capacity. "These sites now build so fast that the power supply is often identified mid-flight," the analysts said. At Colossus 2, 5.9 gigawatt-hours of battery storage, gas generation and a planned grid connection could help offset restrictions on turbine capacity. Even then, SemiAnalysis estimates a possible power shortfall exceeding 300MW. More efficient designs, adjustments to computing workloads and battery storage could help close the gap. "If the datacenters are designed right (and our IT MW assumptions are correct), this could work," the analysts said, referring to their estimates of computing equipment's power needs. artigo.texto: Who Pays for Carbon? Inside The New Charter Party Battleground When a ship completes a voyage, the total emissions are calculated, and under the EU ETS, the ship needs to surrender allowances. The allowances have a price tag that needs to be paid, but who pays the cost? The Owner or the Charterer? Unlike intensity regimes such as FuelEU Maritime, where vessels aim to meet a performance-based target, the ETS is a strict cap-and-trade system: there is no baseline to comply with, only allowances that must be purchased and surrendered for every tonne emitted. Even when operational data is undisputed and emissions are fully reported, a vessel can swiftly become embroiled in a contractual standoff over who actually pays for those surrendered allowances. This friction comes directly from practical enforceability and cost-allocation gaps present in charterparty terms. With the UK ETS expanding to maritime transport alongside the EU ETS framework, operators face overlapping surrender timetables and duplicate administrative burdens. Owners and charterers must ensure their charterparty agreements explicitly allocate carbon liability, reporting obligations, and financial settlement mechanisms across both regimes. The BIMCO Solution In 2022, BIMCO introduced the commercial mechanism for the ETS allowance clause for time charter parties by publishing the Emission Trading Scheme Allowances (ETSA) Clause for Time Charter Parties. The clause is based on the “polluter-pays” principle. Because the time charterer directs the commercial operation of the vessel and determines its fuel consumption, the clause makes the charterer responsible to provide and pay for the emission allowances generated during the charter period. Hence, the owner calculates the previous month’s emissions based on consumption data and notifies the charterer. The charterer then has to transfer the required quantity of allowances into the owner’s nominated account by an agreed monthly deadline, enabling the owner or administering entity to surrender them for compliance. Additionally, the clause provides legal remedies if the charterer fails to transfer the allowances on time. In such a situation, the shipowner can let go of the contractual obligations including refusing voyage orders, while keeping the vessel on hire until the outstanding allowances are transferred. However, maritime law firms and leading P&I clubs, including NorthStandard and Gard, have frequently cautioned that the clause is not a frictionless “set and forget” remedy. In practice, a single vessel often sits within a long charter chain, involving time charterers, sub-charterers, and voyage fixtures across different jurisdictions. If an intermediary in the chain defaults or delays transferring allowances, the owner cannot absorb the cash shortfall, given the regulatory deadlines. Furthermore, exercising the right to withhold performance under English-law governed charters can lead to off-hire and cargo-claim counterarguments from third-party bill of lading holders. UK ETS Add Another Layer To Carbon Cost Allocation As part of the UK government’s statutory Net Zero strategy, the UK ETS expanded to commercial cargo and passenger ships of 5,000 GT and above on 1 July 2026, with offshore vessels joining on 1 January 2027. Crucially, while the EU initially regulated only carbon dioxide, the UK agenda captures carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide from day one. The UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) thus introduces another layer of operational and financial complexity regarding payment for emissions caused while the ship was chartered out. The registered owner remains strictly liable under statutory law for complying with the scheme, unless that statutory duty has been formally delegated to the ISM/DOC manager. Under the charterparty, however, commercial liability is routinely passed to the charterer, and this may mean payments to the owner or allocation of allowances. It is necessary to indicate in the contract whether the provisions of EU ETS, UK ETS or both are included, how emissions are calculated, whose responsibility is to provide data, and how the cost is to be paid. There should be an agreement about what to do when the vessel is delivered before the calculation of the emissions cost is done. The GB–Northern Ireland issue There is a special provision in the UK ETS about voyages from Great Britain to Northern Ireland, which applies a 50% deduction to the vessel’s allowance surrender obligation. At first glance, this looks just like the EU ETS rule, which charges 50% on voyages in and out of the bloc. But the reasoning is completely different. The EU charges 50% on international trips to share coverage with other countries. A voyage between Great Britain and Northern Ireland, however, is a domestic UK trip that would normally be taxed at 100%. The UK cut this to 50% to ensure carbon-pricing PARITY between NI-GB and RoI-GB routes. This creates an easy trap in charter agreements. Standard contracts often talk broadly about “emissions charges” without defining how this discount applies. If the clause does not state whether the charterer pays for the full carbon emitted or only the discounted 50% actually handed over to regulators, a payment dispute is almost guaranteed. The BIMCO ETS – Emission Trading Scheme Allowances Clause for Time Charter Parties 2022 provides a general framework for the discussion. Still, it may be necessary to check if the wording applies to the UK ETS rules for their particular vessel or voyages, and how to accommodate the UK specifics. In practice, owners, managers and charterers can use dedicated solutions such as OceanScore’s Compliance Manager to calculate emissions liabilities, allocate costs between counterparties and manage the associated compliance workflows across EU ETS and UK ETS. artigo.texto: PSEG Power and Constellation Energy are planning a 200-MW uprate at their jointly owned Salem nuclear power plant in southern New Jersey, according to an earnings presentation by Public Service Enterprise Group, PSEG Power’s parent company. Salem’s current installed capacity is 2,280 MW. PSEG Power would have a 112-MW share of the uprate and Constellation would own the remainder, which would support a recently announced nuclear-focused power purchase agreement with Google. PSEG Power’s roughly 3,760-MW nuclear fleet ran at a 95.5% capacity factor in the third quarter, up from 92.4% in the same period last year, according to the presentation. However, there has been a snag at the Salem plant, PSEG said Monday in its quarterly filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. During a scheduled refueling outage at Salem 1, a visual inspection last month revealed that the thermal shield inside the reactor vessel is degraded, according to the filing. “We have initiated further testing, which is ongoing and is expected to extend the refueling outage,” PSEG said. “The impact of the outage on Salem 1 will depend on the timing and results of the inspection and necessary repairs.” Meanwhile, PSEG continues to explore potential deals with data center developers centered around PSEG Power’s roughly 3.8-GW nuclear fleet, according to Ralph LaRossa, PSEG chair, president and CEO. “PSEG Power is continuing to develop terms with large load entities for contracting arrangements involving existing nuclear production, future nuclear upgrades and other generation opportunities, similar to recently announced power purchase agreements in the PJM region and specifically in New Jersey,” he said during the earnings call. FERC’s recent decision to reject key portions of the PJM Interconnection proposed plan for interconnection data centers and other large loads “reinforces that the focus has shifted to the states to address retail curtailment and cost issues associated with large load customers,” LaRossa said. Public Service Electric and Gas Co., a PSEG utility, is working with the administration of New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill, D, and the state’s utility regulators to limit electric cost increases for consumers and consider new utility regulatory models, according to LaRossa. PSE&G, for example, plans to ask the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities to approve a plan for recovering the costs for investments made since its last distribution rate case, LaRossa said. “Our filing … is all about staying aligned with the governor's goals to keep rates flat for as long as possible,” he said. The utility expects to file the proposal by the end of the year, PSEG said in its SEC filing. Meanwhile, the BPU’s study on modernizing New Jersey's electric utility business model is now in its second phase, LaRossa noted. “This initiative is focusing on cost discipline, financing modernization, targeted incentives and shared savings and staged performance-based ratemaking,” he said. Those and other options mentioned in the Phase 1 report, such as multi-year rate plans, performance-based rates, performance incentive metrics, earnings sharing mechanisms, decoupling and shared saving mechanisms, provide “constructive paths to strengthen the connection between customer value, cost accountability and timely recovery of prudent investment,” LaRossa said. PSE&G may have opportunities to invest in solar and grid readiness for distributed resources, but the extent of it could hinge on the state allowing utilities to own generating assets, according to LaRossa. “I think the policy is not yet certain here in New Jersey as to whether or not it will move in a regulated direction or stay solely competitive,” he said. On the financial front, PSEG’s third-quarter income fell to $376 million, or 76 cents/share, down from $622 million, or $1.25/share a year ago, mainly on mark-to-market losses at PSEG Power, the Newark, New Jersey-based company said in its SEC filing. Third-quarter revenue slipped to $3 billion from $3.2 billion in the same period last year.

artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data Held Approximately $50.6 Million of Bitcoin, Cash and Restricted Cash as of November 1, 2026 LAS VEGAS , Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that, as of November 1, 2026, it held 211.4639 Bitcoin representing an aggregate value of approximately $16.5 million based on the Bitcoin closing price of $78,248. Additionally, the Company held approximately $34.1 million in cash and restricted cash. The Company continues to focus on disciplined capital allocation, managing its financial resources and advancing development of its Michigan AI data center to meet its contractual commitments. "Hyperscale Data is making remarkable progress toward energizing the initial 10 megawatts of critical IT capacity at our Michigan AI data center, with energization targeted for December 2026. This represents an important step toward delivering on our recently announced master services agreement," said Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data. "Our focus remains on execution, responsible capital management and building long-term value for our stockholders." For more information on Hyperscale Data and its subsidiaries, Hyperscale Data recommends that stockholders, investors and any other interested parties read Hyperscale Data's public filings and press releases available under the Investor Relations section at hyperscaledata.com or available at www.sec.gov. About Hyperscale Data, Inc. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center at which it offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Another of Hyperscale Data's wholly owned subsidiaries, Ault Capital Group, Inc. ("ACG"), is a hybrid private equity firm and operating company that acquires, finances, builds and actively manages businesses across financial services, digital assets, industrial services, hospitality, defense technologies and other sectors. Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the "Divestiture") to occur in 2027. Upon the occurrence of the Divestiture, the Company would be an owner and operator of data centers to support high-performance computing services, as well as a holder of the digital assets and the third wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Omnipresent Robotics, LLC. Until the Divestiture occurs, the Company will continue to provide, through ACG and its wholly and majority-owned subsidiaries and strategic investments, mission-critical products that support a diverse range of industries, including an AI software platform, equipment rental services, defense/aerospace, industrial, automotive and hotel operations. In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary. Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141. On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the "Series F Preferred Stock") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis. The Divestiture will occur through the voluntary exchange of the Series F Preferred Stock for shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock of ACG (collectively, the "ACG Shares"). The Company reminds its stockholders that only those holders of the Series F Preferred Stock who agree to surrender such shares, and do not properly withdraw such surrender, in the exchange offer through which the Divestiture will occur, will be entitled to receive the ACG Shares and consequently be shareholders of ACG upon the occurrence of the Divestiture. artigo.texto: Parcerias Drax firma parceria para centro de dados de IA em local de geração de energia no norte de Yorkshire Adicione Unite.AI às suas fontes preferidas no Google A Drax anunciou, em 3 de novembro de 2026, que havia assinado um acordo com a Brookfield e a Radiant para desenvolver, entregar e operar capacidade para centros de dados de IA na central elétrica de Drax, no norte de Yorkshire, com a meta de superar 1 GW em três fases. A Brookfield estima que o investimento potencial total, incluindo chips semicondutores, possa ultrapassar £ 20 bilhões, dos quais £ 2,5 bilhões iniciais farão parte da Fase 1. O capital de investimento e as capacidades operacionais serão fornecidos por meio da joint venture de infraestrutura de IA Brookfield-Qai. A infraestrutura de energia existente é a base do plano A proposta se apoia na infraestrutura já existente na central elétrica. A propriedade ocupa mais de 1.000 acres e dispõe de acesso à rede elétrica de aproximadamente 4 GW, geração despachável ativa de 2,6 GW e sistemas de refrigeração. A proximidade da rede de fibra do Reino Unido acrescenta outro requisito ao desenvolvimento de computação em larga escala, além do terreno e da infraestrutura elétrica. A primeira fase prevê até 100 MW de capacidade computacional e o início das operações comerciais a partir do primeiro trimestre de 2028. Ela utilizaria a infraestrutura existente para importar energia diretamente da rede, com a Drax gerenciando esse fornecimento. O modelo de fornecimento de energia muda na Fase 2, que tem como objetivo acrescentar 500 MW de capacidade entre 2028 e 2031. A geração existente da Drax forneceria energia diretamente ao centro de dados, 24 horas por dia, nos termos de um contrato de compra de energia de longo prazo. Esse arranjo atrás do medidor estaria sujeito às autorizações necessárias. A Fase 3 prevê capacidade adicional após 2031, seguindo a mesma abordagem. Essa estrutura em fases separa o desenvolvimento inicial, conectado à rede, do modelo posterior de fornecimento direto de energia. Também coloca a geração existente da central no centro da expansão proposta, em vez de tratar o projeto simplesmente como um centro de dados construído ao lado de uma usina. A construção depende de clientes e aprovações A Radiant, plataforma de infraestrutura de IA da Brookfield com sede no Reino Unido, liderará o projeto, o relacionamento com clientes e a comercialização. A empresa buscará compromissos de clientes-âncora antes do início da construção, enquanto a Drax ficará à frente das questões relacionadas ao terreno, à integração de energia e ao planejamento. A Fase 1 continua condicionada à aprovação do planejamento, às aprovações regulatórias e de conexão à rede por parte do governo e das agências competentes, à contratação de um inquilino aceitável, à celebração de acordos comerciais e a uma decisão final de investimento de cada parte. Uma solicitação de aprovação de planejamento está sendo preparada, e espera-se que a consulta pública comece em novembro de 2026. Os parceiros esperam criar um fundo voluntário de benefícios para a comunidade, desenvolvido em conjunto com as comunidades do entorno do local. O fundo seria separado das obrigações de planejamento e adicional a elas, bem como às iniciativas comunitárias já existentes da Drax. Mahdi Yahya, diretor-executivo da Radiant, afirmou no comunicado público dos parceiros que o projeto proporcionaria a “pesquisadores, startups e empresas britânicas acesso local a recursos computacionais de ponta”. Contrato de energia e financiamento moldam a expansão As fases posteriores se relacionam com os acordos existentes da Drax para geração de energia a partir de biomassa. Em novembro de 2025, a Drax assinou com o governo do Reino Unido um contrato por diferença que abrange aproximadamente 6 TWh de geração anual de energia a partir de biomassa, de abril de 2027 a março de 2031. Esse acordo inclui um mecanismo que permite à Drax solicitar até 500 MW para uso em centros de dados durante o período do contrato. Esse uso dependeria de um acordo com o governo do Reino Unido e a Low Carbon Contracts Company, levando em conta a relação custo-benefício para os consumidores, a segurança energética e a sustentabilidade. A Drax afirmou que permaneceriam inalteradas as funções da central de apoiar a segurança do abastecimento, fornecer energia despachável de baixo carbono e prestar serviços essenciais ao sistema. O veículo de financiamento foi criado antes do acordo de Yorkshire. A Brookfield e a Qai anunciaram sua joint venture de US$ 20 bilhões em 9 de dezembro de 2025, com o objetivo de investir em infraestrutura de IA no Catar e em mercados internacionais selecionados, e ambos os parceiros contribuiriam com capital e experiência operacional. A Qai é uma subsidiária da Qatar Investment Authority. O acordo conecta, portanto, uma propriedade de geração de energia consolidada a uma plataforma dedicada ao desenvolvimento de IA e a um veículo de investimento já existente. O desafio imediato é executar a primeira fase: garantir o inquilino, obter as aprovações e tomar as decisões finais de investimento necessárias. Qualquer expansão maior também terá de estar alinhada aos compromissos de geração da Drax e obter as autorizações exigidas.

artigo.texto: M&A Houston battery tech startup FlowCellutions acquired by Katy energy co. Katy-based TerraFlow Energy, an energy storage and infrastructure company, has acquired Houston-based battery technology startup FlowCellutions. Financial terms weren’t disclosed. FlowCellutions still operates under its established name, but with the tagline “A TerraFlow Energy Company.” Becca Segel, founder and CEO of FlowCellutions, now runs the business as its president. FlowCellutions specializes in electrochemical sensing, diagnostics, analytics, and testing that offer insights into battery chemistry, charging capabilities, and system performance. “FlowCellutions has always been focused on developing better ways to understand what is happening inside a flow battery and using that information to improve how these systems perform,” Segal said in a press release. “Joining TerraFlow gives us the opportunity to apply that work at a much larger scale while continuing to build the capabilities and expertise that make FlowCellutions unique.” The FlowCellutions platform supports data centers and other heavy users of power. It’s designed to help reduce operating costs, prevent failures and costly downtime, and extend battery lifetime from about seven years to more than 30 years. Segel founded the company in 2022. A member of Greentown Labs, the company raised more than $2 million in non-dilutive funding and received $1.5 million in National Science Foundation funding earlier this year. FlowCellutions is one of five finalists in the Energy Transition Business category of InnovationMap’s 2026 Houston Innovation Awards. “FlowCellutions brings a depth of scientific and technical expertise that fits naturally with where TerraFlow is going,” Jon Parrella, CEO of TerraFlow, said in the release. “As we move from developing these systems to deploying them at commercial scale, understanding performance at a deeper level matters,” he said. “Bringing FlowCellutions into TerraFlow strengthens that capability and gives both teams more opportunity to advance the technology.”TerraFlow, founded in 2024, develops long-duration energy storage and power infrastructure for data centers, industrial facilities, utilities and other large power consumers. --- This article originally appeared on EnergyCapitalHTX.com.

artigo.texto: 6K Receives Conditional Commitment for $250 Million Loan from the U.S. Department of War to Support Domestic Cathode Active Material Expansion Conditional financing intended to support construction of 6K's PlusCAM™ production facility in Jackson, Tennessee, strengthening the U.S. battery supply chain NORTH ANDOVER, Mass. , Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 6K Inc., today announced that the United States Department of War, through its Office of Strategic Capital, has provided the company with a conditional loan commitment of up to $250 million intended to support the construction and development of a domestic cathode materials production facility in Jackson, Tennessee. The transaction represents an important step toward establishing a secure, resilient, and scalable domestic supply of metal oxide cathode materials, a critical component of high energy density lithium-ion batteries used in defense, drones, mobility, energy storage, robotics, and other advanced technologies. Today, the United States remains heavily dependent on foreign produced cathode materials. This condition creates significant supply-chain risk for industries that are increasingly reliant on advanced batteries and exposes U.S. manufacturers to potential trade restrictions, geopolitical disruption, and foreign control of strategically important materials. By establishing cost-competitive, commercial-scale cathode production in Tennessee, 6K intends to help address that vulnerability. Using proprietary advanced microwave plasma technology invented in the US and commercially proven by 6K Additive to produce critical metal powders for the defense industrial base, 6K provides a differentiated approach to producing battery materials. 6K's UniMelt® plasma process fundamentally transforms metal oxide cathode synthesis by enabling production without the use of traditional precursors (pCAM). The UniMelt process enables a closed loop manufacturing facility that converts metal or other alternative feedstocks to cathode with minimal waste generation, while also removing dependence on raw materials sourced from Foreign Entities of Concern (FEOCs). "Building a resilient and competitive U.S. battery supply chain requires proven technologies that are scalable and fundamentally designed to overcome existing manufacturing and supply chain constraints," said Saurabh Ullal, CEO of 6K. "This long-term conditional loan commitment will be instrumental in enabling 6K's ability to produce secure, domestically manufactured cathode. The Jackson facility will bring critical manufacturing capacity to the United States while supporting over 200 high-quality jobs and strengthening industries that are essential to our economic and national security." Finalization of the financing is contingent upon substantial conditions, including receipt of authorizations from relevant governmental authorities and the availability of appropriations, completion of due diligence to the satisfaction of the Department of War, along with 6K satisfying a comprehensive set of financial, legal, technical, regulatory, and other conditions outlined by the Department of War before financing is finalized and any funds are disbursed. 6K press releases are available here: https://www.6kinc.com/about/news/ About 6K 6K Inc. produces and innovates UniMelt® microwave plasma technology for the localized production of critical materials. 6K's UniMelt® technology is applied across a vast range of markets, from additive manufacturing (6K Additive) and essential battery materials (6K Energy) to future growth sectors. UniMelt® plasma creates a path for true sustainability, reducing carbon emissions, lowering energy use, and utilizing recycled content to create a circular economy—all while reducing conversion cost and providing a secure, domestic supply chain. UniMelt® is industrially operational, at scale, today, with our Headquarters and Battery Center of Excellence (North Andover, MA), and full-scale PlusCAM™ battery material manufacturing plant (Jackson, Tennessee). For more information, visit www.6Kinc.com . artigo.texto: As ações da Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR) subiram aproximadamente 4% nas negociações pré-mercado na quinta-feira, após a empresa de fotônica divulgar receita e lucros maiores no primeiro trimestre, impulsionados pelo aumento da demanda por produtos de conectividade óptica usados em centros de dados de inteligência artificial. No trimestre encerrado em 30 de setembro, a Coherent reportou lucro ajustado de US$ 2,09 por ação, um aumento de 80% em relação aos US$ 1,16 do mesmo período do ano anterior. A receita cresceu 49,9%, atingindo US$ 2,37 bilhões, enquanto o lucro líquido ajustado aumentou 91%, para US$ 422 milhões. O segmento de data centers e comunicações da empresa foi responsável pela maior parte do crescimento da receita, refletindo o aumento da demanda por infraestrutura de redes ópticas à medida que a capacidade de computação de IA se expande. A receita de data centers e comunicações aumentou 79% A Coherent reportou uma receita de US$ 1,95 bilhão em seu segmento de data centers e comunicações, representando um aumento de 79% em comparação com o ano anterior. O crescimento refletiu a demanda por tecnologias de conectividade óptica usadas para transmitir dados entre sistemas de computação na infraestrutura de IA. Em comparação, a receita do segmento industrial da empresa caiu 14,8%, para US$ 418,6 milhões. O diretor executivo, Jim Anderson, destacou a transição de conexões baseadas em cobre para tecnologia óptica em centros de dados de IA como um fator importante para impulsionar a demanda. À medida que os sistemas de computação de IA exigem maior largura de banda e eficiência energética, a conectividade óptica está se tornando um componente cada vez mais importante da infraestrutura de data centers. A Coherent afirmou que seus negócios consolidados continuaram a se expandir, enquanto novas áreas de crescimento começaram a contribuir para a receita. As margens brutas melhoram com o aumento do lucro operacional ajustado A Coherent reportou melhorias na rentabilidade, tanto reportada quanto ajustada, durante o trimestre. A margem bruta, segundo os princípios contábeis geralmente aceitos (GAAP), aumentou 254 pontos base em relação ao ano anterior, atingindo 39,1%. A margem bruta ajustada aumentou 184 pontos base, atingindo 40,6%. O lucro operacional ajustado aumentou 78,1% em relação ao ano anterior, atingindo US$ 550,3 milhões, refletindo o aumento da receita e a melhoria da rentabilidade operacional. O lucro líquido ajustado atingiu US$ 422 milhões, um aumento de 91% em relação ao trimestre correspondente do ano passado. A melhoria das margens foi acompanhada pelo aumento nas vendas de produtos de conectividade óptica, embora a empresa continue investindo em capacidade de produção para atender à demanda prevista. Os analistas da Stifel identificaram os compromissos dos clientes e os potenciais benefícios financeiros da substituição de componentes a laser de origem externa por tecnologia produzida internamente como fatores relevantes para a rentabilidade futura. “Em nossa opinião, os compromissos dos clientes estão cada vez mais impulsionando o investimento em capacidade, enquanto a substituição interna de lasers continua sendo uma alavanca de margem ainda não explorada. A próxima questão é a rapidez com que esses compromissos se convertem em receita e fluxo de caixa com margens mais altas”, escreveram os analistas. Os comentários destacaram a importância de converter a demanda do cliente em receita adicional, melhorias de margem e geração de caixa. A Coherent prevê receita de até US$ 2,75 bilhões no segundo trimestre Para o segundo trimestre, a Coherent projetou uma receita entre US$ 2,55 bilhões e US$ 2,75 bilhões. A empresa também previu lucros ajustados de US$ 2,28 a US$ 2,48 por ação. Ambas as faixas representam aumentos em relação aos resultados do primeiro trimestre, que foram de US$ 2,37 bilhões em receita e US$ 2,09 em lucro ajustado por ação. A perspectiva reflete as expectativas da administração quanto à demanda contínua nos principais mercados de crescimento da empresa, particularmente em produtos que suportam a conectividade de data centers com IA. A Coherent também prevê que o crescimento da receita pro forma para o ano fiscal de 2027 ultrapasse 60%. A empresa atribuiu essa perspectiva à demanda prevista por suas tecnologias em mercados em expansão. A empresa almeja faturar US$ 3 bilhões por trimestre no ano fiscal de 2027 A Coherent delineou marcos adicionais de receita como parte de suas expectativas financeiras de longo prazo. A empresa espera registrar seu primeiro trimestre com receita de US$ 3 bilhões até o final do ano fiscal de 2027. A empresa também prevê atingir uma receita trimestral de US$ 4 bilhões pela primeira vez durante o ano fiscal de 2028. Essas metas refletem as expectativas de expansão contínua da demanda por redes ópticas e outros produtos em seus mercados em crescimento. A Coherent também aumentou sua meta de margem bruta ajustada de longo prazo. A empresa agora espera que a margem bruta ajustada ultrapasse 45% antes do final de 2028, em comparação com os 40,6% registrados no último trimestre. Atingir essas metas dependerá do crescimento da receita, da capacidade de produção, da variedade de produtos e da capacidade da empresa de gerenciar os custos de fabricação. Analistas avaliam a demanda e o valor da infraestrutura de IA Os analistas da B. artigo.texto: A wave of Democratic candidates across the country—and notably in Texas, a national data center hot spot and home to Elon Musk’s SpaceX—won their state and congressional races on Tuesday, including many candidates who voiced opposition to the data center industry. The results have sent some corners of the tech industry looking to the heavens for answers. In recent hours, data center enthusiasts have proclaimed on social media that they’re still “bullish” on building data centers—just not necessarily in Texas, or even on Earth at all. Instead, they say, it’s time to focus on data centers in space. Elon Musk—who spent more than $400 million of his fortune supporting Republican candidates who all went on to lose their midterms races—has been among those leading the charge. “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk posted on X in the early hours of Wednesday, after it was clear that Democrats had taken the House and Senate. Jordan Lasker—the man behind the X account "Crémieux,” which is a popular follow in the tech world and is known for posting race-based pseudoscience—also weighed in, saying, “Data centers in space are an incredible idea and anyone who doubted them didn't think enough about tonight's election results.” Throughout the day, Musk employees, tech investors, AI researchers, venture capitalists, and industry fans joined the chorus of support for space-based data centers. Soham Mehta, a research fellow at the techno-optimist think tank Foundation for American Innovation, argued that underwater data centers should also be considered. (In June, China began operating what it claims is the world’s first underwater data center.) Some companies are already trying to put compute in orbit. Among them are Google, which launched a satellite that it says contains “data center class TPU,” and SpaceX, which says it aims to deploy “thousands of AI satellites starting as soon as late 2027.” Blue Origin is also in the mix, having filed for a Federal Communications Commission permit to launch 50,000 satellites that will constitute an “orbital data center system.” There are also a few startups aiming to build data centers in space, including Starcloud, which claims to have carried "the first Nvidia H100 GPU into orbit" in November 2025. Despite being technically possible, the realities of in-orbit data centers are difficult. Among other things, space-based data centers are much more expensive than land-based ones, can’t grow to hyperscale size, and are subject to the risks and whims of satellite launches. When it comes to Texas data centers, the concerns of tech bros aren’t completely unfounded. Experts tell WIRED that the change in leadership could translate to some concrete changes in the industry—albeit with limits. Although Democrats will have control of the Texas House of Representatives, Republicans still have control over the state’s senate. Robert Paterson, professor of land use and environmental planning at the University of Texas at Austin, tells WIRED that the split means that some immediate attempts at change “will probably be stymied a bit.” Adrian Shelley, director of nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen’s Texas office, tells WIRED that the legislature would be a likely place to hash out high-impact policies like the reallocation of state agency resources. However, he adds that the governor could effect more immediate changes by issuing executive orders, or requesting the resignation of politically appointed officials in state agencies. Shelley says that these oversight agencies—such as the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, the Public Utility Commission, and the Texas Water Development Board—have the authority to charge fines for breaking state law, or in extreme cases to revoke permits for projects like data centers. But Paterson notes that Texas developers have particularly strong “vested rights,” which protects the terms of their projects from the moment their permits are approved, even if construction hasn’t begun. Another medium-term route to reshaping Texas’ data center industry could be to give more power to its counties. Paterson noted that nearly half of the state’s data centers exist in unincorporated territory, which puts them outside the jurisdiction of city zoning laws. Unlike other states, Paterson says, Texas counties have relatively limited enforcement abilities. Under the state's so-called Dillon’s Rule, counties only have powers that are “specifically allotted to it by the state.” So while they have authority over things like access and egress to county roads or construction on floodplains, he says they don't have the zoning authority that would help closely regulate projects like data centers. Paterson says that the new attorney general could theoretically adjust the terms in the state’s biannual handbook, which establishes the limits of county authority. He also argues that even in a split legislature, especially since anti-data-center sentiment crosses party lines, state lawmakers could propose a viable bill giving counties “limited zoning authority over data centers." Shelley tells WIRED that since “data centers were a decisive factor in this blue wave,” the upcoming legislative season will be “very interesting.” “I will say the data center industry hasn't shown a lot of interest in working with state lawmakers or local leaders,” Shelley says, “and I will be interested to see if that changes.” If not, there’s always low Earth orbit.

artigo.texto: A APsystems apresentará seus mais recentes microinversores e soluções de armazenamento de energia na ExpoSolar Peru 2026 AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 4 de novembro de 2026 Os modelos QS2, DS3D Boosted e APstorage ELS 11.4K serão os destaques do portfólio de produtos da empresa, que também apresentará soluções de armazenamento de energia para sistemas isolados da rede elétrica e uma prévia de sua linha de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS). LIMA, Peru, 4 de novembro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ — A APsystems participará da ExpoSolar Peru 2026, evento que será realizado nos dias 17 e 18 de novembro, no Los Delfines Hotel & Convention Center. No estande 4, localizado próximo à entrada do palco principal da conferência, a empresa apresentará suas mais recentes inovações em geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento de energia, com foco nas necessidades de instaladores, distribuidores e desenvolvedores de projetos. Entre os destaques estará o QS2 de 2.500 W, um microinversor que integra quatro rastreadores independentes do ponto de máxima potência (MPPT), otimizando a geração de energia de cada módulo em aplicações residenciais e comerciais. Também estará em destaque o DS3D Boosted de 2.200 W, uma nova versão que amplia a faixa de potência dessa linha de microinversores. A oferta para projetos comerciais e industriais incluirá informações sobre o QT2 de 1.800 W para redes trifásicas de 480 V e sua versão de 1.728 W para 208 V. Essas soluções complementam o portfólio da APsystems para atender a instalações com diferentes exigências elétricas e módulos de alta potência. O armazenamento de energia terá papel central com o APstorage PCS ELS 11.4K, uma solução com acoplamento em CA que possibilita a integração de baterias compatíveis a instalações fotovoltaicas. Seu gerenciamento inteligente oferece opções para autoconsumo e energia de reserva, dependendo da configuração do sistema. A oferta será complementada por informações sobre a APbattery e sua integração com o PCS. A exposição também incluirá o EZOG-4.0D, um sistema integrado para aplicações isoladas da rede elétrica, com capacidade de armazenamento de 4,0 kWh. Seu design compacto conta com dois controladores MPPT independentes, grau de proteção IP66 e sistema de resfriamento sem ventilador, garantindo operação silenciosa. Também estará em exposição o AHS-6.3H, uma solução residencial completa para sistemas isolados da rede elétrica, que combina um inversor de 6,3 kW com baterias modulares de fosfato de ferro-lítio (LiFePO?). Sua arquitetura empilhável permite expandir a capacidade de armazenamento conforme as necessidades da família aumentam, enquanto sua tela sensível ao toque facilita o monitoramento e o gerenciamento do sistema. Antecipando suas próximas inovações, a APsystems apresentará em primeira mão o Ocean, sua linha de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) voltada a aplicações comerciais e industriais. O fornecimento de energia de reserva, a resposta à demanda e a escalabilidade serão os principais diferenciais dessa linha de produtos, que os participantes poderão conhecer em primeira mão durante o evento. “Na Expo Solar Peru, demonstraremos como estamos expandindo as possibilidades da energia solar com nossos novos microinversores e com as soluções APstorage, lideradas pelo ELS 11.4K. “Queremos trazer para o Peru tecnologias que atendam às necessidades atuais e oferecer uma prévia de nossas soluções de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) de grande capacidade, que marcarão a próxima etapa da evolução do nosso portfólio”, afirmou Alma Aldana, gerente de Marketing da APsystems para a América Latina. A experiência será complementada pelas unidades de comunicação ECU-R e ECU-C, além de conteúdos sobre o APbot e de uma prévia da APacademy. Com essa participação, a APsystems visa fortalecer os seus laços com os profissionais do mercado peruano, apresentando a eles o seu portfólio de produtos e o suporte oferecido por sua equipe regional. A APsystems convida os participantes a visitarem o estande 4 nos dias 17 e 18 de novembro, das 10h às 19h, para conhecer de perto seus equipamentos e conversar sobre oportunidades de aplicação em seus próximos projetos. img alt=”” src=”https://rt.prnewswire.com/rt.gif?NewsItemId=PT87455&Transmission_Id=202611041327PR_NEWS_LATAM____PT87455&DateId=20261104″ style=”border:0px; width:1px; height:1px;” /> Tópicos Relacionados: Notícias de Feiras Comerciais, Serviços Públicos, Componentes Eletrônicos, Computador/Eletrônica, Produtos e Serviços Ambientais, Energias Alternativas A OESP não é(são) responsável(is) por erros, incorreções, atrasos ou quaisquer decisões tomadas por seus clientes com base nos Conteúdos ora disponibilizados, bem como tais Conteúdos não representam a opinião da OESP e são de inteira responsabilidade da PR Newswire Ltda

artigo.texto: Modelos e plataformas de IA NTT DATA inaugura centro de dados de 12 MW preparado para IA em Jacarta e lança o APN Connect Adicione Unite.AI às suas fontes preferidas no Google A NTT DATA anunciou, em 3 de novembro de 2026, a inauguração do centro de dados Jakarta 2 Annex, na Indonésia, acrescentando 12 MW de capacidade de TI para IA e outras cargas de trabalho de alta densidade. A empresa também lançou o APN Connect, um serviço de rede fotônica que conecta o novo local e o JKT2 ao JKT3. Energia redundante e conectividade no campus A instalação, conhecida como JKT2A, foi projetada para cargas de trabalho de computação em escala hiperescalar, empresarial e de alta densidade. Seu projeto elétrico utiliza duas subestações de energia, uma arquitetura de fonte de alimentação ininterrupta 2N e geradores de reserva N+1. O sistema de refrigeração conta com chillers refrigerados a ar N+1 e unidades de tratamento de ar para salas de computadores N+2. O local também dispõe de um projeto certificado Tier III, operações de segurança 24 horas por dia, 7 dias por semana, e controles de segurança física em várias camadas. O JKT2A está localizado no campus de Jacarta da NTT Global Data Centers e amplia o ecossistema de conectividade estabelecido pelo JKT2. A NTT DATA contabiliza mais de 240 provedores de serviços de rede no JKT2, além do JKT-IX, de importantes provedores de serviços em nuvem e de conexões essenciais por cabos submarinos. A interconexão direta no campus permite que os clientes expandam a infraestrutura sem perder as conexões com as redes, os parceiros e os ambientes de nuvem existentes. O próprio JKT2A oferece acesso neutro em relação a operadoras e provedores de nuvem, tanto a provedores de rede nacionais e internacionais quanto às principais plataformas de nuvem. APN Connect conecta instalações em Jacarta A NTT DATA descreve o APN Connect como o primeiro serviço da Indonésia a utilizar a tecnologia All-Photonics Network. Desenvolvido com base na tecnologia Innovative Optical and Wireless Network, o serviço oferece conectividade de Camada 1 entre o JKT2/JKT2A e o JKT3, separados por aproximadamente 35 km. Segundo a empresa, o APN Connect oferece alta capacidade e baixa latência, permitindo a sincronização de dados em tempo real entre instalações geograficamente distantes. Entre os usos indicados estão a recuperação de desastres, a replicação de dados e operações resilientes em vários centros de dados. A conexão complementa o projeto de energia e refrigeração da instalação ao viabilizar a sincronização e a recuperação entre locais, ampliando a resiliência para além de um único centro de dados. Desenvolvimento desde 2024 O anúncio da construção feito em 15 de maio de 2024 pela NTT DATA previa a conclusão no início de 2026, o que significa que a inauguração ocorreu depois do cronograma original. Os 12 MW de carga crítica de TI previstos foram mantidos na instalação concluída. O projeto anterior descrevia um edifício de sete andares no centro de Jacarta, a aproximadamente 20 km do Aeroporto Internacional Soekarno-Hatta, com refrigeração a ar, segurança física e várias fontes redundantes de energia. A NTT DATA projetou investir mais de US$ 10 bilhões na expansão de centros de dados entre 2023 e 2027, programa do qual o JKT2A faz parte. O plano de 2024 também previa opções de energia 100% renovável para os clientes do campus, vinculadas à meta da empresa de utilizar 100% de energia renovável em suas próprias operações até 2030. Doug Adams, presidente e CEO da NTT Global Data Centers, afirmou que a economia digital da Indonésia está gerando uma demanda significativa por infraestrutura escalável e altamente conectada, à medida que os clientes desenvolvem projetos de nuvem, IA e transformação digital. A expansão incorpora resiliência ao aumento de capacidade: o JKT2A fornece a redundância elétrica e de refrigeração necessária para a computação de alta densidade, a interconexão no campus preserva as relações existentes dos clientes com suas redes, e o APN Connect amplia a sincronização e a recuperação entre locais geograficamente distantes.

artigo.texto: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has approved a €30 million loan for a battery energy storage system (BESS) in Tenevo, south-eastern Bulgaria, with the financing part of a wider €60 million package. The project will be delivered by Tenevo Solar Technologies and supported by parallel €30 million funding from Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI). The battery storage facility is expected to deliver 246 MW of power capacity and 512.5 MWh of storage, co-located with an existing 242 MWp solar photovoltaic (PV) plant on the same site. The initiative aims to strengthen grid stability and support the integration of additional renewable energy into Bulgaria’s power system. Background: energy transition and grid flexibility Bulgaria has been accelerating its shift away from fossil fuels and toward renewable energy generation. As more solar and other renewables come online, electricity systems must manage variability and maintain reliability. Battery storage is increasingly used to add flexibility to power grids. By storing electricity and discharging it when needed, BESS can help stabilize the system and improve energy security. The investment: a €60 million package for battery storage in Tenevo EBRD’s financing to Tenevo Solar Technologies covers the development of a major BESS at the Tenevo site. The project forms part of a €60 million financing package, combining the EBRD loan (€30 million) with parallel funding from RBI (€30 million). The BESS will be co-located with an existing solar PV installation of 242 MWp at the Tenevo site. In addition, the site includes a separate 65 MW battery installation with storage of 260 MWh, and the new facility is designed to increase overall storage capacity at the location. Building on earlier solar investment Tenevo Solar Technologies has previously received EBRD support for the Tenevo solar PV plant. The EBRD had provided €50 million to build and operate the fully merchant Tenevo solar PV plant, and the solar project was supported by first loss risk cover under the EBRD’s InvestEU Framework for Sustainable Transition. The new battery project is positioned as an extension of that earlier investment, aiming to enhance the site’s ability to store and dispatch clean electricity. Link to Recovery and Resilience Plan support for renewables and storage The EBRD also worked with Bulgaria’s Ministry of Energy on the design of grant schemes, competitive allocation, and technical verification mechanisms to support renewable energy and electricity storage projects under the country’s Recovery and Resilience Plan. According to the EBRD, September 2026 marked the completion of these schemes. Why the project matters for Bulgaria’s power sector The EBRD described rapid growth in battery storage capacity as a significant energy transition achievement for Bulgaria, supporting renewable energy integration and decarbonisation. In its statement, the bank said the project will help increase system flexibility and integrate more renewables. “By increasing the system’s flexibility and helping to integrate more renewable energy, Tenevo will contribute to a more resilient, secure and sustainable power sector,” EBRD Head of Bulgaria Manuela Naessl said. EBRD’s broader role in Bulgaria The EBRD said it is a leading institutional investor in Bulgaria, having invested almost €5.3 billion across 330 projects to date. The bank’s stated focus includes private sector development, competitiveness, and the green economy transition. Key Details - Initiative or programme: Battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Tenevo - Lead organization: Tenevo Solar Technologies - Partners: Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI) - Funding amount: €30 million loan from the EBRD (part of a €60 million financing package) - Geographic focus: Tenevo, south-eastern Bulgaria - Target groups: Not specified in the source - Duration or timeline: Not specified in the source - Expected reach or outcomes: 246 MW battery power capacity and 512.5 MWh electricity storage; improved grid stability and support for integrating additional renewables Why This Matters Battery storage investments are increasingly central to power-sector decarbonisation, because they help grids manage the variability of renewable generation. For NGOs and development professionals, the EBRD and RBI-backed Tenevo project highlights how large-scale clean energy deployment can be paired with grid flexibility measures. The case also reflects a practical intersection between finance and implementation capacity: the EBRD states it worked with Bulgaria’s Ministry of Energy to design grant schemes and verification mechanisms under the national Recovery and Resilience Plan, with completion reported in September 2026. This is relevant to civil society groups monitoring how renewable and storage policies translate into investable pipelines. While the announcement does not provide details on social outcomes or community-level components, it can inform program design and partnership discussions around energy access, workforce transitions, and the governance of energy transition support mechanisms. Source: EBRD finances major battery energy storage project in Bulgaria

artigo.texto: The initiatives are being led by Ava Community Energy, a local nonprofit electric service provider serving 2 million residents in two counties and 16 cities in the East Bay, the area east of San Francisco. Eight project sites in four cities — Berkeley, Fremont, Hayward and Livermore — are participating in Ava’s Critical Municipal Facilities (CMF) program which will fund the buildout of solar generation and battery storage at key municipal facilities including fire stations and community centers. “We’ve completely financed the systems, no upfront cost to our cities,” said Howard Chang, CEO for Ava Community Energy. The critical energy program, he said, was a way for Ava to engage with its member jurisdictions to better serve them. “What are your energy needs? Where do you have really critical services that you want to ensure that you have sufficient backup power, both for your own energy needs, but also for broader community resilience?” Chang said, as he went through some of the scenarios the program is designed to address. Ava has installed 500 kilowatts of photovoltaic solar panels and 1.32 megawatt-hours of battery storage across the eight sites, capable of generating 778,000 kilowatt-hours of local renewable energy in just the first year, according to a news release. The program, Chang said, was also crafted as a way to “decarbonize, overall,” noting a number of the member cities have in place climate action plans requiring them to tap renewable sources of energy. “Our Climate Action Plan specifically calls for battery storage in city buildings and critical facilities to help reduce emissions and to allow our staff to serve our community during emergencies and grid outages,” wrote Erik Pearson, environmental services manager for the Public Works and Utilities Department in Hayward, a city of about 156,000 residents south of Oakland. The Hayward Corporation Yard and Fire Station No. 1 were the first of the projects to go online about two weeks ago. The city’s climate action plan, Pearson said in an email, “includes very ambitious goals for reducing greenhouse gas emissions,” and adding more renewables to the energy mix “will play a significant part in [helping] us meet our goals.” Hayward is not new to renewable energy. The city installed its first rooftop solar project in 2005, adding others over the years including, Pearson said, a 1.6-megawatt installation at the city’s wastewater treatment plant. With the two new projects, Hayward will now have 14 city facilities equipped with solar generation, including seven of its nine fire stations. Ava’s next CMF projects will be coming online in the coming months, Chang said. The deployments will also help the utility reduce the demand on its power delivery during high-peak times. “Because these are solar-plus-storage, they can be managed in a way that’s beneficial, both for our own portfolio costs as well as for the grid,” Chang said. Batteries can store up excess solar power during the day and discharge it in the evenings when wholesale power rates climb due to high demand. “That’s generally good. That’s good for us as we manage our wholesale portfolio, and it’s good for our customers,” the CEO said. Ultimately, these efforts are aimed at growing resiliency as California cities and counties are all dealing with risks associated with wildfires, extreme weather and the public service demands these events pose. The sites include fire stations, community and senior centers and more. “So there’s a lot of variety of different types of sites that we’re installing these systems at, and it’s not yet fully known how we’re going to operate these battery systems,” said Chang. “At its core, we’re going to charge and discharge at economically optimal times to try to bring down energy costs for our customers. And that’s important.” It should be noted that the solar energy and battery systems deployed are not seen as a direct “one-for-one” replacement of diesel generators, “but it’s a start to really see how batteries can serve as resilience-oriented backup systems for these really critical sites,” Chang said.

artigo.texto: Digital twins will create a new blueprint for data center design Digital twins enable operators to run 'what if' scenarios Digital twins are not simply tools for simulation. They’re assets that have the potential to reconfigure how data centers are designed, tested and optimized. Many operators have already been quick to catch on to the advantages these tools offer, de-risking critical decisions, accelerating innovation, and optimizing performance. The majority of technology leaders in major corporations are already looking to implement digital twin initiatives. Despite this, only 42% of decision-makers in data centers are currently using digital twins, with many still perceiving them as internal tools. In an industry where downtime is incredibly costly, and infrastructure decisions have long-term consequences, the ability to ‘test drive’ different scenarios in a risk-free environment isn’t just an advantage, it’s a gamechanger. AVP Technology at GlobalLogic (a Hitachi Group company). In fact, according to McKinsey, the implementation of digital twins can accelerate the creation and setup of new projects, including AI-enabled features, by up to 60% and cut costs by around 15%. A 360-degree view of operations The data center industry is facing a perfect storm of complexity. Rapid growth in AI workloads, stringent sustainability requirements, and unprecedented IT infrastructure investment are all converging. Traditional approaches to planning and testing – spreadsheets, static models, and gut instinct – simply can’t keep up. Enter digital twins: precise virtual replicas of physical data centers that enable operators to simulate scenarios, test configurations, and optimize performance before committing resources to real-world deployment. Digital twins aren’t new. Manufacturing, aerospace, and energy sectors have been using them for years. But their application to data centers represents a significant leap forward in how the industry approaches design, operations, and resilience planning. By creating a comprehensive digital replica – from server racks to HVAC systems to power distribution – operators can run “what-if” scenarios that would be impossible or prohibitively expensive to test in production. The value proposition is clear: reduce risk, accelerate time-to-market, and optimize resource allocation. But the devil is in the details. Building an effective digital twin requires more than just 3D modeling software. It demands deep integration across IT and OT systems, sophisticated data analytics, and the right talent to interpret results and translate them into actionable insights. Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed! AI initiatives face similar hurdles. Just 25% of AI implementations have achieved expected ROI, likely hindered by poor system integration and ineffective strategies for data management. Eradicating IT/OT siloes One of the most transformative capabilities of digital twins is their ability to expose hidden interdependencies between IT and OT systems. In traditional data center planning, these systems are often designed and managed in silos. IT teams focus on compute, storage, and networking. OT teams handle physical infrastructure – power, cooling, and building management. This separation creates blind spots that can lead to catastrophic failures under stress. Let’s look at an example. Imagine that a data center provider simulates a regional power grid failure. Primary power is cut, backup generators take over seamlessly, and failover scripts reroute workloads to a secondary facility. HVAC and building management systems (BMS), which are not integrated with IT systems, continue running in standard operating mode. The HVAC system, functioning separately to the simulated power outage and increased IT load, does not adjust cooling to match the spike in server activity. In a real-life scenario, this could result in server aisles nearing thermal shutdown. When systems are not “in dialogue” with one another, and the physical interdependencies between IT and OT systems are not well understood, operators end up with a false sense of readiness. Another issue is that the industry currently lacks the talent to deploy digital twin technologies. 58% of operators in the UK currently struggle to fill critical roles, whilst 40% state that retaining their core team is particularly difficult. This revolving door of talent can make upskilling a challenge and, as things stand, there aren’t enough experts who understand how to direct simulations. A test-drive – for the data center Just as manufacturers test production line changes in their digital twin before implementing them on the factory floor, data center operators can simulate cooling adjustments, power reconfigurations, or workload migrations in their digital twin before touching production infrastructure. The ability to test failure scenarios such as power outages, cooling failures and equipment malfunctions enables operators to check if their disaster recovery procedures actually work and identify gaps before they become real-world crises. Finally, digital twins are making a real difference in helping operators to draw up Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with customers, providing assurance that they can deliver on certain levels of uptime. As operators look to scale their infrastructure in line with the exponential growth of AI, digital twins have a critical role to play, ensuring performance isn’t comprised even as capacity expands.
