artigo.texto: Sexta-feira, 06 de novembro de 2026 Por Redação O Sul | 5 de novembro de 2026 A vigência está prevista até dezembro de 2030. Foto: Reprodução A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) alertou o governo federal sobre o risco de ficar sem recursos para quitar compromissos financeiros e manter o funcionamento de serviços básicos. Entre as despesas pendentes estão R$ 30,76 milhões referentes à aquisição de seu próprio centro de processamento de dados (data center), localizado em Brasília. A estrutura tecnológica é responsável por sustentar serviços digitais oferecidos a cidadãos e empresas de telecomunicações, além de sistemas utilizados pela agência em suas atividades de fiscalização. O eventual atraso nos pagamentos pode comprometer a continuidade dos serviços contratados e provocar cobranças adicionais por parte dos fornecedores. Diante da situação, o presidente da Anatel, Carlos Baigorri, solicitou ao Ministério do Planejamento o desbloqueio de R$ 30 milhões. O pedido foi apresentado após tentativas anteriores de antecipar recursos que não foram atendidas pela Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional, vinculada ao Ministério da Fazenda. Em dezembro de 2025, a agência havia firmado um contrato de R$ 44,95 milhões com prestadores de serviços e fornecedores de tecnologia. O acordo contempla equipamentos, programas de gerenciamento, conectividade e serviços de implantação, migração, suporte, manutenção e garantia. A vigência está prevista até dezembro de 2030. Em manifestação encaminhada ao governo, Baigorri afirmou que as projeções financeiras apontam risco de insuficiência de limite para o pagamento integral dos compromissos assumidos, especialmente no último trimestre de 2026. Os valores pendentes do data center estão classificados como restos a pagar, expressão utilizada na administração pública para identificar despesas de exercícios anteriores que ainda não foram quitadas. A agência atribui a dificuldade financeira ao bloqueio de R$ 51,83 milhões determinado pelo governo federal em maio. A medida reduziu o orçamento discricionário da Anatel, destinado a despesas de custeio e investimentos, de R$ 275,37 milhões para R$ 223,54 milhões. A redução foi de aproximadamente 19%. Para se adequar à restrição, a agência afirma que revisou contratos, projetos e despesas. Também informou que procura evitar a incidência de multas, juros e outros encargos decorrentes de atrasos nos pagamentos. A dificuldade não é recente. Em agosto, a Anatel já havia solicitado a antecipação de R$ 23,3 milhões que estavam previstos para dezembro. A agência informou que as medidas adotadas até agora buscam reduzir os efeitos das limitações orçamentárias, mas advertiu que a manutenção das restrições poderá exigir novas reprogramações de despesas. O Ministério da Fazenda afirmou que os bloqueios decorrem da necessidade de cumprimento das medidas de contingenciamento do governo federal. Segundo a pasta, a situação fiscal dos órgãos é reavaliada a cada dois meses. A próxima avaliação está prevista para 24 de novembro, quando poderá ser analisada a possibilidade de redução dos cortes. Paralelamente, cerca de 40 entidades empresariais manifestaram apoio à autonomia financeira das agências reguladoras. O documento apresentado pelas organizações defende que os recursos destinados à fiscalização e à regulação não sejam comprometidos por bloqueios orçamentários.

artigo.texto: ClickIP vê risco de bolha com obrigação de investir em data centers Maykon Souza critica proposta de vincular infraestrutura regional a leilões de espectro e defende crédito para o setor. O CEO da ClickIP, Maykon Souza, vê risco de formação de uma bolha de data centers regionais (“edge”) caso a Anatel vincule investimentos em infraestrutura regional a compromissos de aquisição de espectro. Em entrevista ao TV.Síntese que vai ao ar logo mais, às 19h, o executivo afirmou que a obrigação pode estimular a construção de instalações sem demanda correspondente. “Isso vai criar uma bolha e a bolha vai estourar, e vai dar prejuízo para as empresas e prejuízo para o mercado”, afirmou, ao comentar a proposta. Na avaliação de Souza, a demanda por processamento está concentrada nos grandes data centers, os chamados hyperscales, e sua distribuição para estruturas regionais depende das necessidades das empresas clientes. “Acredito que é errado porque a Anatel está querendo criar um mercado que ainda não existe”, declarou. A posição parte de uma operadora que já investiu em um data center em Manaus. Segundo Souza, a ClickIP destinou R$ 21 milhões à infraestrutura e pouco mais de R$ 20 milhões à capacidade computacional. Inaugurada em 2024, a instalação surgiu da necessidade de melhorar a estrutura utilizada pela própria empresa para prestar serviços de conectividade. Demanda interna sustenta ocupação O executivo informou que cerca de oito racks estavam ocupados no momento da entrevista, com predominância do uso interno. A demanda de clientes externos, segundo ele, começa a chegar, com projetos voltados principalmente a empresas da Zona Franca de Manaus. O projeto começou a ser concebido em 2020, e as obras tiveram início em 2021. Durante seu desenvolvimento, os sócios decidiram ampliar o investimento para transformar a infraestrutura em uma unidade de negócios que também atendesse terceiros. Segundo Souza, a contratação do data center não exige que o cliente utilize os serviços de banda larga da ClickIP. A instalação já hospeda servidores de outras empresas e recebe operadoras em regime de colocation. Viabilidade depende das aplicações Para o executivo, a oportunidade para provedores regionais está na interiorização dos data centers, mas a existência de uma cidade sem essa infraestrutura não basta para justificar o investimento. É necessário avaliar a presença de empresas e de aplicações que demandem processamento próximo dos usuários. “Boa parte das aplicações não dependem de baixa latência”, afirmou. Souza defende um modelo no qual o processamento de uma mesma empresa seja distribuído entre sua estrutura interna, data centers regionais e grandes instalações de nuvem. A definição sobre onde executar cada aplicação, segundo ele, precisa ser construída com o cliente. Nesse cenário, o próprio provedor pode funcionar como cliente âncora do empreendimento. Para Souza, o investimento faz sentido quando o uso interno sustenta o modelo de negócios, sem depender exclusivamente de uma expectativa de contratação futura por terceiros. A disponibilidade de profissionais também foi apontada como obstáculo. Segundo o executivo, os fundadores precisaram aprender sobre a operação do setor, e a empresa continua capacitando sua equipe. IA pode exigir outra infraestrutura A ClickIP também avalia que uma eventual expansão para cargas mais intensivas de inteligência artificial exigiria uma estrutura específica. Souza explicou que o data center foi concebido antes dessa demanda e que os desafios envolvem dissipação de calor e balanceamento de carga. Caso a demanda por IA avance para o processamento regional e exija refrigeração líquida, o executivo prevê a construção de um anexo no terreno da empresa. A possibilidade está condicionada à evolução desse mercado. Na discussão sobre políticas de incentivo, Souza apontou o financiamento como uma forma de apoiar os investimentos. “O que o governo de modo geral pode ajudar é com linhas de crédito”, afirmou.

Aggreko Introduces New Line of Battery Energy Storage Systems for Immediate and Large-Scale Applications Aggreko 4 min read With new BESS nodes, the company offers more options for rapidly growing industries in North America Aggreko Introduces New Line of Battery Energy Storage Systems for Immediate and Large-Scale Applications HOUSTON, Nov. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aggreko, a global leader in engineered energy and temperature solutions, has announced the expansion of its Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) fleet with the addition of three new models in a range of capacities. This launch introduces a small node 120 kW/120 kWh system, along with two large node configurations: trailer-mounted 1 MW/1.2 MWh and 1 MW/1.3MWh units. The refreshed models in the company's battery storage fleet reinforce its focus on designing, deploying, and optimizing engineered energy solutions for its customers across a wide variety of businesses. By integrating advanced BESS technologies with sector-specific expertise, Aggreko delivers right-sized smart energy solutions that help customers improve efficiency, control costs, and manage emissions without compromising reliability. The flexibility and power of these new BESS units make them particularly attractive for highly demanding and rapidly growing sectors, such as data centers. For data center operators and contractors, these engineered solutions can seamlessly integrate with diesel, gas, and renewables to overcome site capacity constraints. Whether powering data center construction operations or substituting delayed or limited grid connections, the new BESS models provide crucial power security and efficiency. The new additions to the Aggreko BESS fleet include: 120 kW / 120 kWh BESS This trailer-mounted unit is designed for ease of maneuverability and low noise levels, making it ideal for noise-sensitive areas. It features a 544A pass-through, ideal for supporting large motor start equipment like tower cranes. The system can be used in island mode, as part of a hybrid solution, or in parallel with other energy storage systems. 1 MW / 1.2 MWh Trailer-Mounted BESS This containerized, mobile trailer package pairs exceptional reliability with rapid deployment and is suitable for both grid-forming and grid-following applications. The trailer-mounted system delivers zero CO2 emissions\ and requires minimal maintenance. 1 MW / 1.3 MWh Trailer-mounted BESS Engineered for the most energy-intensive applications, this containerized, mobile unit provides dependable energy for the most unpredictable loads. Equipped with built-in HVAC, fire suppression, and a wide operating temperature range, it allows operators to safely establish reactive grid interconnection while optimizing performance. "As our customers' need for distributed power across sectors grow, we are excited to unveil our latest energy storage options with our most advanced technologies yet," said Stephen Saal, Vice President of Sales & Marketing at Aggreko North America. "Because every site is different, we are proud to offer these new BESS nodes as part of our engineered energy solutions, which are tailored for customer needs and industry. By providing a containerized, mobile design alongside our technical expertise, we meet our customers wherever they are on their energy journey, ensuring reliable outcomes that are right sized for today and ready to scale for the future." The new units join Aggreko's existing BESS fleet, which ranges from 24 kW to 1000 kW, giving customers more ways to match storage to their load. Each system can operate on its own, in parallel with other batteries, or as part of a hybrid solution with Aggreko's generators, where the battery carries the load and the generator runs only when needed. This reduces generator runtime, fuel consumption, and maintenance. Every deployment is backed by Aggreko's technical expertise and remote monitoring for reliable, uninterrupted operation. We design, deploy and optimize the flexible energy and temperature solutions that are essential to our customers' operations. We work across all major industries and bring deep sector expertise to shaping solutions around our customers' needs. We use our experience of working in demanding environments and complex applications to engineer reliable, efficient and sustainable solutions that meet our customers' needs, from critical emergencies to long-term energy security. In a world of growing energy demand and an increasing focus on sustainability, we are setting the pace. We are investing in new markets, new applications and the sustainable equipment, fuels and services that power our customers and their energy transition, wherever they are on their journey. Headquartered in the UK, we employ approximately 8,000 people worldwide and are active in over 80 countries. For more information, please visit our website at www.aggreko.com. artigo.texto: The News In Piqua, Ohio, voters on Tuesday approved a ban on large data centers and recalled the commissioners who backed Metaâs massive project there. In Trenton, less than 50 miles south, a similar ban passed. And outside Columbus, the heart of Ohioâs data center boom, voters in Ashville repealed the villageâs deal with developer EdgeConneX. These Ohio races were part of a swell of anti-data-center sentiment that echoed across the country in dozens of ballot measures concerning bans, moratoriums, or stricter regulations and oversight. The votes were hyperlocal and often emotional in nature, but they could carry financial consequences, because some of the projects at stake were already in motion. - Meta bought more than 600 acres in Piqua last year for about $110 million, and signed agreements with the city in January. âWe are proud of our investments in Ohio, and will work with local officials to determine the future of our investment in Piqua,â a Meta spokesperson told Semafor on Wednesday. - Amazon had proposed a 600-acre campus on land Trenton hoped to annex; the ban effectively blocks that plan, according to local news. An Amazon spokesperson didnât directly comment on the vote but said the company is âcommitted to setting a high bar for responsible data center development in Ohio, and will continue engaging communities early as we build out this important infrastructure.â - EdgeConneX said its development in Ashville is moving forward despite the vote, given that its permits are secured and construction is underway. More than 40% of the USâ planned data center capacity is located in states where governors or governors-elect have pledged or already imposed a pause on new data centers, according to a Cleanview analysis. That doesnât mean the data center buildout will grind to a halt, but markets are pricing in a slowdown. Shares of companies that are directly exposed to the physical buildout of data centers tanked Wednesday, including Modine (a maker of data center HVACs, down about 21%) and Sterling Infrastructure (site prep and electrical work, also down 21%). Hyperscaler stocks, though, soared, with traders betting they will be forced to rein in the rapid spending that has pushed their free cash flow to negative territory. More restrictions on data center construction also means tech giantsâ compute capacity âpotentially even becomes more valuable,â Morgan Stanley US Equities Strategist Andrew Pauker told Semafor. The View From Washington Tech companies are also recalibrating their data center strategies in Washington as they prepare for a Democrat-controlled Congress. One tech-focused public affairs adviser suggested companies work with Democrats to craft national rules around data center development. Incoming Democrats in the House and Senate say theyâre going into Congress with a mandate to do something about AI data centers, and Republican groups who pushed their party to listen to grassroots concerns about data centers are saying Washington Republicans can only blame themselves for the midterm losses after aligning with AI companies. Ellen DiMauro contributed to this story.

artigo.texto: Nov 5 (Reuters) - Alphabet's Google will invest $17 billion to build its first data center in Wyoming, the company said on Thursday, pushing ahead with a major AI infrastructure investment as political resistance to data center expansion grows following the US midterm elections. Of the 41 data center-related ballot measures voted on this week, all but one went against data centers, according to Ballotpedia. Google's facility will be built in partnership with Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power and Related Digital. The project will be powered in part by a planned 702-megawatt fuel-cell development equipped with carbon capture and storage technology. The fuel cells will be supplied by Bloom Energy. Wyoming is a Republican stronghold, where Donald Trump won more than 70% of the presidential vote in 2024. The announcement comes as investors reassess the pace of the AI infrastructure buildout. Wins by candidates opposed to data-center expansion in key Texas and Georgia races during the midterm elections have added to concerns that political resistance could complicate the industry's rapid expansion. Meanwhile, Microsoft has declined to expand a Texas data-center agreement with AI cloud provider Nscale, with Bloomberg News reporting earlier in the day that the company planned to tighten oversight of some data-center projects from neocloud providers Nebius, IREN and Nscale. Shares of Bloom Energy also slumped more than 14% on worries that any potential restrictions could hit the industry. (Reporting by Prathik Jayaprakash in Bengaluru; Editing by Sriraj Kalluvila)

artigo.texto: Chinese battery producer CATL unveiled a dual-electric range-extender battery system for heavy-duty electric trucks on 20th October 2026. The pack features a large, swappable battery and an onboard battery that adds driving range. The primary battery is offered with the listed capacities of 432 kWh or 513 kWh, while the further range-extension battery provides an extra 77 kWh. Operators can also simply swap out the main battery at compatible swap stations without having to wait for a charging session to complete. The architecture aims at freight operators, who find vehicle downtime, cost of batteries, and adaptability of routes major issues in running vehicles. The primary swappable battery has been separated from the reserve battery to potentially increase utilisation of batteries and reduce some of the financial hurdles to electrify heavy trucks. CATL is developing the system as part of its QIJI battery swapping ecosystem. The firm is planning to increase the number of sites for electric heavy-duty vehicles. Battery swapping could benefit high-utilisation freight routes with predictable demand, but they have to use standardised batteries and vehicles built to use them, and require significant infrastructure investment and other factors to ensure stations will be viable. Building two batteries also complicates engineering. Automakers need to look at the battery packaging for both battery packs, safety features and the control strategy. Why it matters Swappable batteries and the energy content stored in internal reserves could see battery electric trucks become the norm, entering the realm of the possible for commercial freight hauliers working to a timetable.

artigo.texto: A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações enfrenta um grave déficit financeiro e está sem recursos para quitar as faturas do projeto de seu novo data center em Brasília, totalizando uma necessidade de R$ 30,76 milhões. Crise financeira afeta contas básicas Além do projeto tecnológico, a autarquia federal lida com dificuldades para honrar despesas cotidianas essenciais para o seu funcionamento administrativo. O pedido de socorro ao governo Para contornar o problema, o presidente da Anatel, Carlos Baigorri, esteve reunido com representantes do Ministério do Planejamento na semana passada, pleiteando a liberação de R$ 30 milhões que encontram-se travados. Bloqueio orçamentário e impacto O cenário de escassez financeira decorre de um corte de R$ 51,83 milhões imposto no mês de maio, o qual provocou uma retração de 19% na verba discricionária da instituição, voltada a investimentos e manutenção. Contrato milionário de tecnologia O acordo para a implementação da estrutura de dados foi firmado em dezembro de 2025, envolvendo um montante de R$ 44,95 milhões destinados à aquisição de hardwares, serviços associados, suporte técnico e garantia prolongada. Diante do cenário crítico, a autarquia pontuou que “a persistência das restrições orçamentárias e financeiras poderá exigir novas medidas de reprogramação de despesas”.

artigo.texto: Taiwan vai desenvolver CBAM doméstico e sistema de comércio de emissões O presidente de Taiwan, Lai Ching-te, anunciou que o governo pretende desenvolver uma versão doméstica do mecanismo de ajuste de carbono na fronteira da UE e introduzir um sistema de comércio de emissões, segundo o Materiaintel. A iniciativa tem como objetivo ajudar as empresas locais a cumprir os padrões climáticos internacionais e converter a pressão da transição rumo às emissões líquidas zero até 2050 em competitividade de longo prazo. Estrutura existente da taxa de carbono Taiwan já opera um sistema oficial de taxa de carbono que abrange grandes empresas industriais e companhias de energia cujas emissões anuais superam 25.000 toneladas de CO2 equivalente. A alíquota base é de NT$ 300 por tonelada, enquanto empresas com planos de descarbonização aprovados podem se qualificar para alíquotas preferenciais de NT$ 50 ou NT$ 100. As regras entraram em vigor em janeiro de 2025, e os primeiros pagamentos referentes às emissões de 2025 estão previstos para maio de 2026. Implicações para importações e para o aço Um equivalente doméstico do mecanismo da UE também aplicaria uma taxa de carbono sobre materiais importados, medida que deve ter efeito significativo sobre a indústria do aço. Exposição à regulamentação europeia Os exportadores taiwaneses enfrentam um desafio adicional em sua interação com as regras europeias. Segundo a Administração de Mudanças Climáticas de Taiwan, cerca de 2.600 empresas locais estão sujeitas ao CBAM da UE, e os produtos de aço respondem pela maior parte das exportações para a UE, com aproximadamente 2,8 milhões de toneladas por ano. A regulamentação da UE permite que os pagamentos de carbono feitos no país de origem sejam creditados contra o número de certificados CBAM que um importador europeu precisa adquirir. Isso exige comprovação clara dos valores efetivamente pagos, como a alíquota preferencial de NT$ 50 em vez da alíquota padrão de NT$ 300. Quando uma usina repassa os custos ao comprador por meio do preço do material, o importador da UE paga parte dos custos de carbono na fatura do fornecedor e o restante por meio de certificados CBAM. O GMK Center informou anteriormente que o governo do Reino Unido publicou números indicativos para o cálculo de seu CBAM nacional, que entra em vigor em 2027. Uma análise desses números indica que o sistema britânico será consideravelmente mais brando e mais barato para os importadores de aço do que o mecanismo comparável da UE. Este relatório fornece uma análise aprofundada do mercado global do aço, cobrindo tamanho de mercado, crescimento, demanda, oferta, fluxos comerciais, preços, cenário competitivo e previsões até 2035. O estudo é projetado para fabricantes, distribuidores, importadores, exportadores, investidores, equipes de compras, consultores e equipes de estratégia que precisam de uma visão consistente e orientada por dados da dinâmica do mercado e de uma definição analítica transparente do escopo do produto. Cobertura do Produto Este relatório abrange o mercado de aço, uma liga ferrosa composta principalmente de ferro e carbono, com diferentes graus definidos pela composição e pelo processo de fabricação. Abrange todo o espectro de produtos siderúrgicos obtidos na produção primária (fusão e refino) e no processamento secundário (laminação, conformação, revestimento), comercializados nas formas de commodity a granel e de semiacabados. A análise concentra-se na oferta, na demanda, no comércio e na dinâmica de preços das principais categorias de produtos nas grandes regiões produtoras e consumidoras. Incluídos - AÇO-CARBONO E AÇO LIGA (INCLUINDO AÇO INOXIDÁVEL) - PRODUTOS SEMIACABADOS (LINGOTES, TARUGOS, PLACAS) - PRODUTOS PLANOS LAMINADOS (BOBINAS/CHAPAS LAMINADAS A QUENTE E A FRIO) - PRODUTOS LONGOS (BARRAS, VERGALHÕES, PERFIS, FIO-MÁQUINA) - AÇO REVESTIDO E GALVANIZADO (POR EXEMPLO, ZINCADO, FOLHA DE FLANDRES) - DETERMINADOS TUBOS, DUTOS E PERFIS OCOS DE AÇO - FORMAS PRIMÁRIAS PROVENIENTES DE CONVERSORES A OXIGÊNIO (BOF) E FORNOS ELÉTRICOS A ARCO (EAF) Excluídos - MINÉRIO DE FERRO, FERRO-GUSA E FERRO REDUZIDO DIRETO (DRI) - FERROLIGAS E OUTRAS LIGAS-MÃE - ESTRUTURAS E COMPONENTES METÁLICOS ACABADOS - SUCATA E RESÍDUOS DE AÇO - PRODUTOS SIDERÚRGICOS ESPECIAIS, COMO TRILHOS OU MATERIAL FERROVIÁRIO - FERRAMENTAS, CUTELARIA E OUTROS BENS DE CONSUMO ACABADOS FEITOS DE AÇO Cobertura do Relatório e Módulos Analíticos O relatório combina a base padrão de estatísticas de mercado com capítulos estratégicos úteis para planejamento comercial, decisões de sourcing, entrada no mercado, monitoramento de concorrentes e priorização de portfólio. - Tamanho do mercado, desenvolvimento histórico e previsão até 2035 - Arquitetura da demanda por aplicação, grupo de clientes e comportamento do comprador - Estrutura de oferta, papel da produção quando aplicável, sourcing e restrições da cadeia de valor - Exportações, importações, balança comercial, dependência de importação e principais corredores comerciais - Níveis de preço, corredores de preço, efeitos de especificação e lógica comercial de preços - Panorama competitivo, presença de empresas, foco no portfólio de produtos e posicionamento estratégico - Perfis de países para relatórios mundiais e regionais, com o papel da produção declarado apenas quando relevante Framework de Segmentação O mercado é segmentado em grupos relevantes para decisões, de modo que os impulsionadores de demanda, a lógica de preços, as restrições de oferta e as posições competitivas possam ser comparados dentro do mesmo quadro analítico. - Por aplicação: Construção civil, Automotivo, Máquinas e equipamentos, Construção naval, Energia, Eletrodomésticos, Embalagens, Infraestrutura - Por posição na cadeia de valor: Mineração de minério de ferro, Carvão metalúrgico (coqueificável), Produção de ferro-gusa, Produção de aço (BOF/EAF), Lingotamento contínuo, Laminação a quente/a frio, Revestimento, Fabricação e transformação - artigo.texto: Data center approvals could remain paused in Texas until legislators pass new state laws next year if Democrat Gina Hinojosa keeps her campaign promises after winning the governor’s race in a stunning victory Tuesday. Her statements on the campaign trail went beyond Gov. Greg Abbott’s current freeze on environmental permitting and grid connections for data centers during an audit period expected to be completed this year. Grassroots opposition to data centers has mounted in communities across Texas, where critics across the political spectrum expressed concerns about the almost unbelievable projections for how much power the facilities could draw from the state’s grid and the unknown amount of water they would need to operate in a state with serious drought concerns. Hinojosa attacked Abbott’s handling of the matter. She called for a data center moratorium to last until the Texas Legislature meets in January to pass “real protections so Texans can have a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into their communities.” “When I am governor I will issue a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals until laws can be passed by the Legislature to protect Texans,” Hinojosa said in an Oct. 22 video posted to X. Hinojosa’s plan for data centers The governor-elect during her campaign outlined a slate of priorities for lawmakers that included requiring data center operators to hire union workers, protecting communities’ water supplies and stopping data center companies from using nondisclosure agreements that make it harder for the public to track project developments. Similar to Abbott, Hinojosa also said she would push to ensure Texans wouldn’t pay more for electricity because of data centers, and to stop tax subsidies that were depriving the state of billions in sales tax revenue. “We can have economic development and we can have protections for Texans. These things are not mutually exclusive,” she said in a September interview with Politico. Hinojosa will be working with a Democrat-dominated Texas House. She takes office Jan. 19. Abbott slowly cracked down on the facilities, turning from a politician who in November heralded Texas as the “epicenter of AI development” to one who, starting in August, began issuing pauses on data center approvals at the state grid and then the environmental permitting agency so information about the facilities could be audited and collected. The audit by grid regulators and operators was expected to last until December. Abbott had also demanded that officials collect information on tax incentives and water use, whether data centers were bringing their own power or water supplies and whether data centers were taking measures to reduce impacts on the neighbors for light and noise pollution. How that information would be used remained to be seen, but Abbott had demanded data centers pay for their own electrical infrastructure — a process being worked out by state regulators — in addition to using water-efficient technology. He promised to pursue getting rid of tax breaks for data centers during the legislative session. Data center-related donors, meanwhile, gave Abbott some $9 million since July 2025, the Texas Tribune reported. And in October, environmental and community advocates identified some environmental permits related to data centers they said had gotten approval anyway despite Abbott’s pause, forcing the permitting agency to shut down its online filing system. Some county officials had also expressed frustration with their lack of authority under current state law to regulate data centers. “Real anger in communities” Data Center Watch, which researches opposition to data centers in the United States, in a Tuesday analysis said the state “offers one of the clearest examples of data center regulation becoming an election issue.” The group found that 43% of the 74 gubernatorial candidates they studied in 36 states supported a data center moratorium or ban. “We’ve just seen real anger in communities — big, small, in solid red counties and in deep blue counties alike,” said Kathryn Guerra, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality watchdog campaign director for Public Citizen, which identified the errant permit approvals. “What happened yesterday just seems to have been a reflection of that anger,” she added. “We’re in a position now to listen to Texans and help advance solutions to those concerns that they have raised over the past year with the massive influx of data centers that Texas has seen.” Jess Heck, director of government affairs in Texas for the industry association Data Center Coalition, said in a statement that data centers could continue to advance job creation and strengthen the state’s economy through investments in communities and tax revenue generation. “The data center industry is committed to advancing America’s digital infrastructure, including here in the Lone Star State, as well as supporting energy reliability and affordability and promoting long-term, responsible economic development,” Heck said. The coalition, Heck continued, “looks forward to working with state leadership along with local officials, stakeholders, and Texas communities to continue building trust and supporting responsible data center growth.” Elon Musk, who founded artificial intelligence company xAI and supported Abbott, posted on X: “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.”

artigo.texto: Publicidade 5 Nov (Reuters) – O índice Nasdaq Composite encerrou a sessão de quinta-feira com forte queda, registrando sua maior baixa em um único dia nos últimos 19 meses e confirmando que se encontrava em fase de correção, à medida que as fabricantes de chips afundaram devido aos temores de uma regulamentação mais rígida em relação à IA, após os democratas terem conquistado o controle do Congresso dos EUA. As vitórias democratas na terça-feira, inclusive em Estados onde a oposição a novos data centers tem se intensificado, alimentaram preocupações de que uma regulamentação mais rígida possa desacelerar a expansão da infraestrutura de IA, que ajudou a elevar as ações a níveis recordes neste ano. A Nvidia caiu mais de 9%, enquanto o índice Philadelphia SE Semiconductor despencou mais de 12%. A onda de vendas evaporou US$3 trilhões em valor de mercado das empresas do S&P 500. O Nasdaq Composite registrou sua maior queda diária desde o anúncio das tarifas do “Dia da Libertação” do presidente Donald Trump, em abril de 2025. O índice também confirmou uma correção técnica, ou seja, uma queda de 10% em relação ao seu fechamento recorde de 6 de outubro. “Os investidores parecem estar reconhecendo que alguns membros recém-eleitos do Congresso e governadores pretendem desacelerar o ritmo do desenvolvimento da infraestrutura de IA”, disse Melissa Brown, diretora global de pesquisa de decisões de investimento da SimCorp. Continua depois da publicidade “Embora pareça improvável que consigam interromper totalmente esse processo, qualquer desaceleração geraria preocupações, pois o crescimento da IA tem dependido, em grande parte, da rápida construção da infraestrutura de apoio.” Embora as fabricantes de chips que fornecem componentes para data centers de IA tenham estado entre as que mais caíram, outras ações de grande capitalização do setor de tecnologia também perderam terreno após a alta registrada na quarta-feira. A Meta caiu 4%, enquanto a Amazon.com e a Alphabet caíram 2,2% cada uma. As empresas de data centers IREN e Applied Digital desabaram mais de 14%, enquanto a CoreWeave registrou queda de quase 10%. Continua depois da publicidade As empresas de serviços públicos e fornecedoras de equipamentos com exposição à IA, GE Vernova e Constellation Energy, caíram 7,5% e 2,5%, respectivamente. A Tesla e a SpaceX, ambas de Elon Musk, registraram quedas. Musk gastou quase US$0,5 bilhão apoiando candidatos republicanos nas eleições de meio de mandato. A Qualcomm tombou 9,5% depois que a fabricante de chips ficou aquém das estimativas de Wall Street para as vendas de chips para smartphones no quarto trimestre. Continua depois da publicidade “Parece que estamos na fase de capitulação das ações beneficiadas pelos investimentos em data centers, especialmente as de semicondutores”, disse Jed Ellerbroek, gestor de portfólio da Argent Capital Management. “Mas acho que a magnitude desses movimentos é exagerada.” O S&P 500 recuou 4,36%, encerrando o pregão em 7.353,73 pontos. O Nasdaq tombou 5,52%, para 24.315,00 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones Industrial Average caiu 3,44%, para 51.523,06 pontos. Continua depois da publicidade Após a onda de vendas desta quinta-feira, o S&P 500 continua com alta de 7,4% em 2026, enquanto o Nasdaq registra alta de 4,6%. Na quarta-feira, o S&P 500 registrou seu maior ganho percentual em um único dia nos últimos três meses, à medida que a incerteza política diminuiu, impulsionando o apetite pelo risco. Alguns analistas afirmaram que um governo dividido em Washington poderia levar a menos mudanças legislativas drásticas e tornar mais difícil chegar a um acordo sobre os gastos fiscais. A presidente do Federal Reserve de Cleveland, Beth Hammack, e o presidente do Fed de Richmond, Thomas Barkin, sugeriram a possibilidade de futuros aumentos nas taxas em comentários feitos nesta quinta-feira. O foco estará nos dados de empregos não agrícolas dos EUA referentes a outubro, que serão divulgados na sexta-feira. Atualmente, os operadores esperam que o Fed aumente as taxas no próximo mês, após a alta de setembro.

Kampong Speu – Hok Poeun remembers the chemical smell of smoke that drifted through her village in July, when a battery storage facility caught fire. The haze lingered for days over Toul Sambor village in Kampong Speu province. Her grandsons fell ill with respiratory infections and were hospitalized for a week, she said. The Ministry of Environment determined that improper storage of lithium batteries caused the fire, which injured a few workers, and found high levels of air pollutants. The ministry fined the company that owns the facility, Xinshengsheng Metal Materials Industrial Park, and will require it to relocate the facility. But Poeun is still worried. Next to the ruins of the storage facility, a factory that residents say smelts used batteries is still operating. “If they continue running the smelting factory nonstop like this, how are we supposed to live here?” the 53-year-old grandmother said. Residents of Toul Sambor village in Damnak Raing commune have lived in fear of the factory, just 60 meters (about 200 feet) from their homes, since it began operating early this year. They say it smelts used lead-acid batteries, which the government classifies as hazardous waste and bans from import, in a process that can release lead, a toxic metal with no known safe level of exposure. Residents say no one consulted them before the factory opened, and they are asking why it was allowed in a residential area — and why it keeps running despite the fire and the high pollution levels the ministry documented. Fearing long-term harm to their health, environment and livelihoods, they are demanding the facilities be permanently removed. ‘We Know We’ve Been Exposed’ In October 2025, the Council for the Development of Cambodia approved a $6.3 million investment by Xinshengsheng Metal Materials Industrial Park to build a metallurgical and processing factory in Toul Sambor. The council said the factory would create 455 jobs but did not specify what metals it would process. Residents told CamboJA News in September that there was no public consultation before the industrial park was built. CamboJA News was unable to verify whether an environmental impact assessment, which Cambodian law requires for smelting operations, was conducted for the factory and industrial park. The battery factory began operating early this year, according to Toul Sambor village chief Khut Phoeun. He said he learned the factory would process battery materials only after supplies had been delivered to the building. Phoeun and several other residents said the factory smelts used lead-acid batteries mostly from motorbikes and cars for recycling. The factory shares an entrance with the burned facility under a Xinshengsheng sign, CamboJA News observed, and a photo of it accompanied the council’s approval of the company’s project. About 20 Cambodian and foreign workers are employed at the factory, Phoeun said. Without proper controls, the process releases lead fumes and dust that settle on soil and surfaces, where people can inhale or swallow them, according to a 2017 World Health Organization report. Lead can damage the brain, kidneys and cardiovascular system, the report says. Young children absorb about half the lead they swallow, compared with about 10% for adults, and exposure during pregnancy may be linked to reduced fetal growth, preterm birth and miscarriage. Phorng, 51, whose chicken farm shares a boundary wall with the factory, said the plant lacked overhead exhaust stacks, so fumes leaked through its walls and corrugated iron roof into his farm during smelting. During the fire, he lost thousands of chickens and a motorbike, for which he later received compensation from Xinshengsheng’s chairman Zhang Jingchuan, he said. When the factory began operating and producing a foul odor, villagers demanded that the village and commune chiefs inspect the site, several of them told CamboJA News. Phoeun said he contacted the company over the smell about a month before the fire. An environment official also came to seek a resolution, and the factory owner promised to modify its operations and do more testing if the odor persisted, the village chief said. That month, ventilation pipes were installed, which he said improved the smell and reduced complaints. “Toxic substances in the body don’t cause immediate death like a chicken dying suddenly,” said Phoeun. “We know we’ve been exposed, but we haven’t filed any lawsuits.” Xinshengsheng did not respond to a request for comment. artigo.texto: A OpenAI anunciou nesta quinta-feira (5) novas diretrizes para conquistar o apoio de comunidades à construção de data centers nos Estados Unidos. A iniciativa ocorre após vitórias democratas nas eleições de meio de mandato, marcadas pela oposição à expansão dessas instalações. A empresa promete abandonar acordos de confidencialidade com autoridades públicas e divulgar informações sobre os impactos dos projetos. Também destaca a geração de empregos, incluindo uma instalação em Ohio que deve criar 2.500 vagas permanentes. A resistência ao setor ganhou força nas urnas, com vitórias de candidatos favoráveis a restrições em Texas, Geórgia e Ohio. Segundo o Ballotpedia, 40 das 41 propostas submetidas a votação direta tiveram resultados contrários aos data centers, aumentando a preocupação dos investidores. Uma apuração exclusiva do portal Vero Notícias revela que, mesmo após o Tribunal de Contas de Minas Gerais (TCE-MG) se posicionar contra a concessão do serviço de coleta de lixo de 31 municípios do estado, o serviço foi leiloado em bloco por R$ 2,32 bilhões a duas empresas do grupo Solví, do empresário Carlos Villa. A disputa não contou com concorrentes. A concessão foi promovida pelo Consórcio Intermunicipal Multifinalitário do Centro-Oeste Mineiro (CIAS), que reúne 31 municípios, prevê um contrato de 30 anos de transporte, tratamento e destinação do lixo, sem incluir a coleta domiciliar. O CIAS possui histórico de licitações anuladas. A MP 1.399/2026 fixou o Imposto Seletivo em 8% para a maior parte dos vinhos e em 16% para fortificados e bebidas de maior teor alcoólico. A cobrança começará em 2 de fevereiro de 2027. O tributo atingirá produtos nacionais e importados, incluindo vinhos europeus. O setor avalia que a cobrança pode limitar os benefícios da redução gradual das tarifas prevista no acordo entre Mercosul e União Europeia. Os Estados Unidos anunciaram nesta quinta-feira (5) sanções contra empresas dos setores petrolífero e tecnológico ligadas a Cuba. A lista também inclui a filha da presidente do conglomerado militar cubano GAESA. Pela primeira vez, foram atingidas as chinesas CEIEC e Beijing H&C Technologies, acusadas por Washington de fornecer equipamentos de defesa e segurança a Havana. Operadoras de navios-tanque também estão entre os alvos. O dólar comercial subiu 0,67% nesta quinta-feira (5) e fechou a R$ 5,489. O Ibovespa caiu 0,82%, aos 166.191,45 pontos, pressionado pela piora do ambiente nas bolsas americanas. A venda de ações de inteligência artificial, semicondutores e data centers ampliou a aversão ao risco. Investidores também avaliaram a possibilidade de maior fiscalização do setor após a vitória democrata no Congresso dos EUA. O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (5) que a proibição das bets reduzirá a arrecadação prevista para 2027. O governo precisará ajustar a proposta de Orçamento para acomodar essa perda. Entre janeiro de 2025 e setembro de 2026, a tributação das apostas rendeu R$ 15,3 bilhões. Durigan avalia que o dinheiro antes destinado aos jogos migrará para outras atividades, compensando receitas em outros tributos.

TOWN HALL NOTES | Smithtown is considering extending its moratorium on battery energy storage systems for another 12 months while the town reviews state fire safety rules and guidance. The Town Board will hold a public hearing on the proposal at 2 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, in the Victor T. Liss Board Room at Smithtown Town Hall, 99 W. Main St. The board first adopted the moratorium in September 2024 and most recently extended it in May 2026, according to the town’s public notice. The proposed extension would give Smithtown more time to review recommendations from the state’s Inter-Agency Fire Safety Working Group, updates to New York’s fire safety code and a battery storage guidebook from the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority. If adopted, the extension would take effect when the law is filed with the New York secretary of state. It would expire 12 months later unless the board extends it again. The town’s existing zoning variance procedures would still apply. Top: An aerial view of Main Street in downtown Smithtown. (GLI/Andrew Theodorakis, file)

artigo.texto: Anchor company named for Project Red Clay data center in Lowndes County MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - California-based AI infrastructure company Lambda announced Wednesday it will anchor Project Red Clay, a 2,200-acre artificial intelligence data center planned for northeastern Lowndes County. Lambda is committing $33.1 billion to the campus. County officials say the deal will bring more than 1,000 construction jobs, 225 full-time jobs and more than $1.6 billion directly to Lowndes County Public Schools through 2049. Lambda says it will protect ratepayers and reduce water usage. Citizen group Protect Lowndes County, the Alabama Rivers Alliance and others filed a lawsuit against the Lowndes County Commission on Tuesday afternoon. The lawsuit claims commissioners violated Alabama’s Open Meetings Act and Open Records Act to “fast track” a multibillion-dollar tax abatement package for developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure. The plaintiffs are asking a circuit judge to declare the commission’s votes void. Opponents also raise concerns about resource strain. They note the facility will demand up to 1,500 megawatts of power from Alabama Power and hundreds of thousands of gallons of water daily. Another lawsuit filed against the Lowndes County Commission is still pending. Construction on the data center is expected to take about five years and could begin as early as January. The site is off Highway 80, a few miles west of the Montgomery airport. Not reading this story on the WSFA News App? Get news alerts FASTER and FREE in the Apple App Store and the Google Play Store! artigo.texto: Capacidade de armazenamento de energia de novo tipo da China chega a 167 GW/435 GWh A China tinha 167 GW/435 GWh de armazenamento de energia de novo tipo em operação no fim de setembro de 2026, um crescimento de 63% em relação ao ano anterior, segundo dados da Administração Nacional de Energia (NEA) divulgados em 30 de outubro. A NEA apresentou os números durante seu briefing trimestral sobre o desenvolvimento energético nacional. Essa categoria abrange tecnologias eletroquímicas, de ar comprimido e outras tecnologias emergentes de armazenamento, excluindo o bombeamento hidrelétrico tradicional. Frente aos 135,93 GW/351,12 GWh registrados no fechamento de 2025, os novos dados apontam para um ganho líquido de cerca de 31 GW/84 GWh nos primeiros nove meses de 2026. Duração maior e utilização mais alta A duração média do armazenamento subiu para 2,61 horas, cerca de 0,27 hora a mais que um ano antes. As horas de utilização equivalentes chegaram a cerca de 915 horas no período de nove meses, aproximadamente 10 horas acima do mesmo intervalo de 2025. Segundo a NEA, esses ganhos sugerem que a configuração e o uso do sistema estão mudando gradualmente junto com o crescimento da capacidade, e não que a capacidade instalada esteja se expandindo isoladamente. A agência atribuiu a rápida expansão do setor a políticas governamentais, inovação tecnológica, cadeias de suprimentos industriais e à crescente demanda por flexibilidade no sistema elétrico. Expansão de renováveis eleva a demanda por armazenamento A capacidade de geração eólica e solar somada superou 2,01 TW no fim de setembro, cerca de 48,7% da capacidade instalada total de energia. À medida que a geração renovável variável cresce, o armazenamento se torna cada vez mais necessário para absorver o excedente de eletricidade, deslocar a geração para períodos de maior demanda e fornecer serviços de rede com resposta rápida. A composição do mercado também está mudando. Dados oficiais de 2025 mostraram que as instalações de armazenamento independente representavam 51,2% das instalações acumuladas de novo tipo. Projetos de 100 MW ou mais respondiam por 72% da capacidade instalada, enquanto sistemas com duração de pelo menos quatro horas representavam 27,6%. As baterias de íons de lítio permaneceram dominantes, com aproximadamente 96% da capacidade instalada de novo tipo, embora ar comprimido, baterias de fluxo e outras tecnologias estejam ampliando gradualmente sua participação. Reformas e a meta para 2030 As reformas de mercado provavelmente reforçarão esses padrões. A China vem construindo estruturas que permitem aos operadores de armazenamento independente gerar receita com comercialização de eletricidade, serviços auxiliares e remuneração por capacidade, reduzindo de forma constante a dependência de obrigações de armazenamento vinculadas a projetos renováveis. O 15º Plano Quinquenal para o desenvolvimento do sistema elétrico estabelece a meta de 300 GW de armazenamento de energia de novo tipo até 2030, com maior peso para sistemas de maior duração, capacidades de formação de rede e melhor eficiência operacional. O papel do armazenamento nas redes regionais A contribuição crescente do armazenamento já é evidente em redes regionais com abundância de renováveis. No oeste da Mongólia Interior, o operador da rede relatou 20,23 GW/70,47 GWh de capacidade de armazenamento em operação em outubro. Durante o despacho de emergência, o armazenamento forneceu até 12,25 GW, equivalente a 33% da demanda de eletricidade da rede naquele momento. Exemplos como esse mostram como o armazenamento pode oferecer capacidade substancial de balanceamento de curto prazo em sistemas elétricos com alta penetração de renováveis. Para outros países que ampliam a geração eólica e solar, a expansão chinesa oferece lições em fabricação de armazenamento em larga escala, integração à rede e despacho centralizado. Este relatório fornece uma análise aprofundada do mercado de acumuladores elétricos na China, cobrindo tamanho de mercado, crescimento, demanda, oferta, fluxos comerciais, preços, cenário competitivo e previsões até 2035. O estudo é projetado para fabricantes, distribuidores, importadores, exportadores, investidores, equipes de compras, consultores e equipes de estratégia que precisam de uma visão consistente e orientada por dados da dinâmica do mercado e de uma definição analítica transparente do escopo do produto. Cobertura do Produto O mercado de acumuladores elétricos abrange baterias recarregáveis que convertem e armazenam energia elétrica por meio de reações eletroquímicas reversíveis, incluindo seus separadores. O escopo compreende todo o conjunto de acumuladores elétricos nas químicas de chumbo-ácido, à base de níquel e à base de lítio, em aplicações de partida, tração e estacionárias. Incluídos - Acumuladores de chumbo-ácido - Acumuladores de níquel-cádmio - Acumuladores de níquel-ferro - Acumuladores de níquel-hidreto metálico - Acumuladores de íons de lítio - Acumuladores de lítio-polímero - Acumuladores de chumbo-ácido de partida para motores a pistão Excluídos - Pilhas primárias não recarregáveis - Capacitores e supercapacitores - Carregadores de bateria - Sistemas de gerenciamento de baterias - Células a combustível Cobertura do Relatório e Módulos Analíticos O relatório combina a base padrão de estatísticas de mercado com capítulos estratégicos úteis para planejamento comercial, decisões de sourcing, entrada no mercado, monitoramento de concorrentes e priorização de portfólio. - Tamanho do mercado, desenvolvimento histórico e previsão até 2035 - Arquitetura da demanda por aplicação, grupo de clientes e comportamento do comprador - Estrutura de oferta, papel da produção quando aplicável, sourcing e restrições da cadeia de valor - Exportações, importações, balança comercial, dependência de importação e principais corredores comerciais - Níveis de preço, corredores de preço, efeitos de especificação e lógica comercial de preços - Panorama competitivo, presen

artigo.texto: BYD dobra vendas em outubro com alta de 137,6% no Brasil Empresa ampliou participação no mercado nacional de 4,2% para 9,7% e quer liderar o setor até 2030 A BYD emplacou 24.114 veículos no Brasil em outubro de 2026, alta de 137,6% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. O resultado representa mais que o dobro das vendas registradas 1 ano antes, quando a fabricante chinesa inaugurou sua fábrica em Camaçari (BA). A participação da empresa no mercado nacional passou de 4,2% para 9,7% no período. No acumulado de janeiro a outubro, a montadora comercializou 193.227 veículos, crescimento superior a 120% na comparação com os 10 primeiros meses de 2025. Os dados foram divulgados pela empresa na 2ª feira (2.nov.2026). As vendas no varejo somaram 14.487 unidades em outubro, o equivalente a 12,7% do segmento e à 2ª posição no ranking nacional. Já as vendas diretas alcançaram 9.627 veículos, avanço de aproximadamente 600% em relação ao mesmo mês do ano passado. A BYD ficou na 5ª colocação nessa modalidade. Entre os modelos da fabricante, o Dolphin Mini foi o carro mais vendido do Brasil no varejo em outubro, com 5.841 emplacamentos. O King, por sua vez, liderou pelo 2º mês consecutivo o segmento de sedãs no varejo, com 1.343 unidades e participação de 32,2% na categoria. A expansão das vendas acompanha o crescimento da operação industrial da BYD na Bahia. Pouco mais de 1 ano depois da inauguração, a fábrica de Camaçari ultrapassou 150 mil veículos produzidos e alcançou mais de 9.500 empregos diretos, segundo a companhia. BYD quer liderança O vice-presidente sênior da BYD no Brasil, Alexandre Baldy, afirmou que a empresa pretende liderar o mercado automotivo brasileiro até 2030. A fabricante também declarou que continuará ampliando a produção na unidade baiana. “Muita gente duvidou da força da BYD e da nossa capacidade de disputar espaço com as fabricantes mais tradicionais do Brasil. Hoje, os resultados mostram que estávamos certos ao acreditar no potencial desse mercado e investir no país. É especialmente simbólico alcançar esses números justamente em outubro, quando completamos 1 ano de operação da nossa fábrica em Camaçari”, afirma Alexandre Baldy.

artigo.texto: Voters delivered a stern rebuke of data centers in ballot propositions across the country on Tuesday. Except in one tiny North Dakota town. The citizens of Harwood, who number about 940, shot down a measure that would have given residents a greater say in how large projects, such as AI data centers, are constructed in the town. The vote wasn't exactly close, either. Some 325 voted against the measure, compared to 105 who voted for it, according to the North Dakota Secretary of State's office. Of all 45 data-center-related propositions on the ballot across the country on Tuesday, Harwood stood out as the sole constituency in support of them. The other 44 fell on the anti-data-center side, according to Redbud Consulting, a ballot tracking firm. And for residents of Harwood, the issue is germane. A $3 billion AI data center equal in size to 17 football fields is under construction in the community's backyard. The company building it hopes to employ 200 people — a number equal to about 20% of the city's population. "It's frustrating," Mark Coolidge, a 59-year-old resident who voted for the measure, told Business Insider. "We are the people that have to live with this type of industry as a neighbor," said Mike Swartz, a 47-year-old resident who advocated for the proposition. "Do we not have any say in what we want for the community some have vested decades into calling their home?" In an interview, Blake Hankey, the mayor of Harwood, said he didn't support the measure. He said the language of the proposition was imprecise and that some of the stipulations "would have been financially burdensome to a city our size." "This amendment to the home rule charter wasn't strictly aimed at data centers," he said. "It was any kind of business coming to town." He also said the proposition wasn't a referendum on data centers. "It wasn't if there was going to be a moratorium," he added. The proposition, should it have passed, would not have affected the existing data center, which is set to be completed next year. Rather, it would have applied to all future construction projects that met a criteria of scale. For instance, a new gas station wouldn't have qualified, but a new large data center would be subject to independent assessments and mandatory public hearings. Swartz said the measure was necessary because people in town were "blindsided" by how quickly the current data center was approved. "Many in town didn't even know what that was or meant," he said. "Yet it only took 21 days from the time it was announced to the time construction began." Hankey, who said he signed a non-disclosure agreement with Applied Digital, the company building the data center, described the decision as one he and the city council had to make quickly, lest neighboring Fargo got the contract first. "I don't regret signing it," he said of the NDA. "Had I not, that data center would almost certainly be in the city of Fargo right now, without any kind of sales tax or property tax for our community." As major developers, including SpaceX, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, OpenAI, and others, seek new AI data centers to power their products, they've encountered stiff resistance at town halls and city councils across the United States. Americans worry about the environmental impact, about electric bills, or the water supply. Many just don't like AI. After a series of contentious city council meetings in Harwood, including one in which anti-data-center protesters were ejected by sheriffs, Coolidge said Swartz gathered enough signatures to formally put the proposition on the ballot. Voters ultimately shot it down, Swartz and Coolidge said, in part because people in town disagreed with whether the measure would also apply to smaller buildings and businesses, rather than just large ones. Applied Digital did not respond to a request for comment on Wednesday. "It's all about money," Coolidge said. "They could give a rip about us as citizens."

artigo.texto: Florida utility regulators rejected Duke Energy Florida’s proposal to meet the requirements of a new state law intended to shield ratepayers from the costs of data centers. The Public Service Commission voted against Duke’s proposal to create a new large load tariff designation for data centers in the first test of the law pushed in the spring by Gov. Ron DeSantis intended to ensure customers won’t bear the additional costs brought by new facilities that power artificial intelligence. Commissioner Gabriella Passidomo Smith said the new law “made it clear that large load customers must bear their own full cost of service without shifting those costs to other ratepayers.” Smith added that Duke can serve the large-scale data centers, which require vast amounts of energy to power the burgeoning AI field while still following the new law. Brooke Ward, Florida State Director for Food & Water Watch, called the vote “a victory for affordability and testament to the importance of laws that put people above corporations.” But she added the state needs more affordable energy legislation to “ensure a more equitable energy future for all Floridians.” The new law (SB 484) requires the PSC to develop what are known as “tariffs” and service requirements to “reasonably ensure that each large load customer bears its own full cost of service and that such cost is not shifted to the general body of ratepayers.” That would include costs related to connecting to electric systems and increased power transmission and generation costs. The measure reinforces the ability of local governments to refuse to build data centers in their jurisdictions. But it also allows city and county governments to enter into non-disclosure agreements with tech companies for up to 12 months, which would hide data center proposals from the public during that time. Duke will have to refile a new tariffs proposal. The commission determined Duke’s proposed tariffs excluded certain large load customers who would otherwise qualify under the law’s definition. Commissioners also found Duke failed to provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate that its existing rate schedules, together with the proposed contractual and financial protections, would reasonably ensure that each large load customer bears the full cost of its electric service.

artigo.texto: Battery Storage, Hybrid Projects Dominate Renewable Auctions in Q3 2026 Agencies auctioned 28 GW of renewable energy capacity in 9M 2026 November 5, 2026 Follow Mercom India on WhatsApp for exclusive updates on clean energy news and insights Government agencies issued tenders for 21 GW of renewable energy capacity and auctioned 12 GW across energy storage, hybrid, large-scale solar, wind, manufacturing, green hydrogen, and rooftop solar projects in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, according to Mercom India’s newly released Q3 and 9M 2026 India Renewable Energy Procurement and Demand Report. Wind projects led auction activity with 3.2 GW, followed by battery energy storage at 2.8 GW, hybrid projects at 2.5 GW, manufacturing at 1.9 GW, large-scale solar at 1.2 GW, and rooftop solar at 51.2 MW. Together, battery energy storage and hybrid projects accounted for 45.2% of auctioned capacity, suggesting buyers are placing greater emphasis on flexible supply and the timing of power delivery. Energy Storage Led Tenders in 9M Agencies issued approximately 66 GW of renewable energy tenders and auctioned 28 GW of capacity during the first nine months (9M) of 2026. Energy storage was the largest tendered segment, accounting for 40% of the total tendered capacity. Wind accounted for 22% of total auctioned capacity in 9M 2026, making it the second-largest auctioned segment after hybrid projects. The relatively strong auction activity indicates robust renewable energy offtake, alongside new tender issuance. The growing share of storage procurement reflects the increasing importance of integrating renewable energy with flexible capacity to improve grid reliability and meet peak electricity demand. Tendering design also reflected buyers’ peak power procurement requirements. Tenders specified storage duration, firm delivery, peak-period supply, and complementary renewable generation. A substantial portion of newly issued capacity was pending auction at the end of Q3 2026, indicating scope for increased auction activity as these programs progress through the procurement process. In the first half (1H) of 2026, agencies in India issued tenders for 44.1 GW and auctioned 16.3 GW of renewable energy capacity according to the India Renewable Energy Procurement and Demand Report. Solar Tenders Large-scale solar remained a significant part of procurement activity, with approximately 14 GW tendered and 4 GW auctioned in 9M 2026. The wide gap shows that solar tender issuance continued to run well ahead of projects reaching the auction stage, with transmission availability, land, tariff expectations, bid conditions, and buyer commitments affecting the pace of conversion. Rooftop solar tenders totaled 2 GW, while nearly 1 GW was auctioned during the period. Procurement remained driven primarily by residential, government, and utility-led rooftop programs. Large residential and government rooftop programs in Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan, and Tripura supported tender activity. However, most of these projects remained pending auction at the end of September. “The volume of tenders tells only part of the story. The bigger question is how much of that capacity moves through auctions, power purchase agreements, financing, transmission connectivity, and commissioning. With a large pipeline still awaiting award, the rate at which projects move forward will be an important measure of actual renewable energy demand in the coming quarters,” said Raj Prabhu, CEO of Mercom Capital Group. Other Tenders and Auctions Renewable energy manufacturing tenders totaled 5 GW during 9M 2026, while 2 GW was auctioned. Auction activity was largely concentrated in procurement processes initiated earlier, reflecting continued demand for domestic manufacturing capacity and the progression of previously issued tenders. Green hydrogen procurement remained limited during the period, with activity focused on a small number of tenders and only one auction. Transmission tendering also remained active during the period, with agencies issuing tenders for interstate and intrastate transmission networks, substations, high-voltage transmission lines, network augmentation, and renewable energy evacuation infrastructure. Projects awarded during Q3 also supported transmission infrastructure for renewable energy zones, pumped storage connectivity, and emerging demand from green hydrogen and green ammonia projects. Mercom India’s analysis indicates that renewable energy procurement is increasingly being driven by power delivery requirements rather than capacity additions alone. Storage and hybrid projects are gaining prominence, and the gap between tendered and auctioned capacity continues to grow. Buyer requirements, transmission availability, project financing, and commercial viability continue to determine how quickly the tendered pipeline translates into awarded projects. The India Renewable Energy Procurement and Demand Report covers all facets of India’s renewable energy tendering and auction activity. For the complete report, visit: https://www.mercomindia.com/product/india-renewable-energy-procurement-9M-2026

artigo.texto: China has connected the world’s largest liquid-air energy storage facility to the power grid, marking a significant step toward overcoming one of renewable energy’s biggest challenges: storing electricity for use when the sun is not shining and the wind is not blowing. The 60-megawatt facility, located in Golmud City in northwest China’s Qinghai Province, officially connected to the grid on October 30, 2026. With a storage capacity of 600 megawatt-hours, the installation can deliver electricity continuously for up to ten hours. Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries, the system uses ordinary atmospheric air to store energy. Surplus electricity from renewable sources is used to cool air to approximately minus 194 degrees Celsius, transforming it into a liquid that can be stored in insulated tanks. When electricity is needed, the liquid air is warmed, expands rapidly, and drives turbines to generate power. The project, developed by China Green Development Investment Group in collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is designed to absorb approximately 600,000 kilowatt-hours of renewable energy daily and deliver an estimated 180 million kilowatt-hours annually. It is also associated with a 250-megawatt solar power installation. One of the technology’s main advantages is its ability to store large quantities of energy without relying on lithium, cobalt, or other critical battery minerals. Unlike some compressed-air storage systems, it does not require underground geological formations, potentially allowing installations in a wider range of locations. Although questions remain about its overall efficiency, construction costs, and long-term commercial competitiveness, the Golmud facility represents an important demonstration of large-scale, long-duration energy storage. As countries expand solar and wind generation, the challenge is no longer simply how to produce clean electricity, but how to make it available whenever it is needed. China’s new liquid-air facility offers another potential pathway toward an energy system less dependent on fossil fuels, while opening possibilities for renewable-energy development in regions where conventional storage solutions may be difficult or expensive to implement. Sources: Golmud Municipal Government; Science and Technology Daily; PowerChina, October–November 2026.

artigo.texto: Residents in four Madison County townships overwhelmingly said data center development should not be allowed in their communities. Ballot initiatives in Chouteau, Granite City, Nameoki and Venice townships asked voters whether they support future data center development and construction. Residents in all four townships voted no. Chouteau Township had the most decisive result with 83.27% of the vote against data centers. Other townships voted at least 74% against them. In Illinois, townships are subdivisions of local government that operate alongside cities and villages. The township’s elected board may oversee local infrastructure, such as water and sewer services. Each of the townships included in the advisory measure overlaps with Granite City. Because the measures are nonbinding, they do not ban data centers even though residents voted against the projects. Loading... Heather Groetecke is a lifelong Granite City resident and led the effort to collect signatures for the initiatives. She said the initiative will send a strong message to policymakers about the will of the voters despite being a nonbinding measure. “I am so stunned by the numbers,” Groetecke said. “The people actually listened and cared about their neighbors to vote no for that.” Groetecke wanted to put a data center moratorium on the ballot. But she said advisers close to the campaign recommended a nonbinding measure because it would be easier to pass. Madison County data center proposals The developer behind a data center project for Midtown St. Louis recently announced plans to build a 200-megawatt data center at the former Alton Steel site, which closed nine months ago. TerraWatt said it reached a “contingent agreement” to buy the site from Alton Steel Inc. and would close on the property in 2027. That’s if the city agrees to rezone the site, and the plan depends on a study by Ameren Illinois and “TerraWatt’s due diligence.” Granite City officials heard public comment about a proposed data center this spring involving two sites along the Route 3 industrial corridor. The Belleville News-Democrat reported that it received mixed reviews, with some in support of union jobs and others concerned about utility rate hikes, environmental impacts and transparency. Officials in nearby Pontoon Beach heard a similar proposal in May, the Alton Telegraph reported. Some residents accused Granite City Mayor Mike Parkinson and other city officials of misleading the public when they said that they knew little about data center development in public meetings. Residents said in May that officials negotiated a possible land sale for a data center project with special governing district America’s Central Port before alerting the public. Parkinson told the News-Democrat that the documents cited by residents were taken out of context and that the city never collaborated with the port authority to bring in data center projects. Months before the community meetings, Parkinson, Madison County Executive Chris Slusser and Granite City’s economic development director, Cathy Hamilton, were among several St. Louis-area leaders who toured a Google data center on a trip financed by Greater St. Louis Inc. Officials were asked to sign nondisclosure agreements before touring the facility. Granite City officials say the data center project was tabled along with similar proposals in Edwardsville and Troy, Illinois.

artigo.texto: Solis Showcases C&I Energy Storage Solutions at REI Expo 2026 Solis showcases its SolisStorage EverCore C&I Energy Storage System at REI Expo 2026 in Greater Noida, while celebrating 10 years of operations in India and cumulative shipments exceeding 10 GW. November 05, 2026. By News Bureau Solis has recently participated in Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026 in Greater Noida, showcasing its Commercial and Industrial (C&I) energy storage solutions while marking 10 years of operations in India and cumulative shipments exceeding 10 GW. The company presented its SolisStorage EverCore C&I Energy Storage System (ESS), highlighting its capabilities in providing reliable backup power, intelligent energy management, and integrated storage solutions for a wide range of commercial and industrial applications. The showcase reflected Solis' continued focus on addressing the evolving energy requirements of commercial and industrial consumers, with an emphasis on reliable, efficient, and flexible energy storage technologies. Commenting on the company's participation, Idrish Khan, CTO, Solis, said, "As India's energy storage market continues to evolve, our focus remains on delivering reliable and intelligent solutions for commercial and industrial applications. Celebrating 10 years in India and surpassing 10 GW in cumulative shipments reflects our continued commitment to supporting the country's clean energy transition." Throughout the three-day exhibition, the company engaged with industry professionals, installers, customers and partners, exchanging insights on emerging trends, market requirements and opportunities in the C&I energy storage segment. The discussions highlighted the growing demand for integrated storage solutions as businesses seek greater energy reliability, operational efficiency and smarter energy management. Concluding its participation at REI Expo 2026, Solis expressed appreciation to its customers, partners and industry stakeholders for their engagement during the exhibition. please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: The humble power bank has become an essential part of my everyday carry. Between smartphones, laptops and the assortment of gadgets that invariably follow me around, having portable power available is practically a necessity. But while manufacturers have been pushing larger capacities and increasingly ridiculous charging speeds, there is another side to battery technology that deserves attention: safety. Enter the Laser ChargeCore Everyday Semi Solid State Series, a 10,000 mAh, 20,000 mAh and 27,000mAh power bank built around semi-solid-state battery technology. This isn’t the first time Laser has taken a different approach to battery chemistry. Back in April 2025, DRN covered the launch of Australia’s first LiFePO₄ power bank range from Laser’s ChargeCore brand. A month later, I got my hands on the ChargeCore SafeCharge Max for a review, exploring the benefits and compromises of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO₄) technology. Back then, the story was about improved chemical stability, longer battery lifespan and the trade-off of lower energy density. The 10,000mAh model I tested was a fairly straightforward power bank with 20W USB-C charging, but its real point of difference was what was happening inside the battery. Fast forward to the ChargeCore Everyday Semi Solid State Series, and Laser is once again exploring battery chemistry rather than simply chasing higher output figures. This time, we’re looking at semi-solid-state technology, a substantially larger 27,000mAh capacity and 35W charging. It’s an interesting progression, particularly when you consider that battery safety remains an increasingly important topic for consumers and travellers alike. Safety First – Why Semi-Solid-State Matters Traditional lithium-ion batteries generally rely on liquid electrolytes to transport lithium ions between the electrodes. These electrolytes can be flammable, contributing to the risk of thermal runaway when batteries are damaged, defective or subjected to extreme conditions. Semi-solid-state technology takes a different approach, reducing reliance on conventional liquid electrolytes through a more solid-like electrolyte structure. It’s worth noting that LiFePO₄ and semi-solid-state are not interchangeable technologies. LiFePO₄ describes the chemistry of the battery’s cathode material, while semi-solid-state refers to the electrolyte system. Both can contribute to battery safety, but through different mechanisms. Depending on the particular chemistry and construction, the potential benefits of semi-solid-state technology include improved thermal stability, reduced leakage risk and better resistance to some failure mechanisms associated with conventional battery designs. Importantly, semi-solid-state doesn’t mean completely solid-state. Nor does it mean the battery is immune to overheating, catching fire or failing catastrophically. The exact safety benefits depend on the chemistry, cell construction and battery management system. Without independent testing, it would be premature to declare the ChargeCore Everyday inherently safer under every possible condition. Nevertheless, this represents a promising direction for battery development. We’ve spent years measuring progress in milliamp-hours and charging wattage. It’s encouraging to see manufacturers investing in improvements to the fundamentals of battery technology rather than simply chasing another headline specification. After all, there is little point having a power bank capable of delivering enormous amounts of power if its safety becomes the compromise. 27,000mAh – Capacity Isn’t Everything The ChargeCore Everyday packs a substantial 27,000mAh capacity, slightly more than the 25,000mAh power bank I carry daily. On paper, that sounds like an upgrade. However, the difference becomes apparent when we look at the power delivery capabilities. The ChargeCore Everyday is available in three capacities. Both the 10,000mAh and 20,000mAh models are limited to 20W output, while the 27,000mAh version reviewed here steps up to 35W. That’s a useful improvement, although it’s still modest compared with some higher-performance power banks. For smartphones, tablets and other everyday devices, 35W is perfectly reasonable. It can even keep my laptop alive under lighter workloads. But keeping a laptop running and delivering enough power to charge it comfortably are two different things. My existing power bank can deliver considerably more power, making it better suited to my laptop and the demands of working away from a wall outlet. The Laser can certainly help in a pinch, but it’s not going to replace my daily companion. There’s also an interesting engineering question here. Is the 35W limitation a consequence of semi-solid-state battery chemistry, or simply a deliberate design decision? I put that question directly to Laser. According to Laser, the 35W maximum output was chosen to ensure reliable and safe operation. Neither the semi-solid-state chemistry nor the maximum discharge capabilities of the cells inherently restrict the power bank to 35W. In fact, the ChargeCore Everyday contains three 9,000mAh cells, each rated for a maximum continuous discharge of 1C, equivalent to 9A per cell. For perspective, the 99.9Wh battery delivering 35W represents an equivalent discharge rate of approximately 0.35C, before accounting for conversion losses. That leaves some interesting headroom. Laser confirmed that the same cells could support a future 65W model with upgraded power delivery electronics and appropriate temperature management. This could include dynamically reducing output as temperatures rise rather than maintaining 65W continuously. Moving to 100W would require a revised battery design alongside suitable electronics. This is a useful technical detail. The ChargeCore Everyday isn’t limited to 35W because semi-solid-state technology is incapable of delivering more power.
