artigo.texto: A Greenvolt colocou em operação os seus dois primeiros projetos de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) no Japão, com uma capacidade conjunta de 4 MW de potência e 8 MWh de armazenamento. Localizados em Kyushu, no sudoeste do país, os projetos assinalam a entrada em operação desta tecnologia da empresa no mercado japonês e reforçam a sua presença na Ásia. Desenvolvidos através da Greenvolt Power, unidade de negócio do grupo dedicada às energias renováveis de grande escala, os dois sistemas autónomos operam em regime de mercado (merchant), gerando receitas através da participação nos mercados de eletricidade. Além da componente comercial, contribuem para aumentar a flexibilidade e a resiliência da rede elétrica. A entrada em operação dos projetos japoneses surge numa altura em que a Greenvolt está a acelerar a expansão do seu negócio de armazenamento de energia. Na Polónia, o grupo concluiu recentemente os projetos de Ełk e Turośń Kościelna, com uma capacidade conjunta de 400 MW / 1,6 GWh, e iniciou a construção de Siedlce, um dos maiores projetos BESS da Europa, com 600 MW / 2,4 GWh. Na Hungria, colocou também em operação o projeto de Buj, com 99,8 MW / 288,6 MWh. “A entrada em operação dos nossos primeiros projetos de armazenamento de energia em baterias no Japão representa um passo importante no reforço da presença da Greenvolt na Ásia e na consolidação da nossa presença global em três continentes. Com um dos maiores pipelines de projetos BESS da Europa e cerca de 1 GW de projetos em construção ou em operação, continuamos a expandir a nossa presença neste setor nos vários mercados onde operamos”, afirmou João Manso Neto, CEO do Grupo Greenvolt. Também Spiros Martinis, CEO da Greenvolt International Power, destacou a importância do mercado asiático para a estratégia da empresa, sublinhando que o grupo continua a explorar oportunidades no Japão, Coreia do Sul e Indonésia. “O crescimento das necessidades de eletricidade cria oportunidades para aproveitar a experiência que temos vindo a desenvolver em diferentes mercados e contextos de negócio”, referiu. No conjunto, a Greenvolt dispõe de um pipeline de aproximadamente 4,6 GW em projetos de armazenamento de energia em baterias na Europa, América do Norte e Ásia. Mais de 1 GW encontra-se em construção ou já em operação, enquanto a empresa vendeu mais de 800 MW de projetos até à data, no âmbito da sua estratégia de rotação de ativos. O armazenamento em baterias está também a ganhar importância nas soluções de produção descentralizada on-site da Greenvolt para empresas, complementando a produção solar e permitindo uma gestão mais flexível dos consumos de energia.

artigo.texto: R$ 31 milhões: Anatel fica sem dinheiro para pagar o próprio data center Agência pediu, mas não recebeu recurso do Tesouro Nacional em outras ocasiões. A Anatel estaria sem dinheiro para custear o próprio data center em Brasília, segundo informações do jornal Folha de São Paulo nesta terça-feira (03/11). A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações alertou o Governo Federal de que precisa de R$ 30,76 milhões para arcar com as notas fiscais referentes ao projeto. Além disso, a agência também estaria sem recursos para pagar contas básicas. O presidente Carlos Baigorri buscou o Ministério do Planejamento na semana passada para solicitar o desbloqueio de R$ 30 milhões. Em ocasiões anteriores, ainda segundo a Folha, o pedido não foi atendido pelo Tesouro Nacional. A Anatel atribui a falta de recursos ao bloqueio de R$ 51,83 milhões, determinado em maio. Houve uma redução de 19% no orçamento discricionário, aquele destinado a custeio e investimentos. Já o data center foi contratado em dezembro de 2025, ao custo de R$ 44,95 milhões em produtos e serviços. De acordo com a Folha, o contrato inclui desde equipamentos até a manutenção e garantia. Nós buscamos a Anatel. Embora a agência não tenha comentado os valores citados na apuração da Folha, ela alertou que “a persistência das restrições orçamentárias e financeiras poderá exigir novas medidas de reprogramação de despesas”. {{ excerpt | truncatewords: 35 }} {% endif %}

artigo.texto: Resumo - Microsoft não vai exercer opção de mais que dobrar contrato com a Nscale no Texas - Extensão representaria dezenas de bilhões de dólares à provedora de IA em nuvem - Fonte diz que decisão foi tomada há meses, antes do pedido de IPO da Nscale - Contrato atual no Texas não foi afetado, segundo a fonte - Nscale já negocia o restante da capacidade com outros grandes clientes - Carteira total de contratos da Nscale segue em cerca de US$103 bilhões A Microsoft decidiu não exercer uma opção contratual que permitiria mais que dobrar seu acordo com a Nscale, provedora de serviços de inteligência artificial (IA) em nuvem. A possibilidade previa a contratação de capacidade computacional adicional em um data center no Texas, nos Estados Unidos. Caso ativasse a cláusula, a companhia poderia ampliar o contrato em dezenas de bilhões de dólares. No entanto, uma pessoa familiarizada com o assunto afirmou que a Microsoft descartou a expansão meses atrás. A fonte, que pediu anonimato por se tratar de informações confidenciais, acrescentou que a decisão ocorreu antes de a Nscale protocolar seu pedido de abertura de capital, em setembro. Apesar disso, o contrato atual entre as duas empresas para a unidade texana continua em vigor, sem alterações. Microsoft e Nscale firmaram acordo em 2025 Em 2025, a Nscale fechou um contrato para instalar aproximadamente 200 mil chips de inteligência artificial fabricados pela Nvidia. O projeto faz parte de uma parceria mais ampla com a Microsoft, que contempla data centers nos Estados Unidos e na Europa. Além disso, há poucas semanas, a Microsoft desistiu de outro acordo com a provedora. O entendimento previa a hospedagem do maior projeto de data center da Nscale em Loughton, no condado de Essex, na Inglaterra. A decisão ocorreu após o adiamento da previsão de fornecimento de energia para a década de 2030. Os atrasos na conexão elétrica comprometeram o cronograma do empreendimento. Contratos bilionários permanecem no prospecto do IPO De acordo com o prospecto da oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês), a Nscale firmou contratos de prestação de serviços com a Microsoft entre setembro de 2025 e abril de 2026. O valor total dos acordos chega a aproximadamente US$ 43,8 bilhões. Os contratos têm validade até dezembro de 2033, sem considerar possíveis renovações opcionais. Segundo a fonte ouvida sobre o assunto, a decisão da Microsoft de não exercer a opção de expansão não altera a carteira de contratos da Nscale. O prospecto do IPO estima esse portfólio em aproximadamente US$ 103 bilhões. A fonte também afirmou que a provedora mantém negociações com diversos grandes clientes para ocupar a capacidade ainda disponível no data center do Texas. Procuradas fora do horário comercial, Microsoft e Nscale não responderam aos pedidos de comentário. Nscale negocia fornecimento de capacidade à Anthropic Enquanto busca novos clientes para seus data centers, a Nscale também negocia uma possível parceria com a Anthropic, empresa responsável pelo desenvolvimento do Claude. Reportagens publicadas no mês passado indicaram que as companhias discutiam um acordo para fornecer capacidade de computação voltada à inteligência artificial. O negócio poderia alcançar aproximadamente US$ 45 bilhões, caso as negociações avancem.

artigo.texto: NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL) has issued a Supply of Battery Containers and Grid-Forming PCS tender for 10 GW/ 40 GWh BESS across its project portfolio. The proposed 10 GW/40 GWh BESS capacity represents a significant addition to India's planned energy storage infrastructure, as the country looks to address the intermittency of renewable power generation and improve grid reliability. Key Components Of The 10 GW BESS Plan The scope of work includes the supply of LFP-based containerised battery systems along with grid-forming PCS. The selected bidders will also supervise the erection, installation and commissioning of the systems at project sites, up to the PCS output terminals. The procurement is expected to support the deployment of large-scale energy storage capacity across NGEL's project portfolio, helping improve the integration of renewable energy into the power grid. The scope also includes comprehensive servicing and maintenance for 15 years from the commissioning date of each project. The long-term service support will be provided through a Long Term Service Agreement (LTSA), covering the battery storage systems and associated equipment as specified in the tender. NGEL's Earlier BESS Tender For Bikaner Solar Park This is not the first large-scale battery storage initiative undertaken by NTPC Green Energy Limited (NGEL). The company had earlier floated an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) tender for a 7,800 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at the NTPC REL Bikaner Solar Park in Rajasthan. The project was divided into five blocks, with individual storage capacities ranging from 1,200 MWh to 2,200 MWh. The tender covered turnkey execution, including design, engineering, equipment supply, installation and commissioning, along with 15 years of operation and maintenance support. What are battery containers and grid format PCS? Battery containers and grid-forming Power Conversion Systems (PCS) are two key components of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). Together, they enable electricity to be stored, converted and supplied to the grid when required. Grid-forming PCS, meanwhile, converts the direct current (DC) electricity stored in batteries into alternating current (AC) for grid use, and vice versa during charging. Unlike conventional grid-following systems, grid-forming technology can help establish and regulate grid voltage and frequency, supporting grid stability even when renewable energy generation fluctuates. Together, these technologies can improve renewable energy integration, provide flexibility in electricity supply, support grid stability and help ensure reliable power delivery. They are particularly important as India increases its dependence on solar and wind energy, which are variable in nature.

artigo.texto: Rede elétrica pode levar 8 anos para atender data centers construídos em 4 No DCD Connect, executivos apontam gargalos de transmissão, especulação por energia e alternativas para expansão de data centers no Brasil. A ampliação da infraestrutura elétrica brasileira pode levar de seis a oito anos, enquanto a construção de um grande data center exige de dois a quatro anos. O descompasso entre esses prazos foi apontado por Marcelo Wagner Oliveira Silva, facilities manager da SONDA, como um dos obstáculos à expansão da capacidade computacional para IA no Brasil. A diferença entre os cronogramas pode dificultar a conexão de novos empreendimentos à rede elétrica. “Hoje, para se construir um grande data center, está levando em torno de 2 a 4 anos, dependendo do tamanho. E para você fazer hoje uma obra para aumentar a sua rede elétrica, pode levar de 6 a 8 anos”, afirmou Silva durante o painel “Sem energia não há IA: O Brasil consegue acompanhar a demanda por infraestrutura?”, realizado no DCD Connect Brasil 2026. O debate reuniu também Bruno Moreira, CEO da Energ Geradores; Hemil Ribeiro, líder global de infraestrutura da Angola Cables; Emanuel Gustavo Barcarolo, diretor técnico da Mendes Holler Engenharia; e Mark Sánchez, managing director da SouthBridge Infrastructure, responsável pela condução da discussão. Os participantes avaliaram que a capacidade brasileira de atrair investimentos em data centers depende não apenas da disponibilidade de fontes de geração, mas também da expansão das redes de transmissão, dos prazos de conexão, da infraestrutura de telecomunicações e da localização dos empreendimentos. Silva destacou que a participação das fontes renováveis na matriz energética brasileira representa uma vantagem para o país, mas não assegura o atendimento à demanda dos novos projetos. “O fato de ter a energia disponível não garante que você consiga levar até o seu consumidor final com a devida qualidade, com a devida confiabilidade e tudo o que precisa hoje nesse mercado”, afirmou. O executivo também citou projeções da Agência Internacional de Energia segundo as quais o consumo global de eletricidade por data centers pode passar de aproximadamente 485 TWh em 2025 para 950 TWh em 2030. Os números foram apresentados durante o painel como referência para o crescimento da demanda associado à IA. Transmissão não acompanha o ritmo dos investimentos Bruno Moreira, da Energ Geradores, identificou na transmissão de energia um dos principais entraves à implantação de novos empreendimentos. Segundo ele, o Brasil dispõe de recursos energéticos para receber investimentos, mas precisa compatibilizar a expansão das redes elétricas com os cronogramas dos projetos de infraestrutura digital. “O gargalo está na transmissão”, afirmou Moreira. “A gente tem que fazer essa energia chegar onde os empreendimentos estão.” O executivo mencionou as iniciativas de contratação de reserva de capacidade e a perspectiva de leilões de baterias como instrumentos para ampliar a resiliência do sistema elétrico. Ressaltou, entretanto, que a implantação de novas linhas de transmissão não ocorre na mesma velocidade da construção dos data centers. Emanuel Gustavo Barcarolo, da Mendes Holler Engenharia, relacionou parte das dificuldades à concentração territorial dos investimentos. Segundo ele, o setor estabeleceu polos em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Fortaleza, mas a infraestrutura elétrica não consegue acompanhar toda a demanda nas regiões procuradas pelos investidores. “A gente não tem energia disponível onde a gente quer, para onde os data centers querem”, afirmou. Barcarolo chamou atenção para o aumento da potência solicitada pelos empreendimentos. Projetos que anteriormente demandavam conexões de 10 MW ou 20 MW deram lugar a iniciativas que discutem capacidades de 200 MW e até 1 GW. Essa mudança amplia a complexidade dos estudos de conexão e exige avaliar os efeitos das novas cargas sobre o Sistema Interligado Nacional. Diferentemente de consumidores com demanda variável ao longo do dia, os data centers precisam manter alimentação elétrica contínua. Especulação por capacidade elétrica prejudica planejamento Além das limitações físicas das redes, os executivos apontaram a multiplicação de solicitações de acesso à infraestrutura elétrica como um problema para o planejamento da expansão. Barcarolo afirmou que o crescimento dos pedidos de capacidade, inclusive para projetos que não necessariamente chegam à implantação, prejudicou a confiabilidade dos estudos utilizados para orientar investimentos. “Quando a especulação se tornou muito grande, deixou de ter confiabilidade no estudo. E aí a gente passou a perder tempo”, declarou. Moreira concordou com a avaliação e afirmou que a disputa por capacidade disponível passou a interferir nas decisões sobre onde ampliar a infraestrutura de transmissão. “Teve muita especulação e virou uma corrida especulativa por energia”, disse. As manifestações indicam uma preocupação dos participantes com o alinhamento entre os pedidos de conexão, a efetiva demanda dos empreendimentos e o planejamento das obras necessárias para atender aos novos consumidores. Barcarolo também observou que o aumento da escala dos data centers exige estudos técnicos para preservar a estabilidade da rede. Segundo ele, a operação de um sistema elétrico interligado, com dimensões continentais, demanda avaliação dos efeitos que novas cargas podem produzir sobre o conjunto da infraestrutura. Ceará exemplifica alternativa de instalar data centers perto da energia Diante da diferença entre os prazos de implantação de data centers e de ampliação das redes, Hemil Ribeiro, da Angola Cables, defendeu a possibilidade de direcionar novos empreendimentos para regiões onde já exista capacidade energética disponível. “Uma das opções é a gente começar a levar a carga para onde tem a potência pronta”, afirmou. O executivo citou o Ceará como exemplo de convergência entre oferta de energia, disponibilidade de terrenos e infraestrutura de cone

artigo.texto: Vitória democrata no Texas ameaça expansão de data centers no estado | Vero NotíciasVitória democrata no Texas ameaça expansão de data centers no estado A eleição da democrata Gina Hinojosa para o governo do Texas, nesta terça-feira (3), aumentou as incertezas sobre a expansão de data centers no estado. Durante a campanha, ela prometeu suspender novas autorizações até a aprovação de leis que protejam as comunidades locais. O Texas concentra grandes investimentos de empresas como Meta, Google e Microsoft, mas enfrenta preocupações com o consumo de energia e os impactos ambientais. O governador derrotado, Greg Abbott, já havia suspendido novas conexões à rede elétrica e determinado auditorias sobre os projetos. Pesquisa da Universidade de Houston apontou que 79% dos prováveis eleitores texanos apoiavam limites à construção de data centers. A possível moratória ameaça investimentos de dezenas de bilhões de dólares e amplia as dúvidas sobre o futuro do setor no estado. Condenado por crime ambiental, o biólogo Alexander Alves Gomes atuou no polêmico licenciamento da ampliação do Aterro Sanitário Metropolitano de Salvador, operado pela Bahia Transferência e Tratamento de Resíduos (Battre), empresa do Grupo Solví, do empresário Carlos Villa, ambos alvos de investigações ambientais. A reportagem apurou que a própria Ambiente Gaia Consultoria e Engenharia, dirigida por Gomes, confirma ter realizado o "licenciamento ambiental para ampliação" de dois aterros do Grupo Solví: o da Battre, em Salvador, e o Aterro Classe II de Inertes Águas Claras, e apresenta o grupo como "cliente fixo". O petróleo caiu mais de 8% nesta quarta-feira (4), após as eleições legislativas americanas. O Brent para janeiro fechou a US$ 94,62, com baixa de 8,66%, e o WTI para dezembro recuou 8,29%, a US$ 88,12. O mercado avaliou que a vitória democrata reduz o risco de escalada no Oriente Médio. Segundo o Swissquote Bank, o novo Congresso poderá fiscalizar gastos militares e pressionar por uma saída diplomática com o Irã. O Google ampliou em junho seu programa de demissão voluntária para Canadá, Alemanha, Suíça, França e Japão. A iniciativa integra esforços para direcionar recursos a áreas prioritárias, especialmente inteligência artificial. Na Suíça, os funcionários que aderiram começaram a sair em agosto. A indenização corresponde a um mês de salário por ano trabalhado, limitada a 12 meses. O número de adesões não foi divulgado. A Confederação Nacional da Indústria acionou o STF nesta quarta-feira (4) para impedir a aplicação do fim da escala 6x1 a contratos anteriores à emenda. A entidade quer preservá-los até o encerramento. A CNI também pede a suspensão dos prazos de redução da jornada por ao menos um ano. Argumenta que a mudança viola a segurança jurídica e estima custo adicional de R$ 88 bilhões para a indústria. O Mercado Livre registrou lucro líquido de US$ 448 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta anual de 6,4%. A receita líquida e financeira cresceu 45%, alcançando US$ 10,75 bilhões. No Brasil, o volume de itens vendidos avançou 45%. A companhia atribuiu parte do desempenho ao frete grátis, enquanto os investimentos em logística e marketing pressionaram a rentabilidade.

artigo.texto: SambaNova SN50 Chips to Power Supermicro's New Inference Racks, Delivering High-Performance Inference to Data Centers Worldwide Highlights: - Supermicro will work with SambaNova to develop leading-edge SN50 inference racks that operate alongside NVIDIA GPUs as part of Supermicro’s Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS) - The strategic collaboration is initially planning for 10,000 RDU chips from SambaNova SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 3, 2026-- SambaNova, the AI chip company delivering the highest performance inference, today announced that Supermicro (Nasdaq: SMCI), an AI, Enterprise, Storage, and 5G/Edge Total IT Solution Provider featuring Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS), is entering into a strategic collaboration, initially planning for 10,000 SN50 RDU chips, to build and sell AI disaggregated inference systems that include RDUs and GPUs. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261103999239/en/ “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers. Our collaboration with SambaNova expands our broad DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration, helping customers deploy efficient, scalable AI solutions,” said Charles Liang, president and CEO of Supermicro. "Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere," said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and CEO of SambaNova. "Supermicro builds AI infrastructure for data centers globally. Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust. That's how fast, efficient inference gets to scale." Agents work nonstop, and how fast they act depends on how fast the model responds. Supermicro's systems pair NVIDIA GPUs, which read the prompt, with SambaNova SN50 chips built to write the response quickly. “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers. Our collaboration with SambaNova expands our broad DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration, helping customers deploy efficient, scalable AI solutions,” said Charles Liang, president and CEO of Supermicro. Built, Sold and Supported by Supermicro Supermicro will integrate, test, deliver and support the systems for customers, including providing on-site service. SambaNova engineers will get models running and tuned on SN50 and help Supermicro with deployments. The companies will start with NeoClouds and sovereign clouds, then expand to enterprises that run AI in their own data centers. About SambaNova RDU Chips SambaNova’s SN50 is the company’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU) chip, purpose-built for high-performance inference. RDUs serve the largest models at high speed and high throughput without requiring extreme rack power density, which makes them much easier to deploy in existing data centers. RDUs also work alongside existing NVIDIA GPUs to drastically improve system performance and efficiency, with the GPUs running the prefill phase and the RDUs running the decode phase. Operators can therefore add inference capacity without waiting for next-generation data center build-outs, which are constrained by power and cooling, and can extend the useful life of the GPUs they already own. As a result, SambaNova and Supermicro can deliver substantially more high-performance inference capacity in 2027 than would otherwise be possible. About SambaNova SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, providing a full stack platform that powers high-performance inference for enterprises, NeoClouds, AI labs and service providers, and sovereign AI initiatives worldwide. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Jose, Calif., SambaNova delivers chips, systems, and cloud services that enable customers to deploy state-of-the-art models with superior performance, lower total cost of ownership, and rapid time to value. For more information, visit sambanova.ai or contact [email protected]. Connect with SambaNova on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube for company news, AI inference insights, and technology demonstrations. All other brands, names, and trademarks are the property of their respective owners. artigo.texto: Voters made it clear this week that they want to see limits put on data centers for artificial intelligence, passing 40 of 41 proposed ballot measures that would place restrictions on some of the more than 2,000 new facilities planned for communities around the nation. Water and power top the list of ratepayers' concerns. But calculating how much each data center draws from local resources is an elusive task, with operators typically reporting usage figures companywide instead of site by site. Giant 1-gigawatt AI data centers from the likes of Meta, Google, Amazon and SpaceX can consume up to 10 million gallons of water per day, according to Shaolei Ren, a data center researcher and professor at University of California, Riverside. The exact number varies greatly depending on what type of hardware is inside a data center, where it's built, and what method is used to cool the servers and the building as a whole. The complex ways data centers use water have left room for misinformation from both the builders and those fighting against them. CNBC talked to experts to get a clearer picture. Air vs. liquid cooling Data centers need serious internal cooling methods to keep chips and servers from overheating. Legacy data centers, filled with lower-power servers used for things like networking or storage, are often air-cooled. Large fans move hot air away from the servers and outside the building. But modern AI data centers are filled with high-power, denser graphics processing units, or GPUs, which Ren said can run so hot that the servers can "boil your eggs." Water is about 3,000 times more efficient for cooling down these GPUs, according to Equinix sustainability head Christopher Wellise. GPUs "run at such a high wattage, a high temperature, you would need nearly hurricane-force winds to actually cool them down if you were just using air," Wellise told CNBC in an interview. That's why the latest rack-scale AI systems, Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Advanced Micro Devices' Helios, rely on liquid cooling. Most large AI data centers use a closed-loop liquid cooling system that uses very little water on a daily basis. At an Equinix data center in San Jose, California, CNBC got an up-close look at the closed-loop liquid cooling system used to keep temperatures down in a row of eight Nvidia Grace Blackwell racks owned by AI marketing startup Alembic. Equinix builds colocation data centers, where companies like Alembic rent space to run their own server racks, while Equinix supplies the power, network connections, interconnectivity and cooling. Like many data center operators, Equinix doesn't disclose water consumption at individual sites. In 2025, Equinix operations as a whole consumed 1.2 billion gallons of water, up 10% from a year prior. Despite closed-loop internal cooling like what Equinix uses in San Jose, total water consumption is far more dependent on an additional cooling process that happens outside the data center. "How do we reject the heat from the closed loop to the ambient environment?" Ren said. "That's where the water usage comes in." In Lebanon, Indiana, for example, Meta is building a 1GW data center that it says uses a "closed-loop, liquid-cooled system that recirculates the same water and will use zero water for a majority of the year." Water allocation for the site, however, could ramp up to 8 million gallons per day by 2031, according to the company's law firm. Meta says that figure represents peak usage on the hottest days. "We anticipate rarely reaching this maximum usage level, currently projected as only a few days per year," Meta told CNBC in a statement. That's because the hottest days of the year will require more water for that external cooling process, removing the heat from that separate internal closed-loop system. Less water, more power There are two primary methods for this external cooling process at a data center: dry cooling and evaporative cooling. While dry cooling uses far less water, it can require far more power, especially in hotter climates where many of these AI data centers are being built. "There's no sort of silver bullet," Wellise said. "At some point you need to eject that heat out to the atmosphere. And that's where those trade-offs occur." Dry cooling relies on fans to blow air across heat exchangers, using the ambient air to cool it down. Those fans are less effective when the outside temperature is high, so data centers turn on refrigeration units to cool down the air first. "That's a very power-intensive process, and that's exactly why we have power shortages in the summer," Ren said. "Because everybody else turns on their AC." Evaporative cooling, meanwhile, uses very little power. The hot water circulates through cooling towers or over wet pads that are exposed to air, and the portion that evaporates carries heat away with it. Large amounts of water can be lost through that evaporation on the hottest days. In between these two extremes, hybrid methods are common as companies try to find a balance. Some data centers, like Equinix's in San Jose, use dry cooling in the colder months and evaporative cooling when it's hot outside. In Indiana, Meta relies on dry cooling and keeps power consumption down in hotter months by spraying a mist to cool the air instead of relying solely on refrigeration units. Creating cooler chips Near some data center projects, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and others are building water treatment plants to help treat and recycle the necessary water. Meta, for example, spent $100 million on a new water and wastewater system near its data center in Kuna, Idaho. Outside Memphis, Tennessee, Elon Musk pledged $80 million to build a water recycling plant that's meant to turn treated municipal wastewater into cooling water for SpaceX's Colossus data centers. artigo.texto: Mercado global de memória flash 3D NAND: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de 3D NAND até 2035: demanda de data centers de IA impulsiona o crescimento Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de 3D NAND, o setor inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta regionalmente mais diversificada. O mercado global de 3D NAND entra em uma fase de transformação, à medida que cargas de trabalho intensivas em dados remodelam os requisitos de armazenamento em toda a economia digital. Em 2026, a 3D NAND já se consolidou como a arquitetura de memória não volátil dominante, tendo substituído a NAND planar em praticamente todos os segmentos de aplicação. A capacidade da tecnologia de empilhar células de memória verticalmente permitiu o avanço contínuo da densidade e a redução do custo por bit, sustentando o crescimento exponencial do armazenamento em estado sólido em smartphones, data centers e sistemas corporativos. O mercado tem estrutura oligopolista, com um pequeno número de fabricantes globais que detêm recursos financeiros e tecnológicos substanciais. Esses players travam uma corrida incessante para ultrapassar 200 camadas, melhorar o desempenho e reduzir os custos de produção. O período de projeção até 2035 é moldado por novos vetores de demanda, em especial a proliferação de cargas de trabalho de inteligência artificial, que exigem soluções de armazenamento de alto desempenho e alta capacidade. O treinamento e a inferência de IA em data centers geram volumes de dados sem precedentes, que precisam ser armazenados e acessados rapidamente, criando um aumento estrutural da demanda por SSDs de nível corporativo. Ao mesmo tempo, a eletrônica de consumo continua a exigir capacidades de armazenamento maiores, enquanto a eletrônica automotiva surge como nova fronteira de crescimento, com o aumento do registro de dados e dos requisitos de entretenimento a bordo. No entanto, o mercado enfrenta ventos contrários decorrentes de desequilíbrios cíclicos entre oferta e demanda, de exigências significativas de investimento de capital e de tensões comerciais geopolíticas que afetam as cadeias de suprimento globais. Este relatório oferece uma análise abrangente do mercado de 3D NAND, apresentando às partes interessadas uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre a dinâmica do mercado, o posicionamento competitivo e as oportunidades de crescimento até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de 3D NAND prevê expansão sustentada até 2035, com taxa composta de crescimento anual (CAGR) de 8,2% entre 2026 e 2035. Essa trajetória de crescimento está ancorada na transformação estrutural da infraestrutura de dados em todo o mundo, em que os SSDs baseados em 3D NAND substituem os discos rígidos tradicionais tanto em aplicações corporativas quanto em aplicações de cliente. O valor de mercado deve atingir novos patamares, impulsionado pelo aumento da demanda por bits e pela gradual estabilização da dinâmica de preços após as quedas cíclicas observadas em meados da década de 2020. O cenário-base pressupõe um ambiente econômico global moderado, o contínuo avanço tecnológico no empilhamento de camadas e na arquitetura de células, e a aceleração constante dos investimentos em infraestrutura relacionada à IA. Espera-se que a dinâmica do lado da oferta permaneça disciplinada, com os principais fabricantes administrando as expansões de capacidade em linha com o crescimento da demanda para evitar excesso de oferta prolongado. A transição para dispositivos com maior número de camadas, como os que superam 300 camadas, deve gerar ganhos de eficiência de custo que sustentam a recuperação das margens e o reinvestimento em tecnologias de próxima geração. A demanda dos data centers deve ser o principal motor de crescimento, à medida que hyperscalers e provedores de serviços em nuvem ampliam a capacidade de armazenamento para dar suporte a IA, aprendizado de máquina e análise de big data. O segmento de smartphones continuará a impulsionar volumes, com o aumento constante da capacidade média de armazenamento por dispositivo. A eletrônica automotiva representa um segmento menor, porém de rápido crescimento, impulsionado por sistemas avançados de assistência ao motorista e entretenimento a bordo. Regionalmente, a Ásia-Pacífico manterá sua dominância tanto na produção quanto no consumo, enquanto América do Norte e Europa se concentram na expansão de data centers e na resiliência das cadeias de suprimento. O índice de mercado, com 2025 como ano-base em 100, deve alcançar 203 em 2035, refletindo a duplicação do valor de mercado ao longo do período de projeção. artigo.texto: ZEISS Invests in Illumion to Support Next-Generation Battery Imaging Technology ZEISS Ventures has participated in a £1.7 million funding round for Illumion, a University of Cambridge spin-out developing imaging technology for battery research and development. The round was joined by Foresight Group, Cambridge Enterprise Ventures, Parkwalk, Cambridge Angels, and YourVC. As global demand for higher-performing and more sustainable batteries grows, Illumion is developing optical imaging solutions that reveal previously inaccessible processes occurring inside working batteries. Its proprietary charge photometry technology enables researchers and engineers to observe individual battery particles during charging and discharging, providing valuable insights for the development and manufacturing of batteries. It harnesses the principles of optical interference reflection imaging to detect the light scattered by individual particles across an electrode. As ions move in and out of the electrode material, the resulting changes in light scattering reveal the local state-of-charge of each particle. Watch in real-time as each particle charges and discharges, while simultaneously monitoring changes in particle morphology that affect battery performance. The funding will support the further commercialization of Illumion’s technology, execution of its product roadmap, and collaboration with researchers, battery developers, and industrial partners. This includes the further development of illumionONE for real-time particle-level battery analysis, and the next-generation illumionX platform, which is intended to address selected industrial use cases. “Illumion combines scientific excellence with innovative imaging technology for battery research. By helping to visualize dynamic processes within batteries at the particle level, the company aims to deepen researchers’ understanding of battery materials and their behavior. We are pleased to support the team as it further develops its optical analytics platform,” says Dr. Boris Hofmann, Head of ZEISS Ventures. “This funding marks an important next step for Illumion as we translate world-class research into practical tools for battery development. We are excited to continue advancing our technology with the support of ZEISS Ventures, Foresight, and our existing investors,” comments Christoph Schnedermann, Co-founder and CEO of Illumion. The investment reflects ZEISS Ventures’ commitment to supporting innovative imaging technologies for scientific and industrial applications. For more information: www.zeiss.com

artigo.texto: LibertyStream Announces Lithium Carbonate Sales Contract with International Battery Material Maker Covering 2027–2031 Supply LibertyStream Enters into U.S.-Origin Lithium Carbonate Sales Contract for up to 17,500 Metric Tonnes; Provides Operations Update DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 5, 2026-- LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners Inc. (TSXV: LIB | OTCQB: VLTLF | FSE: I2D) (“LibertyStream” or the “Company”) announced that it has entered into a lithium carbonate sales contract (the “Sales Contract”) with a leading international battery material maker that supplies cathodes to the U.S. market (the “Customer”). The Sales Contract provides for the Company to supply 500 metric tonnes of U.S.-origin lithium carbonate in 2027 and sets out binding terms for the supply of an additional 17,000 metric tonnes of U.S.-origin lithium carbonate through December 31, 2031, with detailed terms for 2028 through 2031 to be finalized under a separate long-term supply agreement (the “LTSA”). Volumes for 2028 through 2031 are subject to execution of the LTSA. Pricing and other commercial terms are not being disclosed. Meeting the scheduled delivery volumes will require the Company to develop, finance and commission additional U.S. production capacity. The Sales Contract is the definitive agreement contemplated by a memorandum of understanding between the Company and the Customer dated September 3, 2026. It follows the Company’s field operations, direct lithium extraction and refining testing, lithium carbonate production at its Freedom Launchpad facility, customer qualification programs, third-party testing and initial purchase orders. The Sales Contract is in addition to the Company’s previously announced 600-tonne-per-year industrial offtake agreement. Operations Update LibertyStream continues to advance commercialization activities in support of future lithium carbonate production. LibertyStream has delivered lithium carbonate samples to multiple battery and industrial-grade prospective customers as part of ongoing product qualification and testing programs. LibertyStream currently produces lithium carbonate from U.S. oilfield brine at its Freedom Launchpad facility in Texas. Freedom 1, located in Howard County, Texas, is the Company’s planned initial commercial facility under its previously announced agreement with Select Water Solutions. Freedom 1 is designed to integrate LibertyStream’s direct lithium extraction and refining technologies with existing oilfield water infrastructure to produce battery-grade lithium carbonate from U.S. oilfield brine. About LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners LibertyStream is a lithium development and technology company aiming to be one of North America’s first commercial producers of lithium carbonate from oilfield brine. Our strategy is to generate value for shareholders by leveraging management’s hydrocarbon experience to deploy our proprietary DLE technology directly into existing oil and gas infrastructure, thereby reducing capital costs, lowering risks and supporting the world’s clean energy transition. We are committed to operating efficiently and with transparency across all areas of the business staying sharply focused on creating long-term, sustainable shareholder value. Investors and/or other interested parties may sign up for updates about the Company’s continued progress on its website: https://LibertyStream.com/. artigo.texto: CATL advances 20 Ah solid-state battery cells ahead of 2027 trial production CATL has advanced its all-solid-state battery development from a 10 Ah-class validation platform to 20 Ah sample trials, according to Y-Auto. It targets small-batch production in 2027, with large-scale manufacturing planned around 2030. The company provided an update on October 27 in response to investor questions on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange’s Hudongyi platform. Its development team has more than 1,000 people, and the programme targets an energy density of about 500 Wh/kg. CATL has not confirmed that figure as a production-cell specification or disclosed expected trial output, automotive customers or a vehicle launch date tied to these cells. What CATL’s solid-state cells still need to prove Energy density is only one measure of battery performance. Durability, manufacturing yield, cost, safety and performance under real operating conditions will also determine whether the cells are suitable for production vehicles. Chairman Robin Zeng previously rated CATL’s solid-state battery technology at Level 4 on a nine-level readiness scale. The assessment provides context for the development still required, but the more consequential test is whether the company can manufacture reliable cells at commercially viable cost. Sulfide cells face interface and durability hurdles. Sulfide electrolytes conduct lithium ions effectively, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a challenge. Electrodes expand and contract during charging and discharging, which can disrupt those interfaces. Cell design must manage contact pressure and interface resistance to maintain performance. Sulfide materials also require protection from moisture because reactions can release hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), a toxic gas. Material handling and manufacturing conditions therefore remain important considerations for commercial production. The 500 Wh/kg goal also raises questions about electrode design. Such high cell-level energy density can involve higher-capacity anode architectures, including lithium-metal or anode-less designs. For example, Samsung SDI has described an anode-less approach for its all-solid-state batteries. CATL has not disclosed the anode configuration used in the cells covered by its latest update. CATL, Toyota and Samsung SDI have different targets CATL is targeting small-batch production in 2027. Toyota and Idemitsu aim to commercialise sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries for battery-electric vehicles between 2027 and 2028, while Samsung SDI has targeted mass production in the second half of 2027. These milestones are not directly equivalent. Samsung SDI has also identified humanoid robots as a potential early application for its technology while continuing development for electric vehicles. These timelines do not mean the companies’ products will reach the market at the same time, in comparable volumes, or with equivalent performance. How all-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid designs All-solid-state batteries use a solid electrolyte rather than relying on a liquid electrolyte within the cell. Semi-solid and hybrid designs retain some liquid electrolyte, although terminology and configurations vary by manufacturer. Progress with a semi-solid design does not, by itself, show that a company has overcome the interface, durability, and manufacturing challenges of an all-solid-state cell. For CATL, the central challenge is turning its current development work into repeatable, cost-competitive production. artigo.texto: Data centers em SP podem limitar envio de energia ao Sul, aponta ONS Planejamento para o período de 2027 a 2031 aponta pressão sobre a rede paulista e possível necessidade de mais geração na região Sul do Brasil A expansão de data centers em São Paulo poderá restringir a transferência de energia para o Sul e aumentar a necessidade de geração na própria região, especialmente nos períodos de maior consumo, aponta o ONS (Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico). A avaliação consta do Plano da Operação Elétrica de Médio Prazo (PAR/PEL), para o ciclo de 2027 a 2031. Segundo o relatório, a entrada de grandes consumidores tende a esgotar os recursos disponíveis para controlar a tensão e intensificar os fluxos na rede de transmissão paulista. Esses efeitos impactam a capacidade máxima de envio de energia do subsistema Sudeste/Centro-Oeste para o Sul. O tomo de São Paulo mostra que o aumento desse intercâmbio piora o perfil de tensão da malha analisada. Em uma simulação para o verão de 2031, com carga máxima noturna e recebimento de 12.500 megawatts (MW) pelo Sul, o ONS identificou tensão abaixo do limite inferior nas subestações Fernão Dias e Campinas. Nesse cenário, as restrições aparecem mesmo com a rede completa, sem depender da ocorrência de falhas. O diagnóstico acompanha a expansão das solicitações de conexão. Até setembro de 2026, o operador registrava 212 projetos de data centers na área São Paulo, com cerca de 17,8 gigawatts (GW) de potência solicitada, considerando as redes de transmissão e distribuição. Na Rede Básica, 38 projetos já haviam sido viabilizados, totalizando 4.289 MW. A relação inclui empreendimentos em diferentes estágios: dois, com 223 MW, estavam em operação comercial, enquanto 23, com 2.767 MW, tinham contratos de uso da transmissão celebrados. Os demais tinham acesso considerado viável ou estavam no âmbito da primeira temporada da Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão (Pnast). O ONS ressalta que parcela significativa da potência solicitada ainda não está refletida nos casos de estudo publicados. Na avaliação dos grandes consumidores, foram representados apenas os novos consumidores e data centers com contratos de uso da transmissão assinados ou pareceres de acesso viáveis. “Torna-se necessária a avaliação de soluções adicionais que considerem, de forma integrada, as necessidades de atendimento ao Sul e os impactos decorrentes do crescimento da carga na área São Paulo”, afirma o relatório. O operador prevê aprofundar a análise do impacto dessas cargas sobre o recebimento pelo Sul no próximo ciclo do PAR/PEL, em 2027. As restrições na rede já levaram à recusa de pedidos de conexão. Como mostrou a CNN, o CEO da CPFL Energia, Gustavo Estrella, afirmou em outubro que a companhia negou solicitações de data centers que somavam cerca de 8 GW. O executivo atribuiu a dificuldade principalmente à transmissão e reconheceu que parte dos pedidos tinha caráter especulativo. Em agosto, Estrella havia informado que o consumo de eletricidade dos data centers na área de concessão da CPFL cresceu 35,8% no segundo trimestre de 2026 em relação ao mesmo período de 2025.

artigo.texto: Many of the biggest technology companies are surging on Wednesday, after Democrats scored a seismic victory in the midterm elections, flipping both the House and Senate. During trading on Wednesday, Amazon surged 8%, Google rose over 6%, Microsoft rose 4%, Meta was up 3%, and Apple — which faced Trump's tariffs and recently got refunds — climbed nearly 7%. Tuesday's results remove uncertainty in the market, David Kelly, chief global strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, said on "Squawk on the Street." He said the divided government would lead to "moderation in growth, moderation in inflation, less uncertainty, and I think that's all helping the stock market move up today." However, some stocks, particularly those tied to Trump advisor Elon Musk as well as the AI data center buildout, fell on Wednesday. As results came in last night, some observers saw bad news for big technology companies because of their bets to build large AI-focused data centers. There were 41 local ballot measures on Tuesday to place restrictions or clear the way for AI data centers, and voters sided against data centers in 40 of them. In a CNBC Voter Poll, 56% of voters said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their voting decision. Analysts said that Democrats who proposed data center moratoriums won gubernatorial races in Texas, Georgia, and Ohio, raising fears that projects could get snarled in regulation or blocked by politicians. "Recall that backup power emissions, zoning, water, interconnect/grid, and tax considerations are often overseen by state regulators," Macquarie analyst Paul Golding said in a note on Wednesday. Tesla stock fell 2%, and SpaceX was down 3%. Nvidia, which makes the chips for most of these AI data center projects, slipped just over 1%. Many of the technology stocks rising on Wednesday are what are known as hyperscalers, or the largest cloud providers that also pair massive capex spending with robust free cash flow and have the most experience and capability to construct AI data centers. "We believe higher regulatory barriers entrench incumbents, and increase risks (and raise required ROICs) for new entrants," wrote Needham analyst Laura Martin in a note on Wednesday. "Hyperscalers are AI incumbents." Smaller AI cloud providers, often called neoclouds, got whacked on Wednesday. CoreWeave stock fell 10%. Baird analysts said in a note that the election results create a "sentiment headwind" for neoclouds. Golding, the Macquarie analyst, wrote that he remains bullish on AI infrastructure, and that well-capitalized, high-quality operators stand to benefit the most if projects in some states slow down. "Neoclouds may pay more to lease powered shells for GPUaaS commitments (and pass on costs), while hyperscaler/AI lab capacity needs could intensify competition for even more limited supply," Golding wrote. Tuesday's results could signal restrictions on new data center developments in some states, but it doesn't necessarily signal a nationwide slowdown in construction, Chris Miglino, CEO of Axe Compute, said in an email. Companies are still raising capital, enterprises are spending, and there's still a need for more capacity. Miglino said that increased regulation in some regions could cause investors and customers to look more closely at different cloud computing providers, and opt for those with the capability to deliver capacity, or which offer AI inference to a specific industry niche. "If you've already secured power, have the financing in place and understand how to deploy and operate compute infrastructure efficiently, you're in a much stronger position than a company that's still trying to figure those things out," Miglino said.

artigo.texto: This story was originally published by Canary Media. It has been edited to conform with Corporate Knights style. Developers and utilities are building tons of gas generation to power the data centre boom. It’s an expansion that could cost them and the rest of us dearly, both in terms of climate change and money that may end up wasted if computing demand fails to materialize. But there’s a cleaner, cheaper and faster-to-deploy alternative: batteries. That’s the conclusion of a new report from researchers at Georgetown and Duke universities, which lays out the ways states can push utilities and tech firms to opt for energy storage over fossil fuels whenever possible. Fossil fuel power – whether in the form of giant utility-scale plants or generators installed behind the meter at data centres – has become the go-to for many in the AI industry. That’s because gas generation offers round-the-clock power in a single package. Overall, U.S. utilities are planning more than 60 gigawatts of new gas plants to serve data centre demand, and around 90 GW of behind-the-meter gas generators for data centres have been proposed nationwide. “At the moment, there’s a lot of inertia and status quo pressure for much of the behind-the-meter resources being natural gas,” said Ian Hitchcock, report co-author and senior program coordinator at the Duke Initiative for Science and Society. A safer alternative Moving ahead with those gas power plans does more than spell climate disaster. If data centre proposals fall through or shut down early, other utility customers could be on the hook for the cost of overbuilding gas. That’s called “stranded asset” risk – and states have only begun to tackle it, even amid mounting fears that the AI sector is a bubble about to pop. Batteries “can act as a hedge against that risk,” last week’s report explains. Batteries are much cheaper than round-the-clock gas generation in situations where hours of stored energy can solve near-term needs. They’re also inherently modular and flexible in ways that gas power plants are not, which allows planners to increase or cut back on deployment if data centre demand shifts sharply. Plus, batteries can help avoid the need for costly grid buildouts that would otherwise be used to serve increasing electricity demand, and can act as shock absorbers to cushion the grid against data centres’ massive and fast-changing computing loads. While lithium-ion batteries can’t provide round-the-clock power, they can meet large portions of data centre electricity needs, said Jackson Ewing, director of energy and climate policy at Duke University’s Nicholas Institute of Energy, Environment & Sustainability. And unlike more future-forward solutions – such as advanced geothermal, next-generation nuclear, and novel long-duration energy storage technologies – “batteries are already showing serious momentum in terms of their deployment trajectory.” Developers like it In fact, utilities and data centre developers are increasingly embracing batteries, even as they pursue gas. A new forecast from BloombergNEF sees U.S. energy storage deployment surpassing 11,000 gigawatt-hours by 2036, a 30% increase from its 10-year forecast from just six months ago. Data centre demand is pushing much of that growth. So, what can state decision-makers do to further encourage data centres to opt for batteries? States that directly regulate utility investments can craft “bring your own new clean energy” tariff structures. These regulations can set minimum requirements for data centres to procure or pay for enough carbon-free generation and energy storage to cover some or all of their electricity needs. Certain jurisdictions are already moving ahead with this approach; Google, for example, has signed onto such tariffs with regulators in Nevada and Minnesota. Things get more complicated in states with “restructured” energy markets. In these places, regulators have limited authority over the independent power producers that build big generation and battery projects and sell power into wholesale electricity markets. Still, the report highlights several ways that these states can encourage battery development to serve data centres, including via state energy storage mandates like those launched in Illinois, Maryland and New Jersey, and engaging in state energy planning in conjunction with regional grid operators. “There is not a jurisdiction that has no potential action items if they’re serious about trying to deploy this,” Hitchcock said. artigo.texto: The American Shore and Beach Preservation Association selected five projects nationwide for its 2026 Best Restored Shore Award, which recognizes outstanding natural infrastructure restoration projects that restore natural resources, enhance habitat, increase shoreline resilience, and provide long-term benefits to coastal communities. They noted that the Queen Bess project exceeded its habitat restoration and bird-nesting goals, with monitoring demonstrating significant benefits to avian communities most impacted by the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. “This award is a testament to what Louisiana can accomplish when we put restoration dollars to work with a clear vision and a commitment to our coastal resources,” said Louisiana Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority Chairman Gordon “Gordy” Dove. “Queen Bess Island is an important part of Louisiana’s coastal ecosystem, and its restoration is helping protect critical habitat for generations of birds while strengthening the resilience of our coast. We are proud to see this Louisiana project recognized on the national stage.” Located near Grand Isle in Jefferson Parish, Queen Bess Island is an important nesting site for brown pelicans and other colonial waterbirds. Years of erosion and subsidence had significantly reduced the island’s available nesting habitat in active use by a brown pelican colony. The Queen Bess Island Restoration Project increased the abundance and quality of nesting habitat on the island by placing material to expand nesting habitat and elevate the island. The project also improved the existing protective rock ring, added breakwaters and bird ramp features, and initiated vegetative plantings, all designed to improve the island’s long-term stability and ecological function. The project was funded through the Louisiana Trustee Implementation Group’s Deepwater Horizon Natural Resource Damage Assessment funds and implemented through a partnership among the Louisiana Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority, the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, federal trustees, and other partners.

artigo.texto: No discurso da vitória, o presidente reeleito Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que se encaminha ao quarto mandato após grande virada impulsionada pela população nas ruas e nas redes sociais, defendeu a soberania digital brasileira. Em sua fala, o presidente acenou para medidas como a atração de data centers e o desenvolvimento de uma inteligência artificial (IA) nacional. Ainda que a necessidade de diminuir a dependência do país de plataformas e infraestruturas estrangeiras para dados em larga escala tenha ficado clara, é importante evitar o erro de atrair grandes projetos de data centers sem que os impactos ambientais sejam mapeados e as contrapartidas para a conservação e a mitigação desses impactos sejam garantidas. No plano de governo, a chapa vencedora prevê que a expansão de data centers e infraestruturas de IA seja acompanhada de salvaguardas socioambientais obrigatórias e exigências de eficiência energética. Inclusive a utilização progressiva de fontes 100% renováveis e a avaliação de impactos sobre o sistema elétrico, hídrico e populações locais. No entanto, parece que esse será um dos principais desafios socioambientais no novo governo. Enquanto a soberania digital entra em pauta, um projeto de data center hiperescalável no interior paulista, do tipo ideal para lidar com volumes massivos de dados, não espera que a ideia seja regulamentada para sair do papel. 5º maior datacenter do Brasil em construção A cidade de Pindamonhangaba, no Vale do Paraíba, em São Paulo, sediará o RiverHook Village 18, um campus de data center hiperescalável projetado para figurar entre os maiores empreendimentos de infraestrutura digital da América do Sul. O projeto, com investimento de R$ 5 bilhões, prevê a ocupação de um terreno de mais de 500 mil metros quadrados às margens da Via Estrutural e promete ser o 5º maior do Brasil. O equipamento terá capacidade instalada inicial de 150 megawatts (MW), com possibilidade de expansão para até 300 MW. A notícia da construção chegou à população pelas redes sociais do prefeito, Ricardo Piorino (PL) e do portal da prefeitura, em 28 de abril de 2026. As obras estavam previstas para iniciar em outubro. Tudo certo. Menos o impacto ambiental e as contrapartidas previstas para esse tipo de projeto, cujos estudos ainda não estão disponíveis. A falta de transparência levou moradores do Vale do Paraíba Paulista a acionar o Ministério Público de São Paulo, questionando a instalação e apresentando uma petição para a paralisação do projeto. O pedido aponta que, até o momento, não foi divulgada nenhuma informação oficial sobre o processo de licenciamento deste empreendimento, nem foi realizada qualquer metodologia de consulta à população. A principal preocupação é a pressão que o equipamento geraria na demanda por energia da região. O Village 18 terá resfriamento sem consumo de água, com o objetivo de que ele não seja uma ameaça tão direta aos recursos hídricos. O sistema adotado opera como o resfriamento do motor de um carro: um líquido refrigerante circula em tubos selados, absorvendo calor diretamente dos processadores e dissipando-o por meio de um trocador de calor externo, sem jamais entrar em contato com o ar livre e sem evaporação. A solução elimina as torres de resfriamento evaporativas tradicionais, que consomem milhões de litros de água por ano em grandes instalações. Isso faz com que haja economia de água, mas pode aumentar o consumo de energia. A conta fica no território O funcionamento do data center a plena carga pode consumir, sozinho, o mesmo que toda a indústria de Pindamonhangaba. Considerando a potência inicial do projeto de 150 MW, o data center consumiria em torno de 1,3 milhão de MWh durante o ano, o mesmo que todas as unidades industriais do município consumiram em 2024, segundo dados da Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Logística do Estado de São Paulo. O consumo ainda representa quase 9 vezes mais do que o consumo residencial anual total da cidade. Na fase de expansão, com capacidade aumentada para 300 MW, a demanda por energia pode superar o consumo atual das casas em até 17 vezes. Além disso, o circuito fechado economiza, mas não zera o uso de água. Não só o líquido refrigerante precisa ser abastecido e trocado de tempos em tempos, como a água também é usada para a geração de energia por hidrelétricas, para a fabricação dos chips que compõem o equipamento, assim como para a manutenção e limpeza. Ou seja, mesmo que o resfriamento não precise de água, a pressão sobre o recurso ainda vai aumentar. Somadas, a alta demanda por energia e água pode comprometer o abastecimento e aumentar as contas da população. O Instituto de Defesa de Consumidores (Idec) aponta que, sem regras, o custo de aumentar o consumo elétrico vai para as tarifas de todo mundo. Por exemplo, o instituto cita os Estados Unidos, onde os data centers causaram recordes de demanda energética e fizeram com que a conta de luz de residências e pequenos negócios ficasse mais cara. Quem atende o aumento da demanda energética A eletricidade que vai abastecer o data center vem do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), ou seja, não precisa ser produzida em Pindamonhangaba. Mas a demanda cresce, e alguém precisa suprí-la. Até porque, o Village 18 não é o primeiro, nem o único equipamento do tipo chegando no país. Isso significa que quando as hidrelétricas não derem conta desse boom de data centers, em algum lugar, mais uma termelétrica vai ser construída. O próprio projeto paulista prevê, numa segunda fase, a possibilidade de gerar energia no próprio local. Na prática, isso significaria pequenas termelétricas dentro do terreno. A proposta toca em uma disputa familiar da região. Por cerca de três anos, moradores e organizações do Vale se mobilizaram contra a instalação de uma mega usina termelétrica em Caçapava. artigo.texto: At about 6 a.m. on Sept. 18, 2026, workers at the Moss Landing Power Plant in California spotted a flare-up along the north wall of the Moss 300 battery building. The building had burned in January 2025, and the new flare-up came more than 20 months later. Vistra, the plant’s owner, said it believes about 1,200 of the roughly 2,500 battery modules still inside the structure ignited. Those modules had not been de-energized because they sat in a section of the building that was unsafe to enter after structural damage from the first fire. Monterey County issued a shelter-in-place order, and the natural gas plant on the site was temporarily shut down. By late afternoon, county officials reported the fire was inactive. The episode arrived as the industry can point to a very different set of numbers. The Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) reports that the battery energy storage system (BESS) failure rate, measured against cumulative deployed capacity, fell 99% between 2018 and 2025. Both facts are true at once, and together they define the challenge for utilities that are leaning harder on storage every year. The technology is getting safer, but reliability is being decided by specific engineering choices: how old a design is, how hard it is operated, what protects the cells from one another, and how well the equipment that ties the system to the grid is built to last. Storage Becomes a Grid Fixture The scale of the buildout explains why those details matter. According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), utility-scale battery storage capacity in the U.S. grew at an average annual rate of 70% over the last three years, reaching 43.6 GW at the end of 2025. Operators added another 8.3 GW in the first half of 2026, bringing nameplate capacity to nearly 52 GW. Furthermore, they have reported plans to add 54 GW more over the next two and a half years: 14 GW in the second half of this year, 26 GW in 2027, and 14 GW in 2028. On those figures, the fleet would roughly double. Much of that capacity is paired with solar (Figure 1). The EIA notes that solar photovoltaic plants host the largest battery storage units. The Bellefield Solar and Energy Storage Farm, which serves the California Independent System Operator (CAISO) and began operating in December 2025, couples 500 MW of solar with 500 MW of storage, and plans call for doubling both by November 2026. If that happens, the EIA says, Bellefield will become the largest storage facility in the country. In Florida, the Manatee Solar Energy Center pairs 75 MW of solar with 409 MW of batteries, while Nevada’s Gemini Solar Hybrid combines 690 MW of photovoltaics with 380 MW of storage. 1. Battery storage units are regularly being paired with solar plants and sometimes even wind farms. This rendering shows a renewable generation site with solar arrays, wind turbines, and battery storage cabinets. Courtesy: nVent The reliability case is easiest to see in the West. The Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC), in a December 2025 report prepared with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), the North American Electric Reliability Corp. (NERC), and CAISO, noted that roughly 27 GW of BESS capacity was installed in the Western Interconnection when the report was published. Storage, it said, helps meet system demand “particularly during evening hours when solar generation is ramping down and the demand on the system is still high,” and it contributes to ancillary services that support grid stability. Data centers are adding a new dimension. Vince Sprenkle, director of the Grid Storage Launchpad at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), said in a lab feature last year: “We are seeing a dramatic shift in the energy sector due to things like the scaling of data centers. It is changing the dynamic of where we need energy storage.” PNNL said in a January news release that artificial intelligence (AI) data centers can cause sudden spikes and drops in demand, which stored energy can be called on to absorb. What the Failure Data Shows EPRI’s BESS Failure Incident Database, which the institute started in 2021 after a cluster of lithium-ion fires in South Korea and an incident in Surprise, Arizona, tracks failures worldwide. The 99% figure includes 33 non-public incidents that EPRI is aware of. The institute attributes the improvement to lessons from early failures being built into newer designs and best practices. The database has limits that matter to anyone reading it as a reliability measure. EPRI says its focus is on incidents with wider public health and safety impact rather than operational failures, so it is not a measure of everyday availability. It is compiled from media reports and other public documents, and EPRI acknowledges it cannot guarantee that every incident is captured. As of Oct. 11, 2026, the stationary-storage table listed 165 incidents worldwide. EPRI, working with TWAICE and PNNL, has also classified incidents by root cause (design, manufacturing, integration and construction, operation, or a combination) and by the physical location of the failure, including cells and modules, controls, and balance-of-system equipment. The framework is a reminder that cells are only one place a system can fail. Moss Landing: Lessons From a Legacy Design WECC’s report on the January 2025 fire is the clearest public look at how an early large-scale system differs from what is being built today. WECC stressed that the report is not a root cause analysis, and Vistra says the cause of the fire is still unknown. What the report does document is the design and operating context. Phase 1 of Moss Landing, which reached operation at the end of 2020, was housed in a repurposed turbine building, with racks of nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) cells stacked two high across two stories. artigo.texto: SECI, OHPC Plan 3 GW Floating Solar, BESS Projects in Odisha by 2030 Solar Energy Corporation of India and Odisha Hydro Power Corporation have signed a binding term sheet to jointly develop 3 GW of floating solar and battery energy storage projects across Odisha's reservoirs by 2030 through a 50:50 joint venture, with power offtake envisaged through GRIDCO. The term sheet was signed at the BRE Summit and Expo 2026. November 04, 2026. By Mrinmoy Dey Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) and Odisha Hydro Power Corporation (OHPC) have signed a Binding Term Sheet for jointly developing large-scale floating solar photovoltaic (PV) projects integrated with battery energy storage systems (BESS) across various reservoirs in Odisha. The projects will be developed through a 50:50 joint venture (JV), with power offtake envisaged through GRIDCO Ltd. The term sheet was signed by Sivakumar V Vepakomma, Director (Power Systems), SECI, and Amiya Kumar Mohanty, Director (Operations), OHPC, in the presence of Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, Deputy Chief Minister Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Akash Tripathi, Managing Director, SECI, and Vishal Kumar Dev, Additional Chief Secretary, Energy Department, Government of Odisha. With an estimated floating solar potential of around 12 GW, Odisha offers significant opportunities for harnessing reservoir resources for renewable energy development. Under the proposed partnership, SECI and OHPC are targeting approximately 3 GW of renewable energy capacity under the capital expenditure (CAPEX) mode by 2030. The initiative also represents an important milestone towards SECI's target of adding 10 GW of capacity through its own projects by 2030, strengthening its portfolio of owned renewable energy assets. The proposed integration of floating solar PV and battery storage is expected to support the supply of reliable, clean and dispatchable renewable power, particularly during peak demand hours. The collaboration is also aimed at strengthening Odisha's energy security while facilitating greater renewable energy integration into the power system. artigo.texto: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. The artificial intelligence company said in its commitments that for data centers it owns and operates, it will solicit community input, publish construction plans and stay away from use of non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Additionally, in a policy blueprint, OpenAI encouraged policymakers to enact similar commitments as laws. "What we're doing with this blueprint is really laying out the best lessons that we have learned and committing to applying them as they go forward," OpenAI Chief Global Affairs Officer Chris Lehane told reporters during a Wednesday briefing. "This will help ensure that there is a very high floor in terms of how people move forward." On Tuesday, Americans issued a stinging rebuke of data centers at the polls. Out of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states, voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures for all but one, according to an analysis by Ballotpedia and additional results gathered by CNBC on Wednesday. Opposition to AI data centers mounted swiftly over the summer across both sides of the political aisle. Consumers grappling with inflation, rising grocery prices and stubbornly high prices at the pump grew worried that the facilities could exacerbate environmental harms, raise utility bills and contribute to job loss. For many, they became a physical manifestation of the widespread antipathy and anxiety around AI. AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then. "Having these conversations now actually helps put more energy into the momentum, so that when people come back in late January, new Congress is in in session, a lot of the work is being done in advance," Lehane said. artigo.texto: LG Energy Solution Opens ‘Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) 2026’ to Connect Innovative Research Ideas with Industry Needs - The company invites universities and research institutions worldwide to submit innovative battery research proposals from Oct. 29 to Dec. 6 - Thematic and Open-Topic calls for proposals are designed to deepen industry-academia collaboration, while a two-stage review process safeguards researchers’ original ideas - LG Energy Solution’s Battery Innovation Contest has supported approximately 50 research projects since 2017 SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — LG Energy Solution (KRX: 373220) today announced the launch of the Battery Innovation Contest 2026 (BIC 2026), a global open innovation program to discover and support cutting-edge battery technologies with strong commercialization potential. Universities and research institutions in Korea and around the world are invited to submit concept proposals from October 29 through December 6, 2026, via LG Energy Solution’s online open innovation platform, BRIDGE (bridge.lgensol.com). Priority will be given to proposals that address key pain points in the battery industry and have the potential to accelerate technological advancement. Now in its 10th year, the BIC has enabled LG Energy Solution to pursue joint research with universities and research institutions worldwide. Through the program, the company seeks to help transform creative research ideas into commercially viable technologies while contributing to a stronger battery innovation ecosystem. - Deepening Two-Way Collaboration through Thematic and Open-Topic Calls for Proposals BIC 2026 will continue to offer two calls for proposals designed to combine industry-driven research needs with the creativity and autonomy of researchers. Under the Thematic call for proposals, LG Energy Solution presents specific research topics identified by its product development departments. This year, the company has significantly expanded the number of thematic topics, ranging from materials and cells to battery management systems (BMS) and AI. Researchers will be invited to propose solutions addressing these topics, creating a more structured framework for two-way collaboration. The Open-Topic call for proposals will allow researchers to propose original ideas across broad areas of battery technology. This call preserves the researcher-led format, giving participants the flexibility to develop creative concepts with commercial potential. - Protecting Original Ideas through a Two-Stage Proposal Process and the BRIDGE Platform To better protect researchers’ original ideas, LG Energy Solution will operate a two-stage application and evaluation process, in which applicants will submit a concise concept proposal during the first stage and a full proposal for further evaluation only after being shortlisted. Limiting the detail required in the initial review will help protect ideas that are not ultimately selected. All proposals and subsequent research projects will be managed through BRIDGE, LG Energy Solution’s integrated, interactive platform for open innovation. BRIDGE streamlines industry-academia communication and project record management while protecting collaborative research technologies and minimizing offline administrative work. - A Decade of Impact: From Patent Filing to Publication in Science Since 2017, approximately 50 research projects have been supported through the BIC. Topics with proven feasibility have been expanded into projects at the Frontier Research Laboratory (FRL), LG Energy Solution’s joint research center with leading universities and research institutions in Korea and abroad, which provides additional research funding as well as in-depth support from the company’s researchers. The BIC has also delivered tangible results. For example, a patent application is underway for a physics-based model developed through a BIC project last year to improve BMS computation speed. In 2019, the FRL’s research on a long-life all-solid-state battery operating at room temperature was published in the prestigious journal Science. Je-Young Kim, CTO of LG Energy Solution, said : By joining forces, industry and academia can drive innovation across the battery industry “Building on our differentiated technological competitiveness, LG Energy Solution will continue to accelerate its growth in the battery market.” READ the latest Batteries News shaping the battery market LG Energy Solution Opens ‘Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) 2026’ to Connect Innovative Research Ideas with Industry Needs, source
